author: shreejitverma
body:
## Intent Add an IndexNow key file (public/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt containing its own filename-key, per the IndexNow protocol) so Bing and Yandex can verify ownership and index the site's new pages (/, /resume, /books, /value-investing) immediately when pinged. This is part of the user's explicit goal of ranking at the top of recruiter searches globally - Bing powers the LinkedIn search ecosystem recruiters use. Single static text file, no code changes. After checks-passed I will merge per the user's standing merge instruction, then ping api.indexnow.org with the site URLs. ## What Changed - Added `public/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt`, a static IndexNow key file whose body is exactly the key (no trailing newline), letting Bing and Yandex verify site ownership when the site is pinged via api.indexnow.org. Note from review: since the apex domain 301-redirects to www.shreejitverma.com, IndexNow pings should submit URLs on the www host so key verification is not subject to the redirect. - Added a Playwright test in `e2e/assets.spec.ts` asserting the key file is served with HTTP 200 and the key as its exact body; the full assets suite passed 10/10 on desktop and mobile in the pipeline run. - Updated the `assets.spec.ts` row in `e2e/README.md` to document the new IndexNow key file coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Single static text file that correctly implements the IndexNow key-file protocol (content matches filename, served at site root), with no code paths, security exposure, or behavior changes involved. ## Testing Built and served the production site, fetched the IndexNow key URL as bingbot (HTTP 200 with the key as the exact body, satisfying the ownership-verification protocol), confirmed the four pages to be pinged all return 200, and added plus ran a permanent Playwright e2e test for the key file — all tests pass; no visual artifact because the end-user surface is a plain-text HTTP response, captured verbatim in the transcript. A pre-existing OneDrive symlink at public/library crashes next start in this sandbox and was temporarily swapped for an empty directory during the run, then restored.
Evidence: Crawler-view HTTP transcript of IndexNow key file and ping-target pages $ curl -si -A "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; bingbot/2.0)" http://localhost:3000/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Content-Length: 32 a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38 # IndexNow ownership check: body must equal the key (= filename stem) body = 'a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38' expected = 'a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38' MATCH: search engines can verify ownership of the key per the IndexNow protocol # Pages that will be submitted in the IndexNow ping (status on local prod server): / 200 /resume 200 /books 200 /value-investing 200 ```text $ curl -si -A "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; bingbot/2.0)" http://localhost:3000/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt HTTP/1.1 200 OK Accept-Ranges: bytes Cache-Control: public, max-age=0 Last-Modified: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 20:41:01 GMT ETag: W/"20-19f8b8f7309" Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Content-Length: 32 Vary: Accept-Encoding Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 20:46:47 GMT Connection: keep-alive Keep-Alive: timeout=5 a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38 # IndexNow ownership check: body must equal the key (= filename stem) body = 'a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38' expected = 'a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38' MATCH: search engines can verify ownership of the key per the IndexNow protocol # Pages that will be submitted in the IndexNow ping (status on local prod server): / 200 /resume 200 /books 200 /value-investing 200 ```
- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 info across 1 run (5m52s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `public/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt:1` - vercel.json 301-redirects apex shreejitverma.com to www.shreejitverma.com; when pinging api.indexnow.org, submit URLs on the www host so key verification is not subject to the redirect.
⚠️ **Test** - 1 info - ℹ️ `public/library` - Pre-existing environment hazard, not caused by this change: public/library is a git-tracked symlink to a OneDrive CloudStorage folder. When those files are dataless placeholders (as in this sandbox), Next.js crashes with 'Unknown system error -11, scandir' while scanning public/ on the first static-file request, killing `next start`. Worked around during testing by temporarily replacing the symlink with an empty directory and restoring it from git afterward. Local e2e runs on machines without materialized OneDrive files will hit the same crash. - `git diff ed1156b..8258284` — confirmed the change is a single static key file - `xxd public/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt` — 32 bytes, body equals filename key, no trailing newline or BOM - `npm run build && npm run start`, then `curl -si -A "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; bingbot/2.0)" http://localhost:3000/a31d850309d40502597fcc0663404e38.txt` — HTTP 200, text/plain, body exactly equals the key - `curl status checks for /, /resume, /books, /value-investing on the local production server — all 200` - `npx playwright test e2e/assets.spec.ts` — 10/10 passed, including the new 'IndexNow key file is served with the key as its exact body' test on desktop and mobile
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.
## Summary by Sourcery Add an IndexNow verification key file and cover it with end-to-end tests and documentation updates. New Features: - Serve an IndexNow ownership-verification key file at the site root for Bing and Yandex indexing. Documentation: - Update e2e testing documentation to describe coverage of the IndexNow key file in the assets test suite. Tests: - Extend Playwright asset tests to assert the IndexNow key file is returned with HTTP 200 and a body exactly matching the key.

## Summary

- Extract the transport-independent server runtime and add an encoded in-memory adapter for deterministic integration scenarios.
- Replace brittle or redundant tests with high-value behavior slices covering combat in both directions, chat, whispers, emotes, portals, lifecycle, leveling, forgiving death, and faction rules.
- Consolidate rendering coverage to one seeded playfield golden and document the intentional snapshot-regeneration workflow.
- Remove the legacy PRD and make the accepted ADRs and domain documentation the current source of truth.

## Test-suite impact

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test cases | 1,679 | 1,147 | -532 (-31.7%) |
| Assertions | 29,488 | 25,935 | -3,553 (-12.0%) |
| TypeScript test LOC | 25,479 | 18,639 | -6,840 (-26.8%) |
| Changed source lines | — | — | +6,472 / -13,737 (net -7,265) |

The smaller suite retains broad deterministic coverage while removing assertions tied to implementation detail or volatile presentation choices.

## Notable behavior slices

- Player strike: local prediction produces SFX/VFX, the server validates the strike, and authoritative results reach clients in the zone.
- Monster strike: the player loses HP, receives an invulnerability window, and renders sound and blood particles exactly once.
- Chat and whispers: the real client command path reaches the server and produces the appropriate logs and server-confirmed bubbles.
- Emotes: the real chat command path reaches `GameLoop.emote` and broadcasts authoritative state.
- Portals, lifecycle, leveling, forgiving death, and faction targeting receive focused scenario or deterministic unit coverage.

## Review follow-up

This includes all fixes from the final code-review pass:

- combat scenarios now enter a field through a real portal instead of using invalid Town fixtures;
- lifecycle coverage is correctly classified as integration coverage;
- shared scenario helpers are consolidated;
- runtime entity lookup moved behind `World.avatarOf`;
- chat, whisper, and emote assertions exercise the complete intended paths;
- incoming-hit particles are proven to render exactly once.

- 25,935 assertions

- dependency-cruiser: no violations

body:
## What this PR does

Sets up the full Supabase authentication flow for the SubSight app.

### Changes
- **Supabase client** — `src/lib/supabase.ts` reads from `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` env vars; shows "not configured" state gracefully when missing
- **Auth context** — `src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx` provides `user`, `session`, `signIn`, `signUp`, `signOut`, `signInWithGoogle`, `signInWithGitHub`, `resetPasswordForEmail`, `loading`, `configured`
- **Protected routes** — `src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx` redirects unauthenticated users to `/login`
- **Login page** — Email/password form, Google + GitHub OAuth buttons, "Forgot password?" flow, error handling for invalid credentials
- **Signup page** — Name, email, password, confirm password fields, OAuth buttons, email verification notice after signup
- **Updated nav** — Shows user avatar/name + sign out when logged in, "Sign In" link when logged out (desktop and mobile)
- **`/dashboard`** — Wrapped with `ProtectedRoute`

### How to test
1. Set `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in your environment
2. Visit `/login` — see email/password form with OAuth buttons
3. Visit `/signup` — see registration form
4. Visit `/dashboard` without auth — redirected to `/login`
5. Without env vars set — graceful "not configured" message shown

### Dependencies added
- `@supabase/supabase-js`

body:
## 개요

자는 동안 마이크로 소리를 감지해 **코골이**와 **잠꼬대**를 자동으로 기록하는 자체 완결형 웹앱(`sleep-tracker.html`)을 추가했습니다. 포트폴리오의 **Vibe Coding** 섹션에서 실행할 수 있도록 카드도 연결했습니다.

## 주요 기능

- **실시간 마이크 모니터링** — Web Audio `AnalyserNode`로 RMS 기반 음량(dB) 측정, 실시간 파형·레벨 미터 표시
- **이벤트 자동 감지** — 설정한 임계 음량을 넘고 최소 지속 시간을 충족한 소음을 이벤트로 기록 (뒤척임·순간 소음 필터링)
- **코골이 vs 잠꼬대 분류** — 스펙트럴 센트로이드(주파수 중심) 휴리스틱으로 저주파의 코골이(< ~520Hz)와 말소리 대역의 잠꼬대를 구분
- **오디오 클립 녹음 & 재생** — 이벤트마다 `MediaRecorder`로 짧은 클립을 남겨 아침에 다시 듣기 가능 (옵션)
- **밤새 타임라인** — 캔버스에 시각 눈금과 함께 이벤트 분포·음량을 시각화
- **요약 통계** — 전체/코골이/잠꼬대 횟수, 최대 음량, 소음 지속 시간
- **세션 히스토리** — `localStorage`에 지난 기록 저장·삭제

## 프라이버시

모든 녹음과 분석은 서버 전송 없이 사용자 기기의 브라우저 안에서만 처리됩니다.

## 변경 파일

- `sleep-tracker.html` — 신규 앱 (단일 파일, 기존 사이트 글래스모피즘 다크 테마 적용, 테마 토글·화면 꺼짐 방지 포함)
- `index.html` — Vibe Coding 섹션에 Sleep Tracker 카드 추가

## 검증

헤드리스 Chromium에서 페이지 로드(JS 오류 없음), 설정 슬라이더 바인딩, 이벤트 주입 → 통계/타임라인/이벤트 로그/히스토리 저장 파이프라인이 모두 정상 동작함을 확인했습니다.

body:
## Was

**S1** aus dem SV-Claim-Detail-Audit (Session b0e963b6). Aaron-Steuerung: *„die Tools haben teils ihre Daseinsberechtigung — schau ob sie richtig platziert sind."* Also eine **Platzierungs-Analyse** der vier Flows der nie gerenderten `SvToolsCard` (AAR-757) statt blindem Löschen oder Zurück-Verdrahten.

## Platzierungs-Analyse der 4 SvToolsCard-Flows

| Flow | Bereits korrekt platziert? | Aktion |
|---|---|---|
| Gutachten-Upload | ✅ `GutachtenCard` (slot-basiert, versioniert; `uploadGutachten` ist Legacy laut `qc.ts`) | Duplikat entfernt |
| Freier Datei-Upload | ✅ `WeitereDokumenteCard` + `FallWindowDropzone` (globaler Drop) | Duplikat entfernt |
| ZB1-Foto-OCR | ✅ `VorOrtClient` (`/api/sv/upload-with-ocr`, Vorder+Rückseite, `capture=environment`) | Duplikat entfernt |
| **FIN/VIN-Eingabe** | ❌ **nirgends** — nur in der toten SvToolsCard; `StammdatenAccordion` zeigt FIN nur read-only | **als schlanke `FinNachtragenCard` neu platziert** |

## Änderungen

- **NEU `FinNachtragenCard`** (`SectionCard`-basiert): erscheint **nur** wenn `fall.fin_vin` fehlt, im SV-Fall-Detail in der Aktions-Spalte neben den Stammdaten. Ruft das bestehende `saveFinVinGutachter` → Vorschaden-Prüfung. Eine Karte = eine Funktion (CMM-23-Geist).
- **`SvToolsCard.tsx` gelöscht** (−345): 3 redundante Flows, FIN in die neue Card ausgelagert.
- **`StammdatenCard.tsx` gelöscht** (−75): war nur unter `{false && …}` (CMM-32, durch `StammdatenAccordion` ersetzt), einziger Consumer.
- **`SvEinzuholenBanner.tsx` gelöscht** (−52): 2 tote Imports (page + client), 0 gerendert, 0 andere Consumer.
- **`FallakteDrawer` bleibt** — liefert den `TeamMitglied`-Typ + `Parameters<typeof …>` an `AnsprechpartnerCard` + `FallHeader` (Typ ist tragend, **nicht** tot).
- **CMM-23-Kommentar aktualisiert** (der „keine SvTools"-Passus): für den einen justified Flow (FIN, nur wenn fehlend) bewusst partiell revidiert.

## knip-Baseline (+1, dokumentiert)

`cardentity-actions.ts` (AAR-311, `requestCardentityTypBForFallSv` = manueller Cardentity-Typ-B-Trigger, den der SV nach Vor-Ort-Vorschadenhinweisen auslöst) wurde durch die `StammdatenCard`-Löschung **transitiv verwaist** (StammdatenCard war der einzige Consumer). **NICHT gelöscht** — echtes SV-Tool, zurückgehalten bis zum **Cardentity-Revival** (Marker: „Cardentity TOT / Aaron holt neue Credentials"). Re-Wire in die SV-Fallakte = **Post-Revival-Follow-up** (jetzt wäre es ein Button auf eine tote API). Daher in die knip-Baseline aufgenommen (`+cardentity-actions.ts`; incidentally `−anrede.ts` = pre-existing staging-Drift, hat inzwischen einen Consumer).

## Checks (lokal grün)

- `tsc --noEmit` EXIT 0 · `npm run build` grün
- `check:knip --ratchet` grün (56 known, 0 neu)
- `check:component-set` — kein neuer Drift (`FinNachtragenCard` nutzt `SectionCard`)
- `check:token-audit` grün (claimondo-Tokens)

## Regel 4 — Prod-Smoke (an Merge-/Deploy-Session übergeben)

Nach Deploy auf Prod (`https://app.claimondo.de`), SV-Rolle:

- **Wegwerf-SV** bauen (der Marker `reference-internal-test-account-logins` warnt: `test-sv` trägt CI-TOTP → für SV-Smokes eigene Fixture) + einen SV-Fall öffnen.
- **Fall MIT FIN** (`fin_vin` gesetzt): `FinNachtragenCard` erscheint **nicht**, FIN steht read-only im StammdatenAccordion.
- **Fall OHNE FIN** (`fin_vin` NULL): `FinNachtragenCard` erscheint in der rechten Spalte → 17-stellige FIN eintragen → „Speichern" → Toast „FIN gespeichert. Vorschaden-Prüfung gestartet." → Card verschwindet, FIN steht read-only.
- **Regression**: Gutachten-Upload (GutachtenCard), Datei-Upload (WeitereDokumenteCard/Drop), Vor-Ort-Fahrzeugschein-OCR (VorOrtClient) weiterhin erreichbar; SV-Fall-Detail rendert (kein 500, keine leere Shell).
- Test-Konto `telefon = NULL` → keine echten Comms.

author: fishloa
body:
`verify_digest` rejected the absolute-URL `uri` form its own multimux client sends. RFC-correct fix:
- `HA2` now hashes the client's claimed `uri` (RFC 7616 §3.4.1 digest-uri-value), not the caller's request path.
- `digest_uri_matches` accepts origin-form OR absolute-form (exact path compare — no prefix/suffix rubber-stamp); wrong path/password still rejected.
- Unblocks + lands the **multimux testutil dedup** (wraps `broadcast_auth::Verifier` instead of hand-rolling Digest) — the 3 previously-failing ts_http/hls_pull digest tests now pass.

Mutation-verified (neuter matcher → wrong-uri tests fail). 45 broadcast-auth + 290 multimux tests green; verified by me. broadcast-auth 0.1.1 (patch; dependents ^0.1 unaffected). Closes #724.

author: johnrcarty
body:
## Summary

Secured debts (mortgage, auto) now account for their underlying asset. Design per discussion: the asset is a **separate asset account** with an optional link from the liability — chosen over an asset-value field on the liability because net worth and trend math partition purely on `isLiability`, so a property account flows into assets/net-worth/trend-lines with zero changes to the summing code, gets manual-snapshot trend history for free, and supports paid-off assets plus multiple loans on one asset.

### What's new

- **Account kinds `property` and `vehicle`** — assets automatically (absent from `LIABILITY_KINDS`). Deliberately excluded from the SimpleFin mapping form.
- **`accounts.securedAssetAccountId`** — first account→account FK, on the liability side, non-unique by design (mortgage + HELOC → one house), `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Kind flips clear stale links in both directions.
- **Debt detail page**: new "Secured By" card (link via asset select / unlink), and an equity line — asset value minus **all** liens on that asset — in the Current Balance card next to "paid off so far".
- **Accounts list**: linked assets show an equity subtitle, e.g. `$47.5K equity · Mortgage - 1004 Bevan` (destructive color when negative).
- **Manual valuation with history**: Add Account collects current value + optional **purchase price/date** for physical assets. Purchase price reuses the existing `originalBalanceCents` fixed-reference column (no schema addition); a past purchase date seeds a snapshot so the trend line starts at the purchase point and shows appreciation since. The edit dialog gains an "Update value" form (mirrors `DebtBalanceForm`) writing dated `account_balance_snapshot` rows with newest-wins cache updates, an "up/down $X since purchase" readout, and a purchase-price backfill for assets created before this feature.

### Migration

`0012_outgoing_mongu.sql`: two `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`s + the FK column. Applied to dev; runs automatically on container start at deploy.

## Verification

Throwaway tsx script against the dev DB (property $50K/purchased $45K + $30K loan + $5K HELOC both linked, snapshots today/60 days ago, all cleaned up after — cascade confirmed):

- Property flows into assets; snapshot carry-forward exact ($48K at prior month-end, $50K today)
- Net worth moved by exactly +$15K (asset minus both liens) vs pre-insert baseline
- `getDebtDetail` resolves the secured asset and computes equity = $15K (both liens subtracted, not just the queried one)
- Snapshot upsert dedupes on (account, date, manual)
- Asset→liability kind flip severs inbound links

`tsc --noEmit`, ESLint (React Compiler rules), and `next build` all clean.

author: nolicommoveri
body:
Pro previously unlocked the full app for anyone who opened its origin — there
was no license check anywhere, only the Lite→Pro export/redirect handoff. This
adds the missing gate so Pro can actually be sold.

- shared/data/license.js: activate()/validate() against Lemon Squeezy's
  browser-callable License API (key in the body, no store secret), plus a
  verdict state machine with an interval-scaled offline grace window (yearly
  ~30d, monthly ~7d, unknown → shorter). Interval inferred from the returned
  variant_name via a configurable pattern.
- shared/assets/licenseGate.js: the UI — full-screen activation wall (first
  run), renewal wall (lapsed past grace), and a dismissible grace banner.
  Invoked from app.js boot() before the app renders.
- Cached activation stored under its own settings.js key, deliberately excluded
  from clearAllSettings() so Reset App keeps paid entitlement.
- Gated on editionFlags.licenseGate, true ONLY in pro/editionConfig.js (with a
  licenseConfig carrying the checkout URL + variant pattern); Lite/Demo export a
  null config so the import resolves but the gate stays inert.
- sw.js: precache the two new modules (no CACHE_NAME bump yet — pending).
- Docs: README Step 7, pro/README, End-State guide note, plan §Licensing status.

Browser-verified (headless Chromium): Pro walls every page unlicensed; Lite and
Demo render with no wall; all four verdict paths (valid / renewal wall / grace
banner / stale-offline) behave correctly. No console errors.

## Approval 

[Adobe community contribution approval](https://git.corp.adobe.com/OpenSourceAdvisoryBoard/opensource_submission_process/issues/1944)


## Changes

**`relsim/relsim_score.py`**
- `embed(images, max_image_size=None, micro_batch_size=None)` now accepts a PIL image **or** a list; returns `[N, 384]` (single image still returns `[1, 384]`). New `_embed_batch` helper runs one batched forward (build per-image `<|query|>` message → one `processor(...)` call → one forward → `F.normalize`).
  - `max_image_size`: optional per-image resolution cap (LANCZOS) to avoid OOM.
  - `micro_batch_size`: optional internal chunking so very large lists don't OOM in one forward (concatenated in order).
- `__call__(img1, img2)` now embeds both images in **one** batched forward (same scalar result, faster).
- `preprocess_image` is now list-aware (list in → list out).
- Updated docstrings + loader usage example.

**`README.md`**
- Added a CLIP-style batch usage example; noted RelSim is image-only (no `get_text_features` analog).

**`tests/` (new)**
- `tests/test_embed_batch.py` — 20 tests covering backward compatibility, batching, ordering, normalization, `__call__`, and micro-batching.
- `tests/images/` — three sample JPEGs used by the real-image and parity tests.

## Backward compatibility
- `embed(img)` still returns `[1, 384]`; `__call__` returns the same scalar similarity. Existing callers are unaffected.
- Device-agnostic: runs on CPU or CUDA (inputs move to the model's device via `device_map="auto"`).

## Behavior notes
- **OOM:** by default one forward, so OOM behaves exactly like CLIP/DINO (raised, not swallowed). `micro_batch_size` / `max_image_size` are opt-in mitigations.
- **Order:** output rows are guaranteed to match input order (verified by tests, including a duplicate-transposition guard).

## Testing
- Mocked CPU tests (no checkpoint/GPU) — all pass locally.

author: chemaclass
body:
Closes #2, closes #6.

## #2 — chart.js off first paint
- The five report charts are now `lazy()` + `Suspense` in `App.tsx` (they only ever render after a report loads, never on the landing page), so **chart.js leaves the first-paint download** and arrives with the report.
- Fixed a chunking trap: pinning `react-chartjs-2` into `vendor-charts` dragged **React** into that chunk, which made `index` import React from it and forced it eager. Now only `chart.js` (React-free) is pinned; the tiny wrapper rides the lazy `Charts` chunk.
- Verified on the build: `index` has **no static import** of `vendor-charts`; react-dom is a **single copy** in `index`, and the lazy chunks import React from it.

## #6 — memoization
- Chart components wrapped in `React.memo` with their datasets in `useMemo`, so unrelated App re-renders (opening a menu, switching mode) don't rebuild chart data. Their props are stable `report` field reads, so memo actually skips.
- `Heatmap`: the 365-cell grid is memoized (`useMemo`, hover-independent) and `showTip` is a stable `useCallback`. `onMouseMove` updates only the tooltip now, instead of rebuilding every cell element on each mouse event.

## Verified
typecheck clean · 26/26 tests · build warning-clean · knip clean · madge no cycles.

Closes #2
Closes #6

author: wilsonneto-swe
body:
### 📚 Description

Abrir o PR vinha sendo tratado como o fim da tarefa. Comentário de review ficava sem resposta, e thread era resolvida em silêncio, quando era. Num repositório público as threads são o registro de auditoria da decisão: resolver sem explicar apaga o porquê de algo ter sido, ou não ter sido, mudado.

Este PR adiciona a skill **`pr-watch`** e a torna obrigatória ao abrir um PR, documentada no README.

**O que a skill faz**

Conduz o PR até o fim: consulta as threads de review e os checks de CI, verifica cada alegação antes de agir, responde com evidência, resolve e reporta. A condição de saída é explícita: zero threads abertas **e** todos os checks passando.

Regras que ela fixa:

- **todo comentário postado no PR começa com `(Claude Code)`**, para quem lê a thread saber que quem respondeu foi um agente, e não ler uma afirmação técnica com o peso de uma revisão humana;
- comentar na thread **antes** de resolver, e depois **citar o commit** que endereçou o ponto;
- comentário de bot pode ser fechado na hora; comentário de humano só depois de a pessoa concordar;
- comentário que questiona o **desenho** da mudança, e não a implementação, volta para quem abriu o PR decidir, em vez de o agente decidir sozinho.

**Por que "verificar antes de agir" está lá**

Não é formalidade. Num PR recente o bot de review afirmou que `path.resolve(__dirname, '../..')` a partir de `tests/e2e` resolvia para `tests/` e quebrava um teste. Erra por um nível: resolve para a raiz do repositório. Aceitar a alegação teria produzido uma "correção" em cima de código correto.

**Proteção da branch**

A skill também registra que a `main` roda com `dismiss_stale_reviews` e `require_last_push_approval`. Ou seja, **qualquer push num PR já aprovado derruba a aprovação** e exige review novo. Daí a regra de que trabalho não relacionado vai para PR separado.

Foi exatamente por isso que este PR existe em vez de entrar no #867: aquele já está aprovado e mergeable, e empurrar isto lá custaria a aprovação do revisor.

**Ordem de merge**

O README também linka a skill `validacao-visual`, que vem no #867. **Faz sentido mergear o #867 primeiro**, senão o link fica quebrado até lá.

body:
Fixes #1824 

This also passes the third-party (OpenMP, BLAS, etc) limiting env variables to `multiprocessing` worker processes, as a side-effect of the implementation. That part is not tested, but could be.

## A demonstration of the performance effects of this PR

**Update:** See below for an improved script that gives more meaningful results.

Consider the following script:

```python
import os

import numpy as np
from joblib import Parallel, delayed, parallel_config


def work():
    arr = np.ones((1_000_000,))
    for _ in range(1_000):
        arr.sum()
    return arr.sum()


def start_thread_pool():
    with parallel_config(backend="threading"):
        return Parallel(n_jobs=-1)([delayed(work)() for _ in range(10)])


with parallel_config(backend="threading", n_jobs=os.cpu_count() // 2):
    expected = work()
    for _ in Parallel()(
        [delayed(start_thread_pool)() for _ in range(os.cpu_count() // 2)]
    ):
        pass
```

## Summary

- add a server-side OpenAI Responses API gateway for Content Studio drafts
- require and verify a valid Supabase session before any paid model request
- default to the cost-sensitive gpt-5.6-luna model with low reasoning
- constrain input lengths, task type, output tokens, and strict JSON-schema output
- add per-user warm-instance throttling and generic provider errors
- expose only the current Supabase access token from the cloud adapter
- preserve a clearly labelled demo generator whenever accounts or AI are unavailable
- keep every generated asset in Draft status with human review required
- add configuration/security documentation and regression coverage

## Security and cost boundaries

- OPENAI_API_KEY exists only in Vercel server environment variables
- the browser receives no OpenAI credential
- unauthenticated requests are rejected before reaching OpenAI
- sessions are verified directly against Supabase
- only content_draft is accepted
- input fields are truncated and output follows a strict schema
- six requests per authenticated user per minute are allowed per warm function instance
- raw provider errors are not returned to users
- OpenAI project budgets and alerts are still recommended before activation

## Validation

- frontend, cloud adapter, API function, and test source parse successfully
- no client-side OpenAI secret pattern exists
- Supabase bearer verification and rate guard verified
- Responses API, strict schema, output limit, model default, and review requirement verified
- demo fallback and startup selector safeguards pass
- conflict-marker scan passes

## Test focus before configuration

1. Open Content Studio.
2. Confirm the Agent brief says Demo generation.
3. Generate several drafts and confirm Wave continues working.
4. Confirm each item remains Draft.
5. Open Settings → Reliability and confirm an AI fallback diagnostic was recorded.

Sign in, generate a draft, confirm the UI reports the AI draft is held for review, inspect Audit Trail for OpenAI/model evidence, sign out, and confirm generation returns safely to demo mode.

author: tnsr-q
body:
## What

`rgp_path_register_resolves_embedded_assets_only` used a fixed temp directory (`$TMPDIR/ratty_rgp_path_register_test`), so two overlapping `cargo test` processes — a background run plus a foreground one, or two worktrees sharing `$TMPDIR` — raced: one process's `remove_dir_all` cleanup landed between the other's `create_dir_all` and `fs::write`, failing the write with ENOENT. Observed as an intermittent panic at the `.expect("write disk asset")` during the #32 work; passes alone and on re-run, which is the classic shared-tempdir signature.

The directory is now named with `std::process::id()` plus a per-run atomic counter, so concurrent runs cannot collide. Cleanup is unchanged, and every assertion — the absolute-path refusal, the traversal refusal, the embedded-name success, and the trusted-loader precondition — is untouched.

Verified: the shared-path pattern reproduces ENOENT repeatedly under 24k concurrent iterations; the unique-path pattern produces zero. A sweep found no other test in the repo using a fixed shared temp path.

## Merge safety

Both this branch and #32 modified `src/inline.rs`. Per the #29/#30 lesson (clean mergeability ≠ green build), the merge against post-#32 `main` was performed locally: auto-merge clean, `cargo test --lib` 114 passed on the combined tree.

💡 What: Replaced `re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()` with `" ".join(text.split())` in `app/repo_inspect/claude_md_merge.py`.
🎯 Why: `re.sub` incurs regex engine overhead. `text.split()` splits by any whitespace and automatically drops leading/trailing whitespace, making it perfectly suited for collapsing whitespace.
📊 Impact: Built-in split and join is approximately 5x faster than using `re.sub` for this operation.

Dopo i fix precedenti, l'unico errore rimasto in telive.c su Ubuntu 25.10 era:
  telive.c:1532: error: too many arguments to function 'timeout_receivers';
                 expected 0, have 1   (declared 'void timeout_receivers()')
GCC 15 usa il C23 per default, dove '()' significa '(void)' (zero argomenti):
il vecchio codice K&R che passa argomenti in piu' (ignorati dalla funzione)
non compila. -std=gnu17 ripristina la semantica precedente ed e' il default su
GCC 11-14, quindi innocuo su 24.04.

Aggiunto -std=gnu17 ai flag di compatibilita' rilevati dal probe, in install_telive2.py e install_telive2.sh. La guardia di idempotenza del .sh ora si aggancia a -std=gnu17 (non piu' a -Wno-error=), cosi' aggiunge il nuovo flag anche su Makefile gia' patchati da run precedenti.

Riproduzione e verifica locali: -std=gnu2x ripropone l'errore, -std=gnu17 lo risolve. Nel log reale l'unico errore di telive.c era proprio timeout_receivers; il resto sono warning gia' gestiti.

author: salem874
body:
## 📋 Summary

Closes **#165**. The analytics dashboard, CSV export, and API v1 hard-blocked the shared `[default]` bucket org, so **every individually-registered user got no analytics at all**. Un-blocking naively would leak — all unassigned users share `orgHandle = '[default]'`, so an org-wide aggregate mixes their clicks.

## 🔐 Approach (data-isolation is the point)

Add an optional per-user scope to the data layer. When a `createdByUserUID` is supplied, every query additionally restricts to the rows whose short code the user **owns**:

```sql
shortCode IN (SELECT shortCode FROM tblShortURLs WHERE orgHandle = ? AND createdByUserUID = ?)
```

`shortCode` is unique per org, so within `[default]` this returns **exactly the caller's own links** (uses `IDX_url_creator`). Real-org callers pass `null` and keep org-wide analytics **unchanged**.

## 🔄 Surfaces (all four) + leak closures

- **`web/_functions/analytics.php`** — `Totals` / `ClicksOverTime` / `ScanSources` / `Breakdown` / `TopLinks` gain the optional scope.
- **`pages/analytics/index.php`** — the `[default]` block becomes per-user scoping; the `?code=` drill-down now requires **ownership** (was org-only → a `[default]` user could view another's code by guessing it).
- **`analytics-export.php`** — same treatment (block + drill-down).
- **`api/v1/handlers/analytics.php`** — both handlers scope a `[default]` key to the **key's owning user** (`tblAPIKeys.userUID`); the existence check requires ownership.

## ✅ Testing

- `php -l` clean on all 5 files; **unit suite 594 / 0**.
- **Isolation regression test** (`tests/integration/analytics_test.php`): a `[default]` aggregate scoped to a user who owns **no** `[default]` links returns **ZERO**, even though the org-wide total is 6 — proving one unassigned user can never see another's analytics. Runs in the `mysql:8` integration job.
- GlobalAdmin (also `[default]`) now sees their own links' analytics instead of nothing — strictly better, no leak.

## 🔗 Related

Closes #165. (Launch-gap item from the 2026-07-19 conformance audit.)

author: jarvichi
body:
## Summary

- Adds `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` so opening a GitHub Codespace on this repo installs dependencies automatically and forwards Storybook's port (6006).
- Documents an "Editing via GitHub Codespaces" workflow in `AGENTS.md`, so the map/bundle/battlefield in-app editors (which save by writing JSON files via local dev-server middleware in `web/.storybook/main.ts`) can be used from any browser, without a local dev machine.
- No changes to the editor save logic, `web/package.json`, or the existing GitHub Pages deploy (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) — this only adds the container config + docs.

## Why this approach

A static Storybook build (GitHub Pages/Chromatic/Vercel) can't support the in-app editors, since their "save" writes real files on a live Node process — something a static export has no server for. Codespaces runs the existing dev server unmodified inside a hosted container, so file writes keep working exactly as they do locally. GitHub's free tier (120 core-hours/month) comfortably covers casual editing sessions.

To avoid widening local dev's network exposure, the devcontainer does **not** change the default `storybook` script — the docs instead show running `npm run storybook -- --host 0.0.0.0` ad hoc, only inside the Codespace, needed for Codespaces' port forwarding to reach the server. Local dev keeps binding to `localhost` only.

## Security

- The editor save endpoints have no authentication of their own — security relies entirely on Codespaces' forwarded ports defaulting to **Private** (requires GitHub auth to reach). Docs call this out explicitly and warn never to set the port to Public while editing.
- No new secrets, tokens, or credentials are introduced.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a Codespace on this branch from the GitHub UI
- [ ] Confirm `postCreateCommand` (`cd web && npm install`) completes successfully

author: mikeab7
body:
Deliberately changes solver/geometry math (owner-requested). The polygon the user draws is the **fixed outer limit of disturbance** and never moves.

## D1 — inward berm geometry (outer-toe model)
New pure `lib/inwardBerm.js`. The drawn polygon is the outer **toe**; a rim `h` ft above grade builds the berm **inward** (crest = toe inset by `extSlope·h`), so the water surface + usable storage **shrink** with diminishing returns up to a **geometric ceiling** where the crest pinches closed. `pondGeom.bandedStorage`/`usablePondVolume` take a `gradeFt` and recompute every band on the inset crest when bermed (the classic drawn-ring model is untouched when `gradeFt` is null / the rim is at grade). The `pondSizing` solver is threaded `gradeFt`, and **`solveTobRaise` now scans** for the target/peak because inward usable is **non-monotonic** (it rises then falls to zero at the pinch) — the old monotonic assumption maxed the rim out at the geometric ceiling (an absurd ~100‑ft berm); it now stops at the smallest berm that closes the requirement, else the interior peak.

## D2 — rows / land-use flip to the fixed footprint
Land take = the FIXED drawn footprint (the "incl. berm ring" outward wording is gone; land take never exceeds water). The inspector shows **Water area** (shrinking) + a new **Berm ring** (EST) row, both summing to the footprint; the LAND USE legend reads "{water} ac water + {ring} ac berm (inside {total} ac footprint)". The outward-ring overlap watch-out is removed.

## D3 — the berm ring drawn INWARD
The warm-earth hatched ring now draws **between the outline and the inset crest** — inside the polygon, over the pond (a ground surface, below the building layer) so water shows only in the crest hole — with a "berm {h} ft" tag. Replaces C4's outward apron.

## D4 — function-based pond label
`pondLedger.pondDisplayName`/`pondDisplayNameFor` maps the resolved purpose → **Detention / Mitigation / "Detention + Mitigation" Pond**, at every render site that names a pond (panel header, map label, Yield row, RowInfo, context menu). The stored element type/id stays `"pond"`. A mitigation pond is no longer mislabeled "Detention Pond".

## D5 — computed berm cap (no user input)
The "Max berm (ft)" input + plumbing + "(your Max berm setting)" copy are **deleted**. The cap = the smaller of the **drainage cap** (runoff must reach the pond by gravity: max WSE = the lowest controlling inflow grade − a 0.5‑ft head allowance; max rim + freeboard; needs real terrain, else null) and the **geometric ceiling** (D1). A cap-bound solve names the binding constraint (`bermCapProposalNote`: drainage-bound vs geometry-bound). Without terrain, the solver falls back to a conservative clamp, not the raw geometric ceiling.

## Verification
- **Unit:** `test/inwardBerm.test.js` (water shrinks on square + irregular footprints; water + berm ring = footprint; geometric ceiling; above-flood volume vs a hand frustum; the cap arithmetic + binding selection), `test/pondLedger.test.js` (D4 role→noun), `test/pondChangeSummary.test.js` (`bermCapProposalNote` literals), `test/pondV3PrD.test.js` (SitePlanner wiring). Full suite **5021** green; build green.
- **e2e (real Chromium):** `ui-audit/verify-optimize-applies.mjs` — Optimize now raises the rim to a **sensible** inward berm (94→99.4, card shown, no errors), not an absurd raise; `verify-optimize-no-new-pond.mjs`, `verify-v3-pond-inspector.mjs`, `verify-panel-em-dash.mjs`, `verify-assumptions-disclosure.mjs`, `verify-v3-yield-panel.mjs` all green.
- Parks in ⏳ Verify → **V421** for the real-project confirmation (the drainage cap + inward-ring visuals need real 3DEP terrain).

author: voces
body:
## Draw 1 — branching p2c (INVALID-WASM → FULL support)

`(i32, i32, i32) => {[string]: K0 | i64 | {q: i64}}[] | boolean` — a closure
returning an ARRAY of maps whose value is a mixed litunion-alias + scalar + struct
union — emitted **invalid wasm**.

**Root cause:** the map's own local binding keys the mv table CANONICALLY — a mixed
litunion-alias value `K0 | i64 | {q: i64}` interns as `string | i64 | {q: i64}`
(`mvCanonValName`), a box-backed 7-field map struct. But the closure-result array
ELEMENT name preserves the `K0` alias (the `tyToEmitName` render, #945).
`mAssignTypeIndices`' kind-3 map-element heap resolver looked the value name up
**raw**, missed the canonically-keyed slot, and left the element heap at the shared
MONO map (i32-backed vals) while the captured maps are the box-backed struct:
`array.new_fixed` of a `(ref $boxMap)` into a `(ref null $monoMap)`-element array.

**Fix (one line):** canonicalize the value name via `mvCanonValName` before the mv
lookup, mirroring `mvShapeOfValName` / `mvSlotOfValNameFind`.

Verified: the fix also lets the array-of-maps values round-trip correctly at runtime
(the i64 `5000000077` and the `K0` atom `428` read back through `t0[i]["k"]`). The
consuming path *with* the outer `| boolean` narrowing is a SEPARATE, pre-existing
loud-reject gap ("value-union closure RESULT is not yet representable"), untouched.

## Draw 2 — multiobs p3r (already fixed; entombed as a regression)

`{a: {f: {f: f64}[]} | null, f: i64, z: {f: ({f: f64} | boolean)[] | f64}}` — same-
fieldset `{f}` nesting + a union-element array field — **already validates and runs
correctly** on current master (fixed by the nul-struct-array / emitArr null-seed /
variant-box arc, #1006/#1008/#1010). Added as a regression pin.

## Pins
- `maps/closure-result-array-of-mixed-union-value-maps.vl` — distinguishes the fix
  (baseline emits invalid wasm; fixed round-trips the values)
- `structs/same-fieldset-nest-with-union-elem-array-field.vl` — multiobs regression

## Gate
`refresh-compiler` + `rep-fuzz-check` (exact) + `native-fixpoint` (byte-identical,
947578 bytes) + `lint-self` + `SELFHOST_NATIVE_ALIGN=1 deno task test` (1843 passed,
0 failed) all green.

author: predict-woo
body:
## Summary

Replaces the custom chat UI (SwiftUI transcript/composer + `codex app-server` JSON-RPC) with an embedded [Ghostty](https://github.com/Lakr233/libghostty-spm) terminal that runs the ChatGPT app's packaged codex TUI directly, per note. Codex now owns the whole conversational surface — composer, streaming, approvals, model switching, slash commands — and Simbi just hosts the window. Net **−1,595 / +185 lines** across the feature commits.

- **`TerminalChatLaunch` (CodexKit, unit-tested):** one constant command string; everything per-note travels in per-surface env vars (no shell/TOML escaping anywhere). Note context is injected with `-c developer_instructions="$SIMBI_CHAT_CONTEXT"` — a developer message describing the note folder layout and current file names (never contents; codex reads files itself from the note cwd). Verified against the packaged binary: the injected instructions demonstrably reach the model. Parity flags with the old chat: `-s workspace-write -a on-request`, `--add-dir` for the Simbi home, `CODEX_HOME=~/.codex` (shared ChatGPT login).
- **`ChatWindow` (SimbiUI):** same type, `windowId`, and open flow (app shell and NoteView untouched); now hosts `TerminalSurfaceView` with the note folder as working directory, a degraded banner when the ChatGPT app is missing, and a session-ended overlay with restart.
- **Deleted the superseded stack:** ChatSession/ChatEvents/ChatTranscript/ChatContextPrompt/MarkdownSegmenter, chat views/model, the `chatModel` setting, and the M7 chat spike. `AppServerClient` stays for fixer/converter/transcription/model-list.
- **M8 spike** (`swift run simbi-terminal-spike`) that proved the direction, plus evidence dirs.

## Dependency note (fork)

Xcode's `ProcessXCFramework` copies every static xcframework's `Headers/` flat into `Products/<config>/include/`, so GhosttyKit's `module.modulemap` collided with FluidAudio's NemoTextProcessing ("Multiple commands produce"; Apple forums 682110/726701; `swift build` unaffected). This PR pins **`predict-woo/libghostty-spm` tag `1.3.2-simbi.1`** — upstream 1.3.2 repackaged byte-for-byte with headers moved under `Headers/GhosttyKitHeaders/` (the MacPaw/Setapp fix pattern). Both `swift build`/`swift test` and `xcodebuild` are green. Worth offering upstream to Lakr233 later.

## Ghostty launch traps (unit-tested)

Ghostty runs `command =` via `bash -c "exec -l <value>"` **and** strips a matching pair of surrounding double quotes from the value. So the command must not start with `exec` (→ `exec exec`) and must neither start nor end with `"`. Tokenization proven with an argv-dump substituted for the codex binary under the exact wrapper.

## Verification

- `swift test`: 106 tests, 27 suites, all passing (includes new `TerminalChatLaunchTests`).
- `xcodebuild` Debug build green; app launched and UI-verified end-to-end by an orchestrated Computer-Use worker: the Chat window boots the codex TUI in `~/Simbi/Codex Terminal Demo`, and codex answered a question by reading the seeded `transcript.vtt` ("ships Thursday"). Screenshots + notes: `docs/verification/2026-07-23-terminal-chat/`, spike evidence in `docs/verification/2026-07-23-terminal-spike/`.

## Risks / follow-ups

- `developer_instructions` is a config key of the packaged alpha binary (present in codex docs/config schema, verified working) — re-verify on codex bumps.
- The TUI honors the user's `~/.codex` config (hooks, model); our explicit sandbox/approval flags override the config's approval mode.
- Per-note session resume (`codex resume <id>`) not wired yet; each window opens a fresh session (`/resume` works inside the TUI).
- libghostty-spm is young (~4.5 months) and tracks a pinned Ghostty commit; theming the surface to match Simbi is future polish.

body:
## What does this change do?
Records the lesson behind #148/#149 as a durable rule in Sylvester #15's repo lens
(`.claude/plugins/claude-specialists/specialists/05-15-extension.md`), so the next check or hook that
dot-sources a consumer's repo-owned lib gets it right by design instead of rediscovering it at
runtime. Added in the "Repo-specific rules" section as a third rule of that kind, joining its two
sibling native-command rules (the `$LASTEXITCODE`-before-pipe rule and the stderr-under-`Stop` rule):

- **The rule:** a check/hook that dot-sources `branch-info.ps1`/`repo-config.ps1` to probe it must do
  so in a child scope with `Set-StrictMode -Off`, because the real workflow scripts that consume those
  libs never enable StrictMode and the libs are written on that assumption. Loading under strict mode
  makes harmless pre-strict-mode loose top-level code throw — a false `[ERROR]`, or a full crash under
  `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` — at every session start, for exactly the older consumer repos the
  checks serve. A genuine load failure should degrade gracefully, not abort the check.

Doc-only; no script or config change (the two fixes themselves shipped in #148/#149).

Plugins: specialists

## Type of change
<!-- Check the branch type (prefix + label listed alongside). -->

author: thoenissen
body:
## Summary

RH8303 no longer flags a `///` documentation header that directly follows an ordinary comment (`//` / `////`) or a preprocessor directive. Its exemption set now matches RH5020. An RH8302 regression test is added for the `////` fenced-out block scenario.

## Why

RH8303 demanded a blank line before documentation headers even when the preceding line was a comment or a directive. The formatter treats adjacent comment blocks as a single unit and leaves directive-adjacent comments untouched (issue #415), so no CLI formatting phase could satisfy those diagnostics — they stayed permanently reported after `reihitsu-format` and contradicted RH5020's own directive exemption. The `////` misclassification called out for RH8302/RH8303 was already resolved on `main` via `IsDocumentationLine`; the new RH8302 test locks that behavior in against regressions.

## Linked issues

Closes #449

## Review notes

- RH8303 now additionally skips when the previous non-blank line starts with `//` (comment, including `////`) or `#` (any preprocessor directive), alongside the existing open-brace exemption. The check stays text-based to match the analyzer's line-oriented implementation while mirroring RH5020's trivia-based exemptions.
- Behavior change: fewer RH8303 diagnostics — only headers the formatter will actually separate remain flagged, so every remaining diagnostic is CLI-fixable.
- `documentation/rules/RH8303.md` gains an "Exemptions" section describing the comment/directive carve-outs.

## Follow-up work

None.

author: lukaszpodgorski-pl
body:
## Co się zmienia

Trzy przyciski CTA w hero na stronie głównej miały jednakową wagę wizualną i nie reagowały na hover. Teraz:

- **"Zacznij naukę" i "Wybierz swoją ścieżkę"** tworzą parę o równej szerokości - to dwa równorzędne wejścia do treści.
- **"Współtwórz na GitHubie"** schodzi do własnego wiersza, mniejszym stopniem pisma i wygaszonym kolorem - dotyczy współtworzenia, nie nauki.

Hover unosi przycisk, dodaje poświatę w kolorze akcentu i przesuwa ikonę w stronę, którą ta ikona oznacza. `:focus-visible` dostaje to samo co mysz, więc klawiatura nie jest poszkodowana.

Zmiana dotyczy wyłącznie `src/styles/custom.css`. `index.mdx` zostaje bez zmian - warianty `primary` / `secondary` / `minimal` już niosły właściwą semantykę, brakowało tylko stylu.

## Trzy rzeczy, które wyszły po drodze

**Grid zamiast flexa.** Naturalne `flex-basis: 100%` zepchnęłoby link GitHuba do własnego wiersza, ale przy okazji rozciągnęłoby jego pole klikalne na całą szerokość - kliknięcie w pustkę daleko od tekstu wyrzucałoby poza serwis. `grid-column: 1 / -1` z `justify-self: center` daje ten sam podział, trzymając pole klikalne przy tekście.

**Przyciski lgnęły do lewej.** Powyżej 50rem Starlight ustawia `.actions` na `justify-content: flex-start`, więc przy naszym wyśrodkowanym hero przyciski siedziały przy lewej krawędzi, mimo że nagłówek i tagline są na środku. Naprawione przy okazji.

**Kontrast poniżej progu WCAG.** Naturalnym wyborem koloru tekstu na hoverze było `--sl-color-text-accent`, ale w motywie jasnym to `#0d9488`, co na tle `--sl-color-accent-low` daje 3,3:1 - poniżej progu AA. Użyte `--sl-color-accent-high` daje 6,7:1 w jasnym i 9,8:1 w ciemnym.

## `prefers-reduced-motion`

Blok wycisza **ruch**, a nie całe sprzężenie zwrotne: kasowane są same przesunięcia, a przenikanie koloru i cienia zostaje. Bez tego hover staje się twardym przeskokiem stanu - a Windows ma tę preferencję włączoną zawsze, gdy użytkownik wyłączy "Efekty animacji" w ustawieniach ułatwień dostępu, więc to częsty przypadek, nie egzotyczny wyjątek. W pliku jest komentarz ostrzegający przed powrotem do `transition: none`.

## Weryfikacja

- `npm run build` - 68 stron, bez błędów
- `scripts/verify-geo.mjs` - 24/24 asercji
- Obejrzane w motywie jasnym i ciemnym, przy 1440px i 390px
- Przejście potwierdzone pomiarem `transform` w trakcie animacji (-2,16px → -2,93px → -3,00px przy 60/140/400 ms), a nie samym zrzutem stanu końcowego
- Ścieżka `prefers-reduced-motion` sprawdzona osobno: przesunięcie wyłączone, przenikanie koloru działa

author: shadrackmanfred
body:
## Changes

### Closes #192 — [Backend] Add health check endpoint with dependency status
- `backend/src/routes/health.ts`: added `aggregateStatus()` helper. With critical deps (postgres, redis) failed the aggregate is now `unhealthy`; otherwise `degraded` (peripheral only); otherwise `healthy`. The error-fallback in the catch branch also emits `unhealthy` because a synchronously-thrown check is, in practice, a critical dep failing.
- `backend/src/__tests__/health.test.ts`: updated assertions; added a degraded-but-only-non-critical test case.

### Closes #178 — [Backend] Implement background job processing for email notifications
- `backend/src/workers/emailWorker.js` *(new)*: Periodic worker that drains `queueManager.processQueue()` every `EMAIL_WORKER_INTERVAL_MS` ms (default 30 s). Includes idempotent `start()`/`stop()`, error-resilient `tick()`, runtime stats, env-aware interval resolution per-instance.
- `backend/src/routes/admin/jobs.js` *(new)*: Monitoring dashboard endpoints at `/api/v1/admin/jobs/email/stats` (queue depth + worker stats) and `/api/v1/admin/jobs/email/events?userId=&emailType=&eventType=&limit=` (recent delivery events; limit clamped to 1..1000).
- `backend/src/index.js`: started/stopped worker inside the existing transaction worker lifecycle; mounted the router.

### Design note re. Bull/BullMQ
The issue mentions Bull/BullMQ. We deliberately reuse the existing in-memory `queueManager` (with the optional `config/redis.js` scaffolding already shipped) rather than introduce a new dependency in this single PR. Bull-style semantics — retries with exponential backoff, processor registration, monitoring dashboard, delivery-event tracking, and template variable substitution — are all already in place via the existing email service. A follow-up PR can swap the storage backend to BullMQ without changing callers if/when persistence across restarts becomes a hard requirement.

### Security note (intentional gap)
`/api/v1/admin/jobs/*` exposes `userId`s, queue payloads, and recipient emails. The route is intentionally unauthenticated. Recommended follow-up: mount the router behind gateway/ingress auth, or add `authenticateToken`, `requireAdmin` (from `../../middleware/auth`) at mount time. The header comment in `routes/admin/jobs.js` documents this.

## Tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/emailWorker.test.js` *(new)*: lifecycle, tick, error handling, env-aware interval, stats shape — 9/9 passing in the local environment.
- `backend/src/__tests__/adminJobs.test.js` *(new)*: stats/events endpoint shaping, item cap, limit clamping, error-to-500 path. Some of these currently fail in the local environment due to `tests/setup.js` pre-loading `../src/index` (transitively caching `routes/admin/jobs.js` with real `getQueueManager`/`getEmailService` references) and `MongoMemoryServer` failing to start — both pre-existing test-isolation issues, not regressions in the route logic. Recommended follow-up: move `const app = require(`../src/index`)` out of `tests/setup.js` (it is not consumed by anything in that file) so the per-test `jest.mock(...)` calls in any test can be honored.

## Files
- modified: `backend/src/__tests__/health.test.ts`, `backend/src/index.js`, `backend/src/routes/health.ts`
- new:      `backend/src/__tests__/adminJobs.test.js`, `backend/src/__tests__/emailWorker.test.js`, `backend/src/routes/admin/jobs.js`, `backend/src/workers/emailWorker.js`

body:
# Test-suite mock audit & true-up (all services) + clock-job removal

## What this is

A full audit and true-up of the pytest suites for **bot-core, discord-gateway, and blender-service** against three rules:

1. **No mock where a suitable live object can be constructed** (real ORM models, real SQLite/PG sessions, real pydantic schemas, real discord.py types, respx transport-level HTTP).
2. **Remaining mocks must be complete and true to the entity they represent** — no "accept any request, return 200" responders (the pattern behind the recent prod defect).
3. **≤2 mocks per test** as the target; overages carry an in-file justification.

18 parallel audit workers surveyed all ~330 test files (~9,400 tests), then 13 staged refactor workers applied the fixes area by area, each gated on its own tests passing. Plus, per request: the time-announcement ("clock") prototype job is fully removed.

## Final gates (all green)

| Suite | Baseline | After |
|---|---|---|
| bot-core | 5,657 passed, 5 skipped | **5,559 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed** |
| discord-gateway | 3,430 passed | **3,460 passed** |
| blender-service | 274 passed | **274 passed** |

Count deltas are justified deletions (vacuous/tautological/source-grep tests, documented per file in commit messages) offset by new behavioral coverage; the 1 xfail is a deliberate marker for a real latent bug (below). bot-core live-DB modules ran against disposable migrated+seeded postgres:18 containers — never the prod DB.

## Highlights of what was fixed

- **Accept-anything HTTP responders eliminated or contracted**: gateway cog suites now carry respx contract tests asserting route/verb/payload for every destructive admin command and the player/shop/ship/inventory endpoints; bot-core executor/router tests use respx routed on the real URLs with real error types. The shared `make_mock_response` factory now returns a **real `httpx.Response`** whose `raise_for_status()` actually raises.
- **Central discord mock factory made faithful**: real `discord.Embed`/`Colour`/`Permissions`/`PermissionOverwrite`/`MessageType`, spec'd `Interaction`, Member attribute delegation, falsy-when-unset assets; phantom attributes removed.
- **Gateway API-router tests unpatched the pure code**: real converters serialize the responses (bodies are genuine output), real `get_entity_or_404`/`find_thread_by_id`/`handle_discord_exception` run (real 404 fallback and error mapping); fake-`discord` `sys.modules` swaps deleted.
- **Repository filter tests are real**: SQLite round-trips with seeded rows replace hard-coded mock returns (WHERE-clause bugs can no longer pass green); ARRAY-blocked repos use kwarg-capturing fakes over real model constructors.
- **Migration tests drive the real migrations**: b19 repair and combat_log now run the actual `upgrade()`/`downgrade()` against live PG in rolled-back transactions instead of an in-test reimplementation.
- **MagicMock entity stand-ins replaced with real models** across service/api/integration tests (`Player`, `PlayerShip`, `GuildConfig`, `Bounty`, `DuelRequest`, `CombatLog`, …), killing the "any attribute is truthy" failure mode.
- **Tautologies removed or rewritten**: tests that asserted their own monkeypatched values, `assert len(...) >= 0`, `status in (200, 400)`, spy-only assertions, and inline reimplementations of production logic.
- **Integration suite deepened**: live-PG e2e now drives the real combat-win → loot-write trigger seam; the 150-case loadout property sweep runs the real `LoadoutConsistencyService`; cross-session ops call the real services.

## Clock-job removal

The time-announcement prototype (early APScheduler POC) is fully removed: `/time` router package (it was never mounted in prod — router auto-discovery skips the `announcements/` subpackage), `time_announcement_executor`, the `message_builders/` package (existed solely for the clock builder), the `job_executor` dispatch branch, all clock tests, and doc references.

## Real production bugs surfaced by truer tests (not fixed here — src is out of scope except the removal)

1. **Latent item-loss in `LoadoutConsistencyService`** (`loadout_consistency_service.py:224/:778`): a player legitimately owning 2 copies of one item name, equipped on two ships, loses a copy when either ship is evacuated (sell/transfer/activate-reconcile). Marked by a strict xfail in `test_loadout_consistency_property.py`. Fix options documented in the audit FOLLOWUPS.
2. **`guilds.py::create_role`** uses nonexistent `status.HTTP_422` → `AttributeError` → 500 instead of the intended 422 (both validation branches).
3. **`tags.py::create_forum_tag`/`update_tag`** — same nonexistent-`status.HTTP_422` defect class.
4. **`module_repository.create_or_update`** leaks camelCase source keys (e.g. `builtIn`) into `extra_atts` alongside the correctly-mapped snake_case column — spurious duplicate data for every module seeded from JSON.
5. *(Removed rather than fixed)* the clock DELETE endpoint called `httpx.AsyncClient.delete(url, json=...)`, a `TypeError` on httpx 0.28.1 → guaranteed 500; previously invisible behind an accept-anything mock.

## Remaining follow-ups (documented, deliberately not half-done)

- Bulk happy-path tests in `test_playerCog/shopCog/shipsCog/bountyCog/duelCog/aboutCog` still use the (now-faithful) factory mock; respx contract classes cover the endpoint contracts, but full per-test migration is a large mechanical pass.
- `test_channels_extended.py` converter unpatching (~74 tests) — the two app builders still patch converters.
- `Ship`/`Module` ARRAY columns block SQLite round-trips in two spots (would need a src-side ARRAY→JSON type variant or PG fixtures).
- Gateway `_autocomplete_health_probe` is a non-importable nested closure — recommend extracting for direct testing.
- `test_database.py` MINOR engine-mock swap (rated faithful/low-risk, deprioritized).

## Full-suite isolation fix

The per-group gates all passed, but the first full-suite gateway run failed 331 api tests: xdist workers collect (import) the whole suite up front, and cogs modules that pop `discord` from `sys.modules` at import time leave later imports bound to a second generation of discord classes — fatal once the api tests run real `isinstance`/`except discord.NotFound` dispatch. Fixed with `tests/api/conftest.py`, which pins the discord generation around every api test. This one is worth knowing about: it's the failure mode that appears whenever a test file gets truer about class identity.

## Process notes

- Branch is based on `origin/dev` (not main) so this suite-wide PR applies cleanly to its target; dev == main + your merged fixes at branch time.
- Every slice was committed only after its area gate passed; two `wip:` commits mark session-limit interruptions mid-flight (safe snapshots, superseded by the following commits).
- The full worker-authored follow-up detail is committed as `TEST_SUITE_TRUEUP_FOLLOWUPS.md`, and all items are tracked in `OPEN_ITEMS.md` (TRUEUP-01..05 test quality, TRUEUP-P1..P4 production defects).

body:
## What this does

The new **Course Leaderboard**: one board ranking every rep across all 10 courses, replacing the one-course-at-a-time table. Builds directly on the scoring foundations merged in PR #15.

### The board (web, all five role pages)

- **Overall view (default):** every ranked rep as a roster row card: rank, avatar (initials fallback), name, colored rank pill (Rookie → Legend), badges, branch · team, and a progress ring. Top 3 get medals. Reps with zero progress sit in a collapsed "Not started" group instead of padding the ranking.
- **By Course view:** same cards scoped to one course, with the true company rank shown as `co.#X`. Reuses the existing `?courseId=` endpoint untouched, so the four Flutter screens that depend on it need no release.
- **Filters:** search, Branch, Team. Filtered lists show dual ranks (local + company); medals never appear in a filtered list, they always mean the company-wide top 3.
- **Self-explanatory:** collapsed "What the icons and ranks mean" legend (same UX as the sales board's guide), a dismissible welcome banner, and tooltips on every game term. No em dashes anywhere in copy.
- **Role behavior from AuthContext:** reps and team leads get a pinned "Your rank" strip with a next-milestone nudge; team leads also get a "Your team" card (avg %, team rank); branch managers open pre-filtered to their branch; admins get a visible `⋯` menu (Override, Hide) replacing the old invisible white-on-white buttons. **Export CSV is gone; Override/Hide are now admin-only** (they were previously reachable by leads/BMs/C-Level invisibly).

### Under the hood

- New endpoint `GET /api/training/leaderboard?scope=overall` aggregating per-rep stats server-side through the shared pure modules.
- New pure module `src/lib/training/board.ts` (aggregation, milestones, rank labels, filters, team standings), unit-tested alongside `scoring.ts`: **71 Vitest tests, all green**.
- Badge set v2: dropped First Steps (no signal), renamed Quiz Ace → **Test Ace**.
- The old 976-line `CourseLeaderboard.tsx` is deleted; all five role shells mount the new `src/portals/shared/training-leaderboard/` suite.
- **Aligned with e7bb71d's quiz-pass rule:** `courseStats` now counts a quiz as passed by the presence of a saved result (via the shared `isQuizResultPassing`) instead of re-checking stored scores, so the board can never disagree with the lesson ticks. Test Ace remains score-based (true 100% on the Final Test).

### Fixed along the way

The old Override tool's user picker still matched `roles[]` (offering branch managers as override targets); the rebuilt modal filters on the primary role via the shared `isRankedUser`. Override saves now report failures instead of silently closing, and three stale-response races (course switching in the modal and By Course view) are guarded.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 71/71 passing (scoring + board pure modules).
- `npm run build` clean at every task boundary.
- Manually verified in a local session against production data: scrubbed roster, correct ranks/percentages, filters + dual ranks, By Course, legend/banner/tooltips, admin Override + Hide round-trips, responsive layout, avatar fallback.

## Review

Executed task-by-task with a review gate per task plus a final whole-branch review (verdict: merge ready). The loop caught and fixed 10 real bugs pre-merge, including an admin override path that could silently erase a rep's real quiz progress, and the quiz-pass rule divergence introduced by the mid-flight main sync.

## Not in this PR (later slices)

Per-rep detail modal, deeper per-course stats, Team vs Team panel, rank-change arrows, the guided tour, and real-money rewards. Design spec and implementation plan live in `docs/` (gitignored by convention); happy to share separately.

body:
With the OAuth2 (PKCE) web sign-in flow introduced in #5093, the native GSI-based web implementation in `serverpod_auth_idp_flutter` is no longer needed. The Google-hosted web button was already removed in #5384. 

This PR removes the remaining runtime fallback so the PKCE redirect flow is the only Google sign-in path on web.

- `initializeGoogleSignIn` now throws an ArgumentError on web when redirectUri is not provided, instead of silently falling back to the google_sign_in package.
- `GoogleAuthController` no longer initializes or subscribes to `google_sign_in` on web.
- Removed the `google_sign_in_web` dependency.
- Removed web-only workarounds that existed for the old button.

Note: this PR is stacked on #5384 and should be merged after it.

Fixes #5442 

## Pre-launch Checklist

- [x] I read the [Contribute](https://docs.serverpod.dev/contribute) page and followed the process outlined there for submitting PRs.
- [x] This update contains only one single feature or bug fix and nothing else. (If you are submitting multiple fixes, please make multiple PRs.)
- [x] I read and followed the [Dart Style Guide](https://dart.dev/guides/language/effective-dart/style) and formatted the code with [dart format](https://dart.dev/tools/dart-format).
- [x] I listed at least one issue that this PR fixes in the description above.
- [x] I updated/added relevant documentation (doc comments with `///`), and made sure that the documentation follows the same style as other Serverpod documentation. I checked spelling and grammar.
- [ ] I added new tests to check the change I am making.
- [x] All existing and new tests are passing.
- [x] Any breaking changes are documented below.

If you need help, consider asking for advice on the [discussion board](https://github.com/serverpod/serverpod/discussions).

## Breaking changes

author: fra85h
body:
## Causa

Su un annuncio CERCO l'unica azione disponibile per chi ha già il biglietto giusto era "pubblica un nuovo annuncio" — inutile per chi il proprio VENDO ce l'ha già pubblicato. Non esisteva un modo leggero per avvisare direttamente chi cerca.

## Fix

Aggiunge un "Ping": una notifica leggera (niente offerta, niente chat) che chi ha un VENDO attivo compatibile può inviare al proprietario di un CERCO, con link diretto al proprio annuncio.

- **Migration** `20260722150000_listing_pings.sql`: tabella `listing_pings` con `UNIQUE (from_listing_id, to_listing_id)` come antispam (un ping per coppia di annunci); RLS con sola `select` del proprio mittente (scrittura solo da service-role); estende `notifications.type` con `'listing_ping'`.
- `server/src/models/pings.js` — `sendListingPing`: valida che l'annuncio sorgente sia un VENDO attivo del chiamante e quello target un CERCO attivo altrui (stessa regola di dominio già applicata alle offerte), inserisce il ping e la notifica al proprietario. Una violazione dell'UNIQUE (23505, anche in race su doppio click) è trattata come "già inviato", non come errore.
- `server/src/routes/pings.js` — `POST /api/pings`, con rate limit dedicato (20/10min, `rateLimitPings`).
- `components/OfferCTA.js` — nel ramo CERCO, se l'utente ha almeno un VENDO attivo dello stesso tipo, mostra il bottone "Ho già un annuncio → Segnalalo a chi cerca"; con più annunci compatibili chiede quale segnalare.
- `screens/NotificationsScreen.js` — icona dedicata per `listing_ping` e deep-link diretto al VENDO segnalato.
- Stringhe aggiunte in `lib/i18n/translations.js` (it/en/es, parità verificata).

## ⚠️ Azione manuale

Nuova migration da eseguire a mano nel SQL Editor di Supabase: `supabase/migrations/20260722150000_listing_pings.sql`.

author: n-shadloo
body:
## Summary

Adds the voice-room layer: persistent rooms that store nothing but an id and an
encrypted name, short-lived LiveKit join tokens minted server-side, and live
membership plus ephemeral room text that ride the WebSocket and non-persistent
Redis only. The server signs tokens and relays ciphertext — it never joins the
media path, and no media key ever reaches it.

## What changed

- **`voicerooms` app** — create/read/rename rooms (opaque bucketed name blob,
  full-scope tokens only, per-endpoint throttles); `POST /rooms/{id}/token`
  returns a 300-second HS256 grant scoped to exactly one room and one device,
  microphone-only publish, data channel off, no key material in any claim.
- **Live presence** — native Redis set ops instead of cached pickled sets,
  which measurably lost concurrent joins (16 simultaneous joins left as few as
  3 members). A day-long, activity-refreshed expiry self-heals members
  stranded by a crashed worker.
- **Realtime consumer** — `room_subscribe` / `room_leave` / `room_signal`
  branches: UUID-normalized ids (raw input previously crashed the consumer and
  leaked the value into a traceback), 100-subscription per-socket cap,
  join/leave presence broadcasts, and relay frames that carry no sender.
- **Ops** — LiveKit config bound to loopback behind an nginx `/rtc` proxy,
  systemd unit composing its keys from the environment file, TURN-only coturn
  in a relay-only posture with secrets filled into the root-owned config
  rather than world-readable CLI argv, and new env entries.

## Testing

- Full suite: **424 passed + 35 subtests** (83 in the `voicerooms/` and
  `realtime/` suites), `manage.py check` clean.
- Exit tests: repo-wide media-key isolation (model fields, serializer fields,
  schema grep, decoded token claims); `pg_dump` shows only
  `id, name_blob, created_date, updated_date` with the blob at an exact bucket
  length and no membership/room-text table; two sockets exchange a room signal
  with **zero** new rows in any table; log capture beneath the scrub filter
  sees no id or blob.
- Key tests were verified to fail under deliberate sabotage (grant widened,
  log line added, normalization removed) before trusting their passes.
- Measured: every endpoint does one view query (pkey index scans at 10k rows);
  live count is O(1) Redis at any member count; consumer handlers do no
  synchronous ORM on the event loop.

## Breaking changes

None — new endpoints and socket message types only; existing APIs untouched.

author: jason-shoe
body:
## Why

Neither install path self-updates: `npm i -g @feastalytics/cli` is frozen at whatever version was installed, and `npx @feastalytics/cli` reuses its `~/.npm/_npx` cache. Global-install users have no signal at all that a publish happened.

## What

- `src/updateNotifier.ts` — checks `registry.npmjs.org` for the `latest` dist-tag at most once per 24h, caches `{checkedAt, latest}` in `~/.config/feast-cli/update-check.json`, and prints an upgrade hint to stderr **after** the command finishes so it never interleaves with output.
- Wired into `src/cli.ts` after `runCli` resolves/rejects; its own rejection is swallowed so it can't turn a successful command into a failure.
- Opt-outs: non-TTY stderr, `CI`, `FEAST_NO_UPDATE_CHECK`, `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`. Documented in `feast help` and the README.
- Network call is bounded at 1.5s via `AbortSignal.timeout` and fails silently — offline runs are unaffected, and the cache timestamp is still stamped so a failed check doesn't retry every invocation.

```
Update available: feast 0.1.1 → 0.2.0
  npx @feastalytics/cli@latest <command>   (or: npm install -g @feastalytics/cli@latest)
```

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; built and ran `node dist/cli.js` under a pty:
- seeded cache at `9.9.9` → notice printed
- no cache → live fetch resolved `0.1.1`, no notice, cache written
- `FEAST_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` → silent; non-TTY stderr → silent
- unknown command still exits 1

author: duikland
body:
## PWD.ACT.6 — CityLife pending activation and token redemption UX (PR-E)

Adds the bounded CityLife player flow over the already-merged PWD.ACT backends
(`kooker-service-user` 1.31.0, `kooker-service-auth` 1.13.5, and the public
APISIX `POST /api/users/password-activate` route at infra `e5e8c60a`). Frontend only.

### Flow
- **Request (E1, authenticated):** `PasswordChangePanel` in the signed-in HUD re-proves the current
  password and takes a new one with a private client-side confirmation, calling
  `POST /kooker/api/users/me/password-change-request` as the logged-in player.
- **Immediate signed-out pending state:** on success the backend revokes the session; the client sets
  a one-shot non-secret pending flag, signs out, and reloads to the login gate, which explains the
  change is waiting on activation.
- **Redemption (E3, public token-free):** `PasswordActivateScreen` from the login gate takes the email
  and the 32-hex activation token and calls `POST /kooker/api/users/password-activate`. On success it
  confirms and returns to normal sign-in with the new password.

### Guarantees
- Reuses the visitor-activation interaction language **without conflating** visitor unlock and password
  activation — separate client (`passwordActivateClient`) and screen, sharing only the hex formatter.
- Old and pending passwords never create a session before redemption; the client never fabricates one.
- Every activation failure surfaces one generic message (no oracle).
- Passwords and the plaintext token live only in component state and the single request body — never
  logged, persisted, bridged, or placed in a URL.

### Tests / docs
- `tests/passwordActivateClient.test.ts`, `tests/passwordChangeClient.test.ts` — exact path, body,
  bearer-presence/absence, generic-failure and signed-out behaviours.
- `e2e/passwordActivation.spec.ts` — mocked-backend redeem happy path, generic error, signed-in change
  to signed-out pending, and client-side confirm-mismatch never reaching the backend.
- Spec `docs/specs/154-citylife-password-activation-ux.md` and the docs index link (ALWAYS-DOCUMENTED).
- Playwright port is env-overridable (`CITYLIFE_E2E_PORT`); the 5191 default is unchanged for CI.

### Verification
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (1550 passed), `npm run build`, and the new e2e (4 passed) are green.

### Scope
No merge, deploy, production activation, or DONE — human UAT is final.

author: julius-retzer
body:
## Why

The repo has no `.coderabbit.yaml`, so CodeRabbit auto-reviews **every PR on open**. At our PR volume that drains the shared CodeRabbit account's fair-usage/adaptive review budget — and once it's exhausted, every brass PR stalls waiting for a review that never lands (this happened today across ~6 PRs). Making review **opt-in** means a PR only spends budget when we explicitly ask.

## What this does

Adds a root `.coderabbit.yaml` that turns **off** automatic per-PR review while keeping both opt-in paths working:

- **`coderabbit` label** — a positive label match triggers a review even while `auto_review.enabled: false` (per CodeRabbit's v2 schema), so the label is the visible opt-in signal.
- **`@coderabbitai review` comment** — on-demand review, always works regardless of config.

Config is schema-valid against the current CodeRabbit v2 config schema (`reviews.auto_review.enabled` / `reviews.auto_review.labels`). No app or code behavior changes — repo config only.

## ⚠️ Takes effect only once merged

CodeRabbit reads its config from the **base branch**, not the PR head. So this PR itself — and every other currently-open PR — is **not** gated until this merges to `main`. Automated review on this PR is waived (the account is over its shared limit right now anyway).

A present-but-failing sha tool warns instead of silently skipping checksum verification.
- `.codex-plugin/mcp.json` + `mcpServers` manifest field, so Codex's plugin flow registers the server too.
- `.opencode/plugins/gnomcp.js` self-registers `config.mcp.gnomcp` (binary from PATH or `~/.local/bin`; a user-configured entry wins), the pattern every MCP-bundling OpenCode plugin uses.
- README, docs, and site wording updated: Codex is wired automatically; OpenCode gets printed steps.

Validated live: a real install run followed by `codex mcp list` showing gnomcp enabled; the OpenCode config hook exercised with node (registration, user override preserved, idempotent re-run).

body:
## What (owner request)

Clicking **New Game** / **Continue** dropped the player on the canvas title screen with a character preview and a *second* DESCEND button — a redundant step now that the React Main Menu is the real entry point. This removes that: the menu starts the chosen run directly.

## How

- The engine now accepts a `startMode` via `mount()` and auto-starts that run in `boot()`, skipping the canvas title + character preview:
  - `'new'` / `'continue'` → `onStart()` (fresh run / resume saved session)
  - `'cycle'` → New Game+ (Null Cycles)
  - `'abyss'` → The Null Abyss
- The post-completion **NEW GAME+** and **THE NULL ABYSS** entries lived on the now-skipped canvas title, so they move into the **React Main Menu**, shown only once this wallet has finished the campaign (same `nullstate-protocolzero` per-wallet flag `game.js` already writes).
- The canvas title is still reachable **in-session** via `returnToTitleScreen()` after finishing the campaign, so its buttons keep working as a fallback.
- `startMode` threaded `GameFlowManager → DungeonGameWrapper → DungeonGame → engine mount`. Non-menu / demo mounts (no `startMode`) still show the title exactly as before.

## Notes

- This intentionally reverses a prior "OWNER FIX" that had *added* the preview on Continue — the owner now prefers going straight in.

## Verification

- `node --check public/game-engine/game.js` passes.
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes.
- ⚠️ Needs a device playtest to confirm the straight-to-gameplay feel and that New Game+/Abyss appear in the menu after completing the campaign.

author: jmbish04
body:
## AI Gateway actual-cost tracking + gateway CRUD

The AI Gateway **API exposes no third-party price catalog** (verified — providers endpoint is metadata, models/search is @cf-only). But its **analytics record what Cloudflare actually charged** per model. This captures that as a second, authoritative source and adds gateway management.

### Actual cost → D1
- `ai_gateway_costs` — **daily cron** snapshots `aiGatewayRequestsAdaptiveGroups` (cost + tokens per gateway/provider/model/day) into permanent history (GraphQL retains only ~31d). Deterministic PK, idempotent upsert. **508 rows live.**
- Ingestion: cron over GraphQL analytics — no Enterprise Logpush needed; Logpush stays the future per-request upgrade.

### Cross-check (the "make sure both sources agree" you asked for)
- **Drift check** — scraped list price vs actual gateway cost, **third-party only** (Workers AI @cf models bill by neurons, not the catalog token price). Verified **gemini scraped ≈ actual within 10%** — the scrape validates against reality.

### Dual-source pricing history
- `POST /api/ai-models/pricing-history` (+ MCP `ai_models_pricing_history`): advertised (scraped) **and/or** actual (gateway) over a date range, `source = both | scraped | gateway`.
- Advisor now blends `observedGatewayPerM` so consultations reflect real paid cost + fluctuation.

### Gateway CRUD (API + MCP)
- `list / get / create / update / delete` — `ai_gateway_*` tools + `/api/ai-gateway-admin/*`. Update sends the full merged config so a PUT never resets unspecified settings.
- Verified: list=20, get, update-preserves-config, create errors correctly at the account's 20-gateway max.
