author: weepwood
body:
## 目标

将正式前端构建产物写入 Spring Boot 可执行 JAR，使前端、后端、产品版本和 Git Commit 成为同一个业务制品；Nginx 继续承担统一入口、维护模式、访问审计、文档和代理能力。

本 PR 实施第一阶段双模式兼容：默认使用 JAR 内嵌前端，同时保留发布包中的 `frontend/` 目录作为紧急回退。

## 构建与发布

- 新增受测工具 `scripts/embed_frontend_in_jar.py`；
- 工具会重写 JAR，删除仓库中残留的旧 `BOOT-INF/classes/static/**`，原子写入本次 Vite 产物，避免同名 ZIP 条目和过期哈希资源；
- 保留后端类、配置、Manifest、嵌套依赖的原始 ZIP 元数据和压缩方式；
- Windows 发布工作流在组装离线包前再次验证：
  - `BOOT-INF/classes/static/index.html` 仅存在一份；
  - `BOOT-INF/classes/static/assets/**` 非空；
- 外置 `frontend/` 暂时继续打包，供第一阶段回退；
- Docker 在 Maven 打包前清空旧 static 目录并复制本次 Vite 产物，Nginx 容器调整为网关和文档服务。

## 后端静态资源与 SPA

- 提取 `SpaPathResourceResolver`，真实静态资源优先；
- Vue History 路由回退到 `index.html`；
- `/api/**`、Actuator、Swagger、OpenAPI、文档和带扩展名的缺失资源保持真实 404，不会错误返回 HTML；
- 增加单元测试覆盖资源命中、SPA 回退和保留路径边界。

## Windows 运维

- Nginx 默认将主页面代理到 Spring Boot JAR；
- 保留 80 端口、维护模式、入口审计日志、文档、API 和 Swagger 路由；
- 新增 `frontend-mode.inc` 双模式配置：
  - `embedded`：JAR 内嵌前端；
  - `external`：`current/frontend` 外置回退；
- `mrrctl.ps1 frontend embedded|external` 可安全切换，切换前检查资源，切换后执行 `nginx -t`，失败自动恢复；
- 新发布包部署时强制验证内嵌前端；
- 回滚到尚未内嵌前端的旧受管理版本时，先切换 `external` 后仍可回滚；
- `status` 和 `doctor` 展示并校验当前前端模式；
- 一键管理中心增加前端模式状态和两个切换按钮；
- 新安装默认使用内嵌模式；
- `migrate-embedded-frontend.ps1` 会先验证当前 JAR，再备份和迁移现有 Nginx 配置，不修改数据库、密钥、OSS 或图片配置。

## 缓存策略

- 页面入口与 Vue 路由：`Cache-Control: no-cache`；
- `/assets/`、`/browser_upgrade/`：一年不可变缓存；
- Nginx 对 Spring Boot 返回的静态文件继续动态 gzip；
- API 不套用前端缓存策略。

## 不包含的变更

- 不删除 Nginx；
- 不把病案图片、OSS 文件、配置或密钥写入 JAR；
- VitePress 用户文档和内部文档仍保持外置；
- 第一阶段不删除外置前端回退目录。

## 已完成验证

在包含最新 `main` 运维诊断中心代码的 PR 合并结果上，以下检查已通过：

- Windows PowerShell 5.1 语法解析、UTF-8/BOM 编码约束和管理中心自检；
- Python 发布与 JAR 嵌入工具测试；
- 后端 PostgreSQL 16 完整单元和集成测试；
- 前端类型检查、变更文件 Lint、正式构建、单元测试和 Chromium E2E；
- Windows 正式构建的“前端构建并写入 JAR”步骤；
- 最终离线包组装、JAR 二次验证和制品上传；
- 发布基线验证。

首轮构建发现后端源码中已有旧前端静态资源，原实现会拒绝重复写入；现已改为安全重写 JAR，并增加旧资源替换、重复条目和嵌套依赖压缩方式测试。

author: onetwo3d
body:
## Phase 2c periodic full-chain: X-02, X-05, X-07 + X-03 parked (o3d-lgo.7)

Extends `e2e/full-chain/periodic.spec.ts` (which already carried X-01, the batch-mode foundation) with the remaining Phase-2c cross-cutting tests. Every test asserts the journal **read back out of Xero** (POSTED, balanced, exact account/amount), not the IMS's own sync-log row, and registers every posted document for teardown. Verified live green against the Xero Demo tenant on the e2e rig.

### Tests

- **X-05 — MANUFACTURING_JOURNAL + MANUFACTURING_RECLASS** (green). A BOM manufacturing order with a seeded overhead cost line: completion posts `DR inventory (631) / CR overhead (330)` for the capitalised overhead; a post-completion cost-line edit (all output still on hand) posts the reclass `DR 631 / CR 330` for the delta. New harness drivers in `ims.ts` (`createManufacturingOrder`, `addManufacturingCostLine`, `editManufacturingCostLineAmount`, `startProduction`, `completeProduction`, `openManufacturingOrder`). Seeds stock with posting **disarmed** so component adjustments can never queue an untracked journal, then arms sync; captures and **restores the exact prior** `xero_sync_manufacturing_journal` state.

- **X-02 — transit GL reconciliation sweep** (green; closes gate `onetwo3d-ims-6oyu.4.1`). The rig holds no transit balance snapshots, so the transit account has never been swept. `seedTransitReconciliationResidue` crafts a within-tolerance sub-£1 residue (opening/closing `632` snapshots that absorb the live subledger movement) on a **fresh, never-posted reconciliation date** each run, so the daily batch sweeps exactly £0.30 into a POSTED `DAILY_BATCH_TRANSIT_RECONCILIATION` journal (`DR transit 632 / CR rounding 860`), asserted from Xero. `transitReconciliationSwept === +0.30`.

- **X-07 — INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT write-off** (green; on this branch, closes the `e2e/xero.spec.ts:139` fixme). A reason-coded stock write-off posts `DR write-off / CR inventory (631)`. (Built in a prior session; reordered here to seed with posting disarmed.)

- **X-03 — UNREALISED_FX_JOURNAL** — **parked `test.fixme`**, blocked by **bd o3d-lgo.6.1** (P1). The period-end FX revaluation (`lib/accounting-fx-revaluation.ts`) posts its control leg to Xero **SYSTEM** accounts 610/800, which Xero rejects (`"Account code 800 is not a valid code for this document"`) — the same defect PP-08 surfaced live. The fixme names the bug and describes the scenario it would drive once o3d-lgo.6.1 lands.

### Not included: X-04, X-06 (researched, not built — see report/follow-ups)

- **X-06** (stock transfer + landed-cost exclusion): research showed a warehouse transfer posts **no Xero journal at all**; the real gate (`6oyu.19.1`) content is the *retrospective landed-cost revaluation excluding transferred units*, a substantial procure-to-pay fixture. Deferred.
- **X-04** (tax-rate sync/drift): the drift path is detect-only (no Xero writeback) and gated on the rig token's `accounting.settings` scope; needs tax-rate-component seeding + multiple rate-limited cron runs. Deferred.

### Rate-limit note (o3d-lgo.13)

X-01 and X-02 both trigger the `accounting-daily-batch` cron, which production rate-limits to 1/hour/IP (unfixed by design; not weakened here). They must run in **separate invocations** (documented in the spec header) — X-02 detects the 429 and **skips loudly** (never a false pass) when accidentally co-run, and is exercised for real in its own invocation. Codex flags this as a coverage gap; it is the mitigation the task explicitly sanctioned, and the hazard is filed as o3d-lgo.13.

### Verification

Ran `npm run e2e:full-chain -- --grep "X-05:|X-02:"` on the rig repeatedly — **3 passed** each time, `voided N Xero document(s)`, `[quiesce] released.`, `.full-chain-xero-docs.json === []`. X-02 verified across 5 runs on 5 distinct reconciliation dates, confirming its fresh-date design is rerunnable.

### Codex

Adversarial-reviewed over 5 rounds. All correctness findings addressed: failure-safe teardown registration with a loud strand warning (o3d-lgo.7.1 window), exact-prior-value setting restore, fresh-per-run reconciliation date checked against both accounting events and live sync logs, and a fresh pg client per connection retry. The sole remaining item is the X-02 rate-limit skip, justified above.

### Cross-port

N/A — IMS-internal Woo→IMS→Xero e2e, not the Mintsoft/ShipHero sync plugins.

author: rangsimanch
body:
Three related pieces of document-module work: monitoring dashboards, standardized names, and an admin-configurable label system.

## 1. Per-module dashboards (issue-lifecycle family)
RFA-style monitoring header widgets on each List page, on three configurable abstract bases in `app/Filament/Widgets/Documents/` (stats / status doughnut / monthly trend). This PR covers **NCR / NCN / SWN** (shared `HasIssueLifecycle`): per-status counts, doughnut, 6-month trend, plus **Open** / **Overdue** / **High severity**. RFA's own widgets untouched. Follow-up PRs: RFI+RFN, Letter+Daily, Close-Out.

## 2. Standardized module names — "Full Name (ABBR)"
Every document module now follows the RFA format across nav + list/view, on both the admin resources and the App-panel registry: Request for Information (RFI), Request for Inspection (RFN), Non-Conformance Report (NCR), Non-Conformance Notice (NCN), Site Warning Notice (SWN), Letter (LTR), Memorandum (MEMO), Transmittal (TRN), Submittal (SUB), Daily Work Request (DWR), Daily Work Report (DR), Close-Out (CO), Close-Out Inspection (COI), Close-Out Punch List (COP).

## 3. Admin-configurable module labels
The system admin can now rename any module from the UI, no code change (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-configurable-module-labels-design.md`):
- `app_panel_modules.label` (new nullable column) holds the override; `AppModuleService::getLabel()` resolves DB override → registry default → key.
- `HasConfigurableModuleLabel` trait reads it for nav/model labels; wired into all 14 document admin resources (the hardcoded label props from part 2 are removed — the registry default is now the single source). App-panel resources inherit via `extends`, so one edit updates both panels.
- The **App Module Manager** (`/admin/app-module-manager`) gains a per-module display-name field (blank = revert to the standard default); saving persists and clears the resolver cache.

## Testing
- Dashboard: widget registration + seeded overdue/open/per-status counts for NCR/NCN/SWN.
- Labels: resolver fallback/override/blank/unknown-key, trait on resources, and the manager save (persist + revert-on-blank).
- Full suite: **721 passed**.
- Browser-verified: NCR List dashboard renders; sidebar shows the standardized labels; the App Module Manager label editor renders; a DB override makes the sidebar show the custom name, and clearing it reverts to the standard default.

## Next (separate)
Remaining dashboard families (RFI+RFN, Letter+Daily, Close-Out); optionally a unified cross-type dashboard. Deferred on labels: per-locale and per-tenant variants.

## What changed

Added two comprehensive implementation-ready specifications for Crystal Runtime v0.3:

### 1. Runtime-Module-Interfaces.md (1,022 lines)

Formal interface definitions for all 7 runtime modules with complete implementation contracts:

- **Coordinator:** `execute_workflow()`, Task, WorkflowResult, error handling
- **Registry:** `register()`, `query_capability()`, `get_status()`, `heartbeat()`

Complete testing strategy with 104 test cases across 5 testing layers:

**Testing Layers:**
1. Unit tests — Module isolated, mocked dependencies

author: nk94076
body:
## Summary

This PR now contains **two parallel, full-featured implementations** of the same Corium leather-goods storefront + admin CMS:

1. **Next.js 15 edition** (repo root) — TypeScript, Prisma (SQLite), Tailwind CSS v4, Auth.js.
2. **PHP / MySQL edition** (`php-app/`) — vanilla PHP 8 (no framework), MySQL, Tailwind CSS v4 compiled to a static stylesheet (no Node.js needed at runtime). Built for classic shared PHP hosting where Node.js isn't available. See [`php-app/README.md`](./php-app/README.md) for setup and deployment.

The PHP edition has full feature parity with the Next.js version **except the coupon/discount-code system, which is intentionally omitted** (explicit scope for this rewrite).

---

## Next.js edition (repo root)

**Storefront**
- Home, Shop (filters/sort/pagination/grid+list), Category pages, Product detail (gallery zoom, variants, reviews, related products), Cart, Wishlist, Checkout (coupons, addresses, payment method selection), Order confirmation
- Auth: register/login/forgot-password with OTP flow, role-based sessions (Auth.js v5 + bcrypt)
- Account area: overview, orders + tracking timeline, addresses, password change; guest order tracking
- About Us, Contact Us, Privacy Policy, Terms & Conditions, Shipping & Return Policy, FAQ — all CMS-driven, plus a branded 404
- Live search suggestions, mega-menu navigation, sticky header, mobile-first responsive throughout

**Admin panel** (`/admin`, role-gated)
- Dashboard with revenue/orders/products/customers stats and a sales chart
- Full CRUD: Products, Categories, Orders (status + tracking), Customers (read), Reviews (moderate/reply), Coupons
- **Homepage Manager** — announcement bar, hero/promo banner slides, every section's heading/subtitle/visibility, "Why Choose Us" items, Instagram gallery — all editable without touching code
- **Pages CMS** — edit About/Contact/Privacy/Terms/Shipping content + FAQs
- **Settings** — branding, live-editable theme colors, social links, SEO/analytics IDs, payment/shipping/tax config, currency, SMTP
- **Media Manager** — real file uploads tracked in a database-backed library
- Admin mutations call `revalidatePath` so edits appear on the storefront immediately

**SEO / performance**
- Per-page metadata, canonical URLs, Open Graph, JSON-LD (Organization, Product, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage)
- Dynamic `sitemap.xml` / `robots.txt` generated from live data
- Self-contained deterministic SVG placeholder image system (`/api/placeholder`) — no third-party image CDN, so there are no broken images regardless of network policy
- 50 statically generated product pages + 10 category pages at build time

**Data**
- Prisma schema covering products/variants/images, categories, orders/items, addresses, reviews, coupons, wishlist/cart, homepage sections, CMS pages, FAQs, settings, media assets
- Seed script generates realistic, original demo content (no Lorem Ipsum): 10 categories, 50 products, reviews, 8 customers + 1 admin, 18 orders, 4 coupons, banners, FAQs, policy/about/contact copy

### Deploying
`DEPLOYMENT.md` covers Hostinger/Passenger-style Node hosting; a plain VPS just needs `npm run build && npm start`.

---

## PHP / MySQL edition (`php-app/`)

A ground-up rewrite requested to run on hosts with no Node.js — vanilla PHP front-controller routing (clean URLs via `.htaccess`/regex router, no `.php` in any URL), PDO/MySQL, session-based auth and guest cart, and the exact same brand design system recompiled as a static Tailwind CSS build.

**Storefront** — Home, Shop, Category, Product detail (gallery/zoom, colour picker, reviews with write-a-review), Cart, Wishlist, Checkout (address book, 5 payment methods with live fee recalculation, order placement with stock decrement), order confirmation, full Account area (overview, orders + cancel + tracking timeline, addresses CRUD, password change), guest order tracking, About/Contact(w/ working form)/Privacy/Terms/Shipping (CMS-driven)/FAQ (accordion), branded 404/403.

**Admin panel** (`/admin`, role-gated) — Dashboard (stat cards, 30-day sales bar chart, top products, latest orders), Products CRUD (real multi-image upload + placeholder generation, colour picker, SEO fields), Categories CRUD (image/banner upload, delete-protection when in use), Orders (status filter, status/tracking updates that append to the tracking timeline), Customers (list + detail with orders/wishlist/addresses), Reviews (approve/reject/reply/delete, with `avg_rating`/`review_count` recomputed from approved reviews), Homepage Manager (announcement bar, banner slides, every section's title/subtitle/visibility, Why Choose Us, Instagram gallery), Pages CMS (About/Contact/legal page editors + full FAQ manager), Media Manager (upload/copy-URL/delete), Settings (general/theme colors/social/SEO/payment/shipping/tax/currency/SMTP).

**SEO** — per-page meta/canonical/OG tags, site-wide Organization JSON-LD plus Product and FAQPage JSON-LD, dynamic `sitemap.xml` (71 URLs from live data) and `robots.txt`.

**Data** — MySQL schema (18 tables, intentionally no `coupons` table) + a CLI seed script that's a faithful PHP port of the Next.js seed data (same 10 categories, 50 products, reviews, customers, 18 orders, banners, homepage sections, CMS pages, FAQs, settings, media assets).

### Setup / Deploying
See [`php-app/README.md`](./php-app/README.md) — local dev with PHP's built-in server, and shared-hosting deployment (point document root at `php-app/public`, import the schema, run the seed script, ensure `public/uploads/` is writable).

## Test plan

**Next.js edition**
- [x] `npm run build` — clean production build, no type/lint errors
- [x] `npm run lint` — no warnings
- [x] End-to-end manual flow verified: register/login → browse → add to cart → apply coupon → checkout → address → place order → confirmation → order appears in account with tracking timeline (real DB writes, stock decrement, coupon usage tracking all confirmed)
- [x] Admin flow verified: login as admin → dashboard renders real stats/chart → create/edit product → homepage manager edit reflects on storefront immediately → media upload works
- [x] Responsive checked at desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px) viewports across home, shop, product, cart, account, admin
- [x] `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` verified to render real data

**PHP edition**
- [x] `php -l` clean across every `.php` file in `php-app/`
- [x] End-to-end manual flow verified (curl + real DB assertions): register → login → browse → add to cart → checkout (all 5 payment methods, live fee recalculation) → place order → stock decremented → order appears in account with tracking timeline → cancel order → guest order tracking by order number + email
- [x] Password reset OTP flow verified end-to-end (request → demo OTP shown → reset → login with new password)
- [x] Admin flow verified for every section: product/category create+edit+delete with real image upload and placeholder generation, order status updates, review moderation with rating recomputation, homepage manager (all 6 form types), FAQ CRUD, CMS page content save, media upload/delete, settings save
- [x] Access control verified: unauthenticated → redirected to login; authenticated non-admin → 403
- [x] Responsive checked at desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px) across home, shop, and product detail
- [x] Playwright crawl across 17 representative pages — zero console errors, zero 5xx responses

### Demo credentials (both editions)
- Admin: `admin@corium-leather.com` / `Admin@12345`
- Customer: `aarav.mehta@example.com` / `Customer@123`

### Known scope notes
- No live payment gateway is wired up in either edition (payment methods are selectable with correct fee/GST logic; swap in a real gateway server-side before production)
- Password-reset OTP is surfaced in the UI since no SMTP is configured in this environment
- Next.js edition uses SQLite for zero-setup local dev (provider-agnostic Prisma schema, ready for Postgres/MySQL in production); the PHP edition uses MySQL di

author: rfiorentino1
body:
## Problem

When a server drops (restart, network blip, ping timeout), the client showed a "connection lost" dialog and booted you to the server list — it never actually reconnected, even with the *Auto-reconnect* preference on. The auto-reconnect machinery existed but never worked, due to a few ordering bugs where state was wiped right before it was needed.

## Fixes

- **`startReconnectTimerLocked()` called `cancelReconnectLocked()`**, which nulled the `reconnectRecord`/`reconnectPassword` the caller had just set — so the first retry bailed at its guard and booted the user instead of retrying. Now it cancels only the timer.
- **Only the idle `CON_LOST` path honored the preference.** A server-restart logout (`MYSELF_LOGGEDOUT`) and drops caught in the command-completion loop booted unconditionally. All three now route through one `handleServerDropLocked()` that honors `autoReconnect`. (Safe: the app never calls `TT_DoLogout`, and a kick/ban is `MYSELF_KICKED`, handled elsewhere — so `MYSELF_LOGGEDOUT` can only mean the server dropped us.)
- **`attemptReconnectLocked()` read the rejoin target *after* `cancelReconnectLocked()` had cleared it**, so every reconnect landed in the root channel. The target is now snapshotted before cancelling.

## Rejoin by path

Rejoin now keys on the channel **path** (resolved via `TT_GetChannelIDFromPath`) instead of the numeric channel ID, so it survives a full server restart that reassigns IDs — and preserves the channel password across the drop. Retries every 5s until the server returns, then rejoins the exact channel you were in.

Adds reconnect diagnostics to the audio log (`Connection drop …`, `Reconnect attempt …`, `Reconnect: rejoining channel by path …`).

## Testing

Verified live against a real server restart: `CON_LOST` → retry loop → `rejoining channel by path /Lounge/` → reconnected into the same channel, no dialog.

body: A user prompt starting with "-" reached `rekal recall` as a bare `--query <prompt>` arg, which argparse mistook for a flag and rejected, so that turn's recall silently returned nothing. Pass it as one `--query=<prompt>` token, which argparse accepts regardless of leading dash.

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

Some data warehouse import tables repeatedly OOM-kill their sync pods (surfaced as the `dwh_pod_heartbeat_timeout` event). After the in-place auto-repartition controller shipped it handled the bulk of these, but a long tail remained, from three distinct mechanisms:

- **Perpetual repartition loop.** A table whose in-place rewrite keeps failing never converges. `MAX_REPARTITION_ATTEMPTS` only bounds attempts against a *single* pending target, but pre-extraction detection re-arms a fresh target every sync, and the cooldown only engages after a *successful* repartition. So a permanently-failing table re-attempts a full-table rewrite on every sync, indefinitely.
- **Unpartitioned first load.** The partition auto-detect only recognizes an incrementing integer key or a `created_at`/`inserted_at`/`createdAt` column. A table whose timestamp is named differently (e.g. `received_at`, a report `date`) or whose only key is a string/UUID falls through to no partitioning and loads the whole table into the delta-merge working set — OOMing on its first load, which repartition can't rescue (there's no delta table yet to rewrite).
- **Date-only tables stuck at the finest tier.** A datetime key with no time-of-day (e.g. an ad-platform report `date`) caps at the `day` tier. If a single day still exceeds the partition budget, the controller parks it at "finest tier" while it keeps OOMing.

## Changes

- **Repartition circuit breaker.** Adds a cumulative `repartition_failure_count` (survives the per-target re-flag) and, once it crosses a threshold, `reset_repartition_state()` clears the pending/swap/claim markers and parks the table with a timed backoff. Detection skips a parked table until the backoff elapses, then clears the marker and allows one fresh cycle — so a table fixed out-of-band (data shrank, or a finer scheme became available) recovers without operator action.
- **Generic initial-load partition fallback.** When the built-in auto-detect finds no mode, fall back to (a) the schema's incremental timestamp field as a datetime key when present, else (b) md5 over the primary keys, with a bucket count sized from the source's estimated row count and the first batch's per-row bytes. Any table with a primary key is now partitioned on its first load. `select_repartition_target` likewise returns a concrete md5/datetime scheme instead of relying on rewrite-time auto-detect (which couldn't size md5 and failed on a string-only key).
- **Composite `datetime_md5` partition mode.** A date-only table stuck at its finest datetime tier escalates to a composite scheme — a date bucket split into md5 sub-buckets over the primary keys (partition value `YYYY-MM-DD_<bucket>`). This keeps date locality (incremental merges still touch only recent dates, so the fix doesn't reintroduce the whole-table read) while bounding each partition's size. Used only when the primary key has within-date cardinality; otherwise the table stays parked for the circuit breaker to handle.

No schema migration — the new repartition state lives in the existing `sync_type_config` JSON.

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests only (no manual or production run). Added and ran locally against Python 3.13 + Postgres:

- `test_repartition_controller.py` (full file green): circuit-breaker abandonment once the cumulative failure threshold is crossed, backoff gating plus auto-recovery of detection after the backoff elapses, the `is_repartition_backing_off` fail-safe branches (missing/unparseable `retry_after` treated as still-parked), and the failure counter resetting on a completed rewrite.
- `test_pipeline_utils.py`: the incremental-field-datetime and md5-over-PK fallbacks exercised through `setup_partitioning`, the source-size-based md5 bucket-count estimate, and the `datetime_md5` composite key builder (same date → same prefix, deterministic sub-bucket, sub-bucket in range).
- `test_repartition.py::TestSelectRepartitionTarget`: finest-tier → `datetime_md5` escalation, staying parked when the primary key can't split a date, sub-bucket growth for an over-budget composite table, and the concrete-md5 fallback for unpartitioned-with-keys.

Each group targets a regression the existing suite didn't cover: cumulative-vs-per-target failure counting; timestamp-named or string-PK tables going unpartitioned; and the finest-tier park. Two existing detection tests that asserted the old `mode=None` auto-detect target were updated to the new concrete-target behavior.

- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

author: sukrish3637d
body:
## Summary

Adds a two-layer noise suppression pipeline (WebRTC + RNNoise WASM) and real-time
microphone quality monitoring (muted / low volume detection) to the teacher recording
flow. Both features sit upstream of the Whisper transcription pipeline, since audio
quality directly affects transcript accuracy and downstream AI-generated question quality.

## Why

- Background noise and inaudible audio corrupt Whisper transcripts, which degrades
  auto-generated question quality.
- Teachers previously had no feedback if their mic was muted or too quiet — the
  problem only surfaced after a bad transcript.

## What's included

### 1. Noise Suppression (WebRTC + RNNoise)

Two-layer pipeline applied to the teacher's mic stream before it reaches
`MediaRecorder` and the transcription service:

- **Layer 1 (WebRTC built-in):** `noiseSuppression: true` on `getUserMedia`.
- **Layer 2 (RNNoise):** ML-based denoising via `@timephy/rnnoise-wasm`, running
  in an `AudioWorkletNode` (~10–20ms added latency).
  **Key design decisions:**
- AudioContext is forced to 48kHz, matching RNNoise's training rate and 480-sample
  (10ms) frame size. Verified this doesn't break `AudioQualityDetector` (sample-rate
  agnostic RMS/ZCR), `MediaRecorder`/Opus (native 48kHz), or `convertWebMToWav`
  (decodes into its own 16kHz context for Whisper).
- WASM bundle (1.88MB) is pre-warmed into HTTP cache via `preloadNoiseSuppressor()`
  fired on page mount, so first-recording latency is ~50ms instead of up to ~10s
  on slow connections.
- Graceful fallback: if `AudioWorklet`/WASM fails to load, `applyNoiseSuppression()`
  returns the raw stream with `method: 'webrtc-only'` — recording is never blocked.
- `rawStreamRef` tracks the original `getUserMedia` stream separately from the
  synthetic clean stream, so `stopRecording()` correctly releases the OS-level mic
  indicator (previously a bug risk, since stopping tracks on the AudioContext
  destination stream has no effect on the OS mic light).

### 2. Audio Quality Detection (mute / low volume)

`createAudioQualityDetector()` polls an `AnalyserNode` every 300ms and shows an
advisory warning in the UI when:

| State | Condition | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `muted` | RMS < 0.002 sustained ≥ 4s (debounced to ignore normal pauses) | ✅ Working |
| `low_volume` | RMS < 0.015 | ✅ Working |
| `noisy` | ZCR > 0.25 | ⚠️ Implemented, unreliable — see Known Issues |

State transitions are edge-triggered (`onIssue`/`onClear` fire once per transition,
not repeatedly).

## Testing

- Unit tests for both services covering happy path, fallback behavior, and resource
  cleanup (see `noiseSuppressionService.test.js`, `audioQualityDetector.test.js`).
- Manual testing in-browser: confirmed `rnnoise` method activates correctly (vs.
  `webrtc-only` fallback), confirmed mic indicator releases on stop, confirmed
  recording continues uninterrupted across multiple sessions in the same page load.
- Manual testing with loud background speech present: transcript held up cleanly,
  no degradation observed.

## Known issues / follow-ups (not blocking, tracked separately)

- **`noisy` (ZCR) detection is unreliable in practice** — produces false positives
  on speech and false negatives on low-frequency rumble. Only `muted` and
  `low_volume` (RMS-based) are considered production-ready; `noisy` should be
  revisited or removed in a follow-up.
- **`AudioQualityDetector` may need threshold retuning post-RNNoise** — observed
  the low-volume warning firing more often than expected during natural pauses in
  live testing. Worth confirming which stream (`raw` vs `clean`) it should read
  from and whether `volumeThreshold`/`muteThreshold` need adjusting for the
  post-suppression signal.
- Unrelated to this PR: existing WebSocket reconnect warnings on page load and a
  missing MiniMax API key in local dev were observed during testing — noted here
  for visibility but out of scope for this change.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `frontend/src/services/noiseSuppressionService.js` | New |
| `frontend/src/services/audioQualityDetector.js` | New |
| `frontend/src/pages/RoomDetailPage.jsx` | Modified — preload/apply/dispose wiring, `rawStreamRef` |
| `frontend/package.json` | Added `@timephy/rnnoise-wasm` |
| `frontend/src/__tests__/noiseSuppressionService.test.js` | New |
| `frontend/src/__tests__/audioQualityDetector.test.js` | New |

author: davidalvarezr
body:
Adds a CSV import flow to the admin dashboard: upload a `guest1,guest2,code` file, get a server-computed dry-run preview classifying every row as create/skip/error (structural checks, file-internal duplicate names/codes, and comparison against existing invitations), then confirm to apply. Applying runs inside one interactive transaction that creates invitations with nested guests and partner-links couples atomically; a confirm with any error rows is rejected outright. Re-importing the same file is a safe no-op — existing rows classify as skips.

One endpoint (`POST /api/admin/invitations/import`) serves both phases with a `dryRun` flag, so the preview and the apply can never disagree on classification. The Go admin side parses the CSV itself (`encoding/csv`, header + BOM validation) and guards the confirm with a SHA-256 token over the parsed rows, so a stale preview can't apply changed data.

Also adds `scripts/export-guests-to-csv.ts` (writes the real, gitignored `prisma/invitee-list.csv` from `prisma/guests-data.ts`) and a fake-data example CSV in `docs/`. All committed fixtures use fake names and fixed fake UUIDs. Verified end-to-end against a scratch database: preview → confirm → idempotent re-import → error CSV with no confirm button.

author: issif
body:
## Summary

Kubernetes Events created by the `k8sevents` notifier were not showing up in the ArgoCD "Events" tab, even though they were visible via `kubectl get events`. ArgoCD requires `InvolvedObject.uid` (in addition to `name` and `namespace`) to associate an Event with a resource, and `k8sevents` never set this field.

## Changes

- `notifiers/k8sevents/k8sevents.go`:
  - Look up the involved Pod via `client.GetPod(podName, namespace)` before building the `corev1.Event`.
  - Set `InvolvedObject.UID` from the fetched Pod's `UID`.
  - If the Pod can no longer be found (e.g. already deleted), the Event is still created without a UID, preserving the previous behavior instead of failing the notification.

## Why

Fixes #769. ArgoCD needs `InvolvedObject.name`, `InvolvedObject.namespace` and `InvolvedObject.uid` to list events for a resource in its UI. Without the UID, events created by falco-talon exist in the cluster but are invisible in ArgoCD's Events tab.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./notifiers/k8sevents/...`
- [x] `go test ./notifiers/k8sevents/...`
- [ ] Manual verification: trigger a Falco rule with a `k8sevents` notifier action and confirm the resulting Event now shows up in ArgoCD's Events tab for the involved Pod.

body:
## Summary

Rebuilds Toilet Map v2 as a canonical, provenance-aware data platform while preserving the existing Streamlit/SQLite application and the legacy v2 API identifiers.

## Data model and publication

- adds long-lived `facilities` independent of dataset versions
- stores provider observations in `source_records`
- records explicit `pending` / `matched` / `rejected` decisions in `facility_source_links`
- generates immutable `published_place_snapshots`
- serves the public v2 API from snapshots by default
- preserves legacy place IDs and supports temporary rollback with `PUBLIC_READ_MODEL=places`
- revalidates facility/source links inside the publication transaction
- keeps the previously published dataset active when publication validation fails

## Migrations and operations

- replaces monolithic schema reapplication with ordered, checksummed SQL migrations
- serializes migration execution with a PostgreSQL advisory lock
- retains `schema.sql` as a thin `psql` bootstrap over the same migrations
- adds migration status and expanded data-quality reporting
- upgrades the job queue with idempotency keys, leases, heartbeats, retry waits, dependencies, cancellation, error details and execution statistics

## Ingestion and entity resolution

- separates provider discovery, normalization and provenance
- adds bounded OpenStreetMap ingestion for Kumagaya, Gyoda and Fukaya
- persists OSM observations without silently merging facilities
- automatically reuses only exact prior `provider + external_id` decisions
- generates name/address/distance candidates for administrator review
- adds administrator actions for match, new facility and reject
- adds a `/admin` data-resolution interface

## Scores, trust and reports

- separates dimension observations from facility-level score aggregates
- supports cleanliness, odor, congestion, freshness, equipment, accessibility and child-friendliness
- exposes score calculation basis and source count
- calculates source trust from confidence, verification and freshness
- adds public filters for trust, wheelchair access, changing tables, fees, 24-hour access and current-location radius
- adds current-location map display and external navigation
- accepts closure, fault, wrong-location, accessibility and cleanliness reports
- stores reports as `user_submission` source records pending administrator review

## Compatibility fixes

- resolves the Folium/streamlit-folium dependency conflict
- preserves the legacy SQLite API integrity hook
- preserves tolerant direct-script CLI behavior while making package execution reject invalid limits
- fixes conditional imports in snapshot integrity checks
- adds atomic snapshot rebuild regression coverage

## Security and documentation follow-up

- upgrades the v2 frontend from Next.js `15.4.2` to maintenance-LTS security release `15.5.21`
- adds weekly Dependabot monitoring for `/v2/frontend`
- updates `README.md` and `README.en.md` for the v1/v2 transition, local validation, rollout and rollback
- replaces stale `AGENTS.md` guidance with the current v2 data model, migration, job queue, compatibility and verification rules

## Verification

### V2 CI

- Ruff: passed
- backend pytest: passed
- migrations applied twice: passed
- `psql` bootstrap applied twice: passed
- PostgreSQL/PostGIS legacy import: passed
- post-validation publication guard: passed
- snapshot, trust and dimensional-score assertions: passed
- FastAPI smoke test: passed
- frontend dependency installation on Next.js `15.5.21`: passed
- frontend typecheck: passed
- frontend production build: passed
- Docker Compose config/build: passed
- clean-start Compose migration/import/API/UI smoke: passed

### Existing application CI

- Ruff: passed
- mypy on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: passed
- pytest and data verification on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: passed
- Streamlit smoke test: passed
- root Docker build: passed

## Rollout notes

Production database migration and live Overpass ingestion are intentionally not performed by this PR. Apply the migrations in Preview first, compare compatibility rows with snapshots, run data quality, then perform the production cutover using the documented rollback switch.

## O que muda
- **`core/telemetry.py` (novo):** constantes do schema comum v1 congelado ([docs/schema.md](https://github.com/CidLucas/ops-centro/blob/main/docs/schema.md)) — sem strings soltas; span pai `agent_execution` (agent_name, model, tokens_input/output, session_id, `tenant_id` **por request**); `InstrumentedMCPToolExecutor` — todo tool call dos graphs passa por `execute()` e vira span filho `mcp_tool_call` (tool_name, mcp_server, tenant_id, status a partir do `ToolResult`).

Spans são emitidos pelo `BatchSpanProcessor` da lib (assíncrono, batch); sem OTLP configurado o tracer é no-op. Nada síncrono no caminho quente.

Uma execução em dev gera no Tempo 1 trace com `agent_execution` pai e N `mcp_tool_call` filhos, todos com os atributos comuns — validável com `{ resource.app_name != nil }` + `name = \"agent_execution\"`.

- 면접 초기 질문 PRD 신규 작성 (`docs/prd/interview.md`)
- 디스패치 metadata(sessionId, interviewType, position, resumeContext) 파싱 및 부재·오류 시 폴백 (#95)
- 검수된 질문 목록(유형별 2개, 총 8문항)에서 LLM이 **질문 번호만** 선택하고, 발화는 코드가 고정 인사말 + 목록 원문으로 조립(`session.say`) (#96) — few-shot 스타일 생성은 예시를 어중간하게 섞은 질문이 나와 폐기. 번호 파싱 실패·범위 밖·LLM 호출 실패는 목록 내 랜덤 폴백으로, 목록 밖 질문·요약 주입의 발화 유입을 구조적으로 차단
- 페르소나·음성 제약·신입 전제 시스템 프롬프트, candidate 입장 후 첫 질문 발화(`wait_for_participant`), Spring 연동 전 픽스처 환경 변수(`KKORI_POSITION_FIXTURE`·`KKORI_RESUME_CONTEXT_FIXTURE`), 텍스트 검증용 미리보기 스크립트(`agent/scripts/preview_initial_question.py`)
- 초기 질문 생성 테스트 (#97): 파싱·프롬프트 조립·선택 폴백 단위 테스트 22개 + LLM 스모크 2개(`KKORI_LIVE_LLM=1` 명시 시에만 실호출, 기본 skip), agent CI의 "수집된 테스트 없음(exit 5) 통과 처리" 제거
- 질문 로직을 `src/interview/` 서브패키지로 정리 (worker의 도메인 구조 관례와 일치)

## 관련 이슈

Closes #95
Closes #96
Closes #97

## 실행 검증

- import 검증: `cd agent && uv run python -c "import src.main"` 통과
- 테스트: `cd agent && uv run pytest` — 22 passed, 2 skipped(LLM 스모크는 기본 skip) / `KKORI_LIVE_LLM=1` 명시 시 스모크 2개 통과(선택 결과 목록 **정확 일치** 검증)
- 파싱·프롬프트 조립·폴백 검증: metadata 정상/부재/비JSON/비객체 폴백, `{position}` 치환·제외, 번호 파싱(유효/무효/범위 밖), 목록 밖 출력·LLM 실패 시 목록 내 랜덤 폴백(스텁 LLM으로 재현)
- 선택 미리보기(`scripts/preview_initial_question.py`): 선택 분포를 집계 출력 — 다양성은 확률적 특성상 자동 게이트 대신 수동 관찰
- 콘솔 음성 테스트(`uv run python -m src.main console`): 픽스처 주입 상태에서 초기 질문 발화 확인

| Before | After |
| ------ | ----- |
| (부트스트랩) 음성 연결 확인용 고정 인사 — "사용자에게 인사하고 음성이 잘 들리는지 확인" | "안녕하세요, 만나서 반갑습니다. 편하게 답변해 주시면 됩니다. 백엔드 쪽으로 진로를 정하게 된 이유가 있을까요?" (고정 인사말 + 목록 원문) |
| (개발 중 few-shot 안) "백엔드 관련해서 공부하거나 경험해 오신 것들을 간단히 소개해 주시겠어요?" — 예시를 어중간하게 섞은 질문 | "지금까지 했던 프로젝트 중에 가장 기억에 남는 경험을 하나 소개해 주시겠어요?" (목록 원문 그대로 — LLM은 번호만 선택) |

## 관련 PRD

- `docs/prd/interview.md` §1(세션 컨텍스트 주입), §2(초기 질문 생성) — 본 PR에서 신규 작성

## 완료 조건

- [x] metadata의 position·resumeContext가 초기 질문 지시에 반영된다
- [x] metadata 부재·파싱 실패 시 크래시 없이 기본 질문 목록으로 폴백하고 경고 로그를 남긴다(픽스처는 metadata가 아예 없을 때만 적용)
- [x] position이 있으면 `{position}` 문장이 치환되어 목록에 포함되고, 없으면 목록에서 제외된다
- [x] 발화된 질문이 목록 원문과 **정확히 일치**한다(발화는 코드 조립 — 목록 밖 질문·요약 유입 구조적 차단)
- [x] LLM 출력이 유효한 번호가 아니어도(파싱 실패·범위 밖·호출 실패) 목록 내 질문으로 폴백한다
- [x] 발화가 plain text·구어체·한국어다(목록 검수로 보장)
- 선택 분포(특정 질문 고착 여부)는 확률적 특성상 자동 게이트 대신 미리보기 스크립트로 수동 관찰

## 리뷰어에게

- 질문 생성 방식은 few-shot 스타일 생성이 아니라 **검수 목록 선택**입니다. 실출력에서 예시들을 어중간하게 섞은 저품질 질문이 나와, LLM은 이력서 요약을 참고해 목록에서 **질문 번호만** 출력하고 발화는 코드가 고정 인사말 + 목록 원문으로 조립합니다(`session.say`). 번호 파싱 실패·범위 밖·호출 실패는 목록 내 랜덤 폴백이라, 목록 밖 질문·요약 내용(프롬프트 주입 포함)이 발화에 유입될 경로가 없습니다.
- 엔트리포인트 순서는 **참가자 입장 확인(룸 자동 연결) → 질문 선택 → 세션 시작 → 발화**입니다 — 참가자가 입장하지 않으면 유료 선택 호출이 발생하지 않고, LLM 지연이 룸 연결을 막지 않으며, 선택 LLM 호출 동안 자동 턴 응답과 초기 질문이 경쟁하지 않습니다.
- position은 Spring 직무 enum(현재 `BACKEND`·`FRONTEND`)에서 선택된 값입니다. agent가 **코드→표시명 매핑**으로 변환해 발화에는 매핑된 표시명만 쓰고, 미등록 값은 직무 미지정으로 폴백합니다(임의 문자열의 발화 유입 차단). 파싱 실패 로그에는 LLM 출력·이력서 원문을 남기지 않습니다.
- 개발 픽스처는 metadata가 아예 없을 때만 적용되고, LLM 스모크 테스트는 `KKORI_LIVE_LLM=1` 명시 시에만 실호출합니다. 선택 다양성은 확률적 특성상 자동 게이트 대신 미리보기 스크립트로 수동 관찰합니다.
- 모델은 LiveKit Inference `gpt-4.1-mini` 유지(LiveKit 크레딧, 별도 키 불필요). Claude/Bedrock 전환은 본론 질문 스토리에서 Orchestrator 구조화 출력(tool use)과 함께 검토 예정. 프롬프트가 짧아(목록 8문항+요약 몇 줄) 첫 발화 지연 영향은 미미합니다.

## 남긴 논의 / 후속 과제

- metadata 계약 중 `interviewType`(`THIRTY_MIN`·`FIVE_MIN`)과 `position`(`BACKEND`·`FRONTEND`)은 Spring enum으로 확정 — 전체 필드 구성·전달 방식의 최종 합의는 세션 생성 스토리에서 **[미확정]**
- 이력서 요약 출처는 Spring이 `resumes.structured_data`에서 코드 조립하는 방향으로만 기록 — 세션 생성 스토리에서 확정
- 이력서 세부 경험의 질문 반영·RAG는 본론 질문 스토리 범위
- 요약 없음 폴백에서 자기소개형 고착 경향 관찰됨 — 운영 중 고착이 심하면 목록 순서 셔플로 완화

author: ogoffart
body:
The //#sls citations were added too liberally: many sat on tests that merely contain the construct without testing the cited paragraph.

Keep a citation only when the test really covers the paragraph: a structural paragraph needs a test exhibiting that structure, and a shall-clause needs its violation tested. The traceability matrix now honestly reports the pruned paragraphs as uncovered.

Removed citations, and why:

- inheritance.slint, file.component.inherits: the test checks that a user-defined base is rejected in SC mode; no test resolves an unknown base name.

- component_declaration.slint, export.default-private: visibility to importers can't be observed because SC has no imports; the tested errors are SC restrictions, not privacy.

- component_declaration.slint, export.declaration-site: nothing there observes that the component was exported. The runtime case component/empty.slint keeps its citation: Empty::new() in the Rust snippet observes that the exported name is the component's name.

- component_declaration.slint, file.component.definition-forms, and case component/empty.slint: only the inherits form appears; the form without a base never does (an SC component must inherit Window).

- component_declaration.slint, export.no-duplicates: the tested error is "multiple exported components", not a duplicated name. The normalization-collision test doesn't carry it either: it duplicates a name only after normalization, never literally.

- identifiers.slint, lex.identifier.classes, lex.identifier.normalization, lex.contextual-keywords: a component named My_Test_Component exercises no character-class boundary, no normalization pair, and no keyword used as an identifier.

- export_specifiers.slint, export.forms, export.list, export.rename: SC rejects export lists outright, so the paragraphs describing how lists work aren't tested. left-must-exist stays: the "'DoesNotExist' not found" error is the violation of that clause.

- elements.slint, the four element-structure paragraphs: that test is about SC rejecting builtin elements and properties; element_nesting.slint covers the structure.

- element_nesting.slint, file.element.instantiation-typename: only resolvable type names appear; no test uses an unknown element type.

- source_file.slint, source.file-extension, file.component.name, file.component.body-braces, export.placement: the file contains only the boilerplate every test shares; nothing targets these rules.

- whitespace.slint, lex.tokens: definitional, any compiling file demonstrates it. source.whitespace.chars: the file contains no tab, so the whitespace character set isn't fully exercised.

- case component/background_color.slint, expr.color.forms: the 4-digit form and case-insensitivity are missing; the syntax test color_literals.slint covers all the forms.

Also move the surviving citations from the top of the file next to the line that tests them, when they don't describe a whole-file property.

author: fernandezc
body:
## Summary
- keep the public NMR 1D processing example executable end to end after the recent 1D stabilization work
- add targeted tests showing that the processed TopSpin 1D ppm axis stays linear and preserves common metadata
- document the current sliced-axis linearity limitation in tests instead of letting the public example fail on it

## Why
The scientific-validation work fixed the public 1D pipeline itself, but the example still hit two follow-up problems:
- peak picking on a sliced ppm region could fail because the current core `Coord` machinery may lose the `linear` flag after slicing even when the sub-axis remains scientifically regular
- the peak annotation path assumed quantity-like `.values.m` access, which is not true for the scalar returned here

This PR keeps the example usable without widening scope to a broader core coordinate refactor.

## Validation
- `python3 -m py_compile plugins/spectrochempy-nmr/examples/processing/nmr/plot_processing_nmr.py plugins/spectrochempy-nmr/tests/test_experiment.py`
- `pytest plugins/spectrochempy-nmr/tests/test_experiment.py -k 'processed_topspin_axis_stays_linear or example_style_slice_remains_monotonic or Public1DMathConventions or Public1DRealAxisValidation'`
- `MPLBACKEND=Agg .../python plugins/spectrochempy-nmr/examples/processing/nmr/plot_processing_nmr.py` now gets past the previous example/plugin crashes; remaining warnings are environment/core-related

body:
Serves #273.

## Summary

- make `TrackReplaySnapshotCache(context:)` cheap for large replay lists by storing context lazily instead of eagerly encoding every prefix snapshot
- warm full prefix snapshots on a utility task after replay context is applied, with cooperative cancellation and a generation guard before applying the warmed cache
- cancel replay snapshot precompute when replay/static contexts change and when `MapScreen` disappears
- format track timeline date markers with the supplied calendar locale/time zone instead of hard-coded English month labels

## Root Cause

`TrackReplaySnapshotCache` eagerly clipped and encoded every event prefix during replay list open. For 500 visits that produced roughly 125k segment encodes on the main path.

## Verification

- Red measurement before fix: `testTrackReplaySnapshotCacheConstructionStaysInsideLargeReplayListOpenBudget` failed at `3.5202780961990356s` against a `0.025s` budget.
- Focused rerun after fix:
  `./scripts/sim-lock.sh xcodebuild -project ios/App/MakingTracks.xcodeproj -scheme MakingTracks -destination platform=iOS\ Simulator,id=C4A64D49-24A2-4429-B6E2-AD9A14142A99 -derivedDataPath /private/tmp/dd-codex3-wp273 -only-testing:MakingTracksTests/AppShellTests/testTrackReplaySnapshotCacheReturnsEventPrefixes -only-testing:MakingTracksTests/AppShellTests/testTrackReplaySnapshotCachePrecomputedMatchesLazySnapshots -only-testing:MakingTracksTests/AppShellTests/testTrackReplaySnapshotCachePrecomputeStopsWhenCancelled -only-testing:MakingTracksTests/AppShellTests/testTrackReplaySnapshotCacheConstructionStaysInsideLargeReplayListOpenBudget -only-testing:MakingTracksTests/AppShellTests/testTrackTimelineDateMarkerLabelsUseCalendarLocale test`
- Focused result: `5 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped`.
- Cache budget case passed in `0.004s`; precomputed parity in `0.004s`; cancellation in `0.001s`; locale marker in `0.008s`.
- Teeth proof: temporarily neutering the cancellation guard made `testTrackReplaySnapshotCachePrecomputeStopsWhenCancelled` fail with the expected `XCTAssertNil` failure; restoring the guard returned the focused set to green.
- First full release gate on `5f6447b` exposed one real existing-test locale expectation mismatch: `testTrackTimelinePositionsAreVisitEventsNotElapsedTime` expected English labels while the formatter now honors the supplied calendar locale. Fixed by giving that test an explicit `en_GB` Gregorian UTC calendar, then focused-reran the timeline locale/position tests green.
- After `origin/ios` advanced to include #422, merged latest base cleanly and pushed refreshed PR head `c1fcb6c4322d79142c177ada5dc5f762e3816a55`.
- Final full iOS release gate on refreshed head:
  `./scripts/sim-lock.sh ./scripts/release-gate.sh`
- Final xcresult summary before cleanup: `218 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped`, device `agent-ios-tests` / iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2.
- `git diff --check`

## Review

- Adversarial review findings raised: 4
- Survived/fixed: 3
- Fixed: removed out-of-scope ledger doc diff from this PR, re-grounded on latest `origin/ios`, renamed stale prefix test, added precomputed parity/cancellation tests, added cooperative cancellation/generation guard/onDisappear cancellation.
- Rejected as non-blocking: no direct SwiftUI async handoff test; behavior is covered through the cancelable cache seam, generation-guard code review, and the full app gate.
- Sourcery review: commented with no requested changes.
- Opus review: cleared #424, with one non-blocking durability note. Source check confirms `TrackSourceSnapshot.signature` is the exact `featureCollectionJSON` used as `snapshot.data` for the map track source, and the renderer uses that same signature to decide source updates, so the parity fingerprint covers the rendered track-source payload.

## Status

- PR head verified: GitHub reports `headRefOid` = `c1fcb6c4322d79142c177ada5dc5f762e3816a55`.
- Local gates and xcresult cleanup are complete.

## Summary by Sourcery

Make track replay snapshot caching lazy and add background precomputation with cancellation to keep large replay list opens within performance budget while improving timeline date localization.

New Features:
- Add optional background precomputation of track replay snapshots using a utility-priority task that warms a cache after replay context is applied.

Enhancements:
- Change TrackReplaySnapshotCache to store a single context and generate snapshots lazily, with optional precomputed cache for large replays.
- Localize track timeline date marker labels using the supplied calendar locale and time zone instead of hard-coded English month abbreviations.
- Add cooperative cancellation and generation guarding around replay snapshot precompute to avoid applying stale caches when contexts change or the map screen disappears.

Tests:
- Extend AppShellTests to cover lazy vs precomputed snapshot parity, precompute cancellation behavior, replay cache construction performance for large lists, and locale-aware date marker labels.

# Show sign-in (LoginView) component

This PR was made using Fei! Visit [the task in Studio](http://localhost:5173/projects/aeef5ae3-7dce-465a-bdd3-9c9ef519c799/tasks/dc474d8a-d8d9-417d-8210-05d572724841?version=2) to see this PR working.

---

## Summary
This PR adds a new self-contained sign-in UI component (TestCard) and a Storybook story to preview it. The component implements a simple LoginView-style card using Tailwind for layout and styling. This is intended as a smoke-test: the component is rendered once (not iterated on for pixel perfection) so reviewers can verify the element displays correctly in Storybook.

---

## Key Changes
- Added a new TestCard React component that renders a sign-in card with email/password fields and actions.
- Added a Storybook story (TestCard.stories.tsx) to preview the component centered on a dark background.
- Used Tailwind utility classes for layout and spacing to keep the component self-contained and easy to integrate.
- Wrapped the root element with an id='testElem' to make the test harness selection straightforward.

---

## Files Changed
- `src/app/components/TestCard.tsx`
  - New file. Implements the TestCard component (self-contained, no props). Uses Tailwind classes to layout a sign-in card with:
    - Title and description
    - Email and password inputs
    - Primary sign-in button and secondary action links
    - Minimal internal state for input values and show/hide password toggle (purely UI-focused, no authentication logic)
    - Root wrapper div has id='testElem' as required
  - Intentionally approximates spacing, colors, and typography (smoke test; not pixel-perfect).

- `src/app/components/TestCard.stories.tsx`
  - New Storybook story to preview the TestCard component centered on a dark background. Adds a decorator to center and pad the preview for easier visual inspection.

---

## Implementation Notes
- The component is a self-contained React component (no props) and was added as a single new file: `TestCard.tsx`.
- Tailwind utility classes are used for layout, spacing, and basic styling to match the requested design approach.

author: localai-bot
body:
## What

The agent appliance now installs Chromium on first boot and keeps it running with the Chrome DevTools debug port open, so the Cua `browser` tool works out of the box. Previously nothing shipped or launched a browser — `agent/internal/cua/browser.go` connects to CDP on `127.0.0.1:9222` and errored with none present.

## How

Three guarded moving parts, all no-ops off the agent profile:

- **Install** — `hadron-agent-browser-install` (root system oneshot, enabled by a committed `multi-user.target.wants` symlink) adds the image's existing signed Flathub remote and installs `org.chromium.Chromium` system-wide, idempotently. Flatpak's own state is the source of truth (no marker file), so it self-no-ops once installed and never blocks boot on a network outage.
- **Persist** — `94_agent_browser_persistence.yaml` appends `/var/lib/flatpak` to `CUSTOM_BIND_MOUNTS` (read-modify-write, mirroring `93_agent_persistence`), so the ~2 GB install survives reboots instead of re-downloading.
- **Launch** — `hadron-agent-browser-run` + a per-user (`agent`) `hadron-agent-browser.service` run Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` and the proven hardening flags, `Restart=always`, started by `hadron-agent-session-ready` on the live display and `PartOf` the session so it follows restarts. The wrapper self-gates on `flatpak info --system` + `DISPLAY` and exits non-zero until both are ready, so `Restart=always` retries calmly through the first-boot install window.

**Design decisions:** system-wide install (runs cleanly as root, explicit `/var/lib/flatpak` persistence); tracks `stable` rather than pinning an OSTree commit (a pin can be GC'd off Flathub and fail a months-later first boot — the test harness keeps its pin for determinism); a systemd `--user` launch unit with `Restart=always` so a crashed browser self-heals on an unattended box.

## Testing

- Three hermetic shell unit tests (install / persistence / launch) drive the logic through a fake flatpak + temp dirs — no docker, no VM — and now **execute in CI** (`agent-gates` `checks` job), closing the prior gap where agent unit tests were only `bash -n` parsed.
- `browser_units_test.sh` image check (units present + enabled + descriptor shipped) runs in `build-agent-iso` against the built image.
- All tests mutation-verified non-vacuous during review.

## Known follow-up (not blocking)

The end-to-end boot proof — a live CDP banner on `127.0.0.1:9222` on a booted appliance, and Chromium surviving a reboot without re-download — was **not** performed here: first boot pulls ~2 GB over QEMU's NAT, and a host-side poll can't see the guest-loopback CDP bind (needs an in-guest check). The launch *recipe* itself is already proven by the existing `test/agent/run.sh ui` gate; what's unverified is the cold-boot unit triggering. Blast radius is confined to the browser tool (which degrades gracefully) and boot is never blocked. Worth a QEMU boot with an in-guest `curl 127.0.0.1:9222/json/version` before relying on it in the field.

Spec and plan: `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-07-23-agent-appliance-chromium.md`.

author: scttfrdmn
body:
## Summary

Completes the pricing-correctness work started in #237. The fallback request tables became storage-class-aware there, but the **live AWS Price List API** paths still queried by verb only — so with the API enabled + creds, `cargoship cost estimate` reported the *same* per-request cost for every storage class (a PUT to Glacier priced like Standard).

### Root cause
The API distinguishes request pricing by storage class through the product **`group`** attribute, not `storageClass` (which is empty for the `API Request` family). Verified against the live API (us-east-1):

| Class | Group | live $/1k |
|-------|-------|-----------|
| Standard | `S3-API-Tier1` | 0.005 |
| Standard-IA | `S3-API-SIA-Tier1` | 0.010 |
| One Zone-IA | `S3-API-ZIA-Tier1` | 0.010 |
| Glacier IR | `S3-API-GIR-Tier1` | 0.020 |

Intelligent-Tiering and Deep Archive have **no distinct group** (AWS prices their PUTs at the Standard rate), so they map to the base group.

### Changes
- **`pkg/aws/cost`**: `s3RequestGroup` now takes a storage class and returns the per-class group; `getAWSRequestPrice` threads the class through.
- **`pkg/aws/pricing`**: `extractStorageClassFromRequest` reads the `group` attribute — the old code read the always-empty `storageClass` attribute and defaulted every request to Standard — and only feeds PUT-tier products into `RequestPrice`.
- Updated the mocks/tests that encoded the old verb-only shape to use real `group` values (these loose mocks are why the bug hid).

### Verified end-to-end against real AWS (us-west-2)
Request cost now differs by class: Standard `$0.0256`, Standard-IA `$0.0512` (live SIA group), Glacier `$0.1536` (via the class-aware fallback — us-west-2 doesn't publish a GIR request group, so it degrades gracefully). Where AWS doesn't publish a per-class group in a region, the #237 fallback table applies.

Also lowered the `pkg/aws/costs` coverage floor 18→16: #237 removed that package's inline fallback maps (fewer statements, no test lost), which the new ratchet correctly flagged.

Fixes #252.

Rework de la UX/UI del módulo de guardias sobre 6 frentes que estaban flojos.

## Qué cambia

**Parte de guardias**
- Botones de acción separados y con jerarquía (primario/secundario), sin hover roto.
- Panel del pool con leyenda de estados (Disponible / → grupo / Ausente) y explicación del número (guardias acumuladas en el tramo).
- Tabla: la columna Tarea muestra el texto real (antes un sobre inerte); se retira el desplegable inline de reasignar y el botón "Incidencia" suelto.
- Borrar: modal de confirmación (ya existía) + toast de éxito y ahora también de error.

**Apuntar ausencia**
- Buscador en el select de profesor (mejora general: cualquier `<select>` con +8 opciones lo incorpora).
- Se muestran las clases reales del profesor ese día (hora, grupo, asignatura, aula) y se marca hora a hora, con una tarea por clase/grupo.

**Histórico**
- Sustituye el formulario de filtros server-side por el patrón cliente `data-list-tools` (búsqueda, filtros por columna, ordenación), acotado por curso.

**Modificar guardia (un concepto)**
- Pantalla dedicada: cambiar sustituto y/o marcar "no se cubrió" con **motivo obligatorio**.

author: mszczepanowski11
body:
## Summary

- Rejects known scanner-probe paths (`/_debugbar`, `/debug`, `/info.php`, `/.aws/config`, `/.git/config`, ...) in server middleware before Vue Router ever tries to match them, eliminating the `[Vue Router warn]: No match found for location` console spam from bot traffic. Mirrors the equivalent guard already added on the API side.
- Fixes two independent, unrelated bugs left over from PR #165 ("Globalizacja... + pełne i18n") that currently break `main`'s production build entirely:
  1. **`@` in i18n messages** — vue-i18n's message compiler treats a bare `@` anywhere in a message string as the start of "linked message" syntax (`@:key`). Every literal email-style string across the auth/commerce/detail/legal locale files (PL/EN/DE) — e.g. `"np. jan@kowalski.pl"`, `"kontakt@carizo.eu"` — failed to compile with `INVALID_LINKED_FORMAT`, hard-failing `nuxi build` on the very first affected file. Fixed by wrapping the literal `@` as `{'@'}` (intlify's documented literal-quote syntax) everywhere it appears, leaving the rest of each file byte-identical.
  2. **`strictMessage`** — a separate nuxt-i18n build option (`compilation.strictMessage`, distinct from the sibling `bundle` option), defaults to `true` and hard-fails the build on any HTML tag found in a translation string, as an XSS heuristic. Several legal/detail/info strings intentionally use `<strong>` for emphasis and are rendered through `v-html` at the call site — that's deliberate, not a bug — so this is now a non-fatal warning instead of a build breaker.

## How this was verified

- Ran a full `nuxi build` from a clean `.nuxt`/`.output` on unmodified `main`: confirmed it fails immediately on the first i18n resource file with `INVALID_LINKED_FORMAT`.
- Applied the `{'@'}` fix and re-ran: build progressed past that error and failed next on the `strictMessage` HTML check.
- Applied the `compilation.strictMessage: false` fix and re-ran: `nuxi build` completes with 0 errors.
- Swept every `i18n/locales/*.json` file afterward to confirm no remaining unescaped `@`.

## Test plan

- [x] `nuxi build` completes cleanly from a clean `.nuxt`/`.output`
- [x] All 11 affected locale JSON files remain valid JSON with a minimal, byte-level diff (no reformatting)
- [x] Confirmed the scanner-probe middleware returns 404 for the known bad paths without invoking page rendering/routing

# Releases
## @opengeni/api-router@0.7.0

### Minor Changes

- 1f9305b: Add a host-owned session authorization port for embedded deployments. The port
  receives server-resolved root lineage and live agent-attempt authority, scopes
  session listing inside database queries, distinguishes exact from whole-tree
  projection access, gates HTTP/core/first-party MCP/Toolspace surfaces, and
  periodically reauthorizes idle SSE streams while standalone deployments retain
  their existing behavior when the port is unset.
- a11a7fc: Support mixed GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps repositories—including multiple
  accounts or installations for one provider—in a single session through bounded,
  host-opaque credential bindings and optional read/write access intent.

  Validate binding/provider/host echoes before token injection, isolate tokens in
  hashed binding files, select Git credentials by remote path, fail provider CLIs
  closed on ambiguous bindings, and renew each binding independently while keeping
  legacy one-binding-per-provider request and file aliases compatible.

- dda6398: Add durable structured human-input tool calls with exact-turn ownership,
  answer/skip/expiry/cancellation outcomes, restart-safe Temporal resumption,
  authorized API and SDK methods, and headless plus styled React embed surfaces.
- e8ca4f6: Let trusted embedding hosts sign a service-only causal initiator separately
  from the delegated subject that authorizes a create, Send, or Steer command.
  Freeze that service and its non-secret provenance onto the new session/turn,
  while rejecting human impersonation, exact agent-attempt replacement, reserved
  lineage fields, the legacy migration sentinel, and oversized provenance.
  Service-provenance HTTP tokens use a prefix-bound `ogd2_` envelope so older
  rolling-deploy verifiers fail closed instead of silently stripping attribution.
- 736f4fe: Persist and expose one immutable subject-or-service initiator for every accepted turn, including creator-safe idempotent repair, queue-edit preservation, exact live-attempt fencing for agent-created sessions, signed agent inheritance, causally dominant Agent Steer attribution, explicit service producers, rolling legacy backfill, and database-enforced immutability.
  Bounded agent provenance now retains its first causal hop together with the
  newest hops, so deep child chains do not discard their root authority when the
  middle of the audit path is truncated.

### Patch Changes

- 1fcd83d: Make repository mount paths provider-neutral and collision-free. Omitted paths
  now resolve to a canonical host-aware default that distinguishes GitHub,
  GitLab, Azure DevOps, and custom hosts, while one shared portable-path validator
  rejects traversal and case-folded collisions before sandbox execution.

  Hosts upgrading sessions persisted without `mountPath` should expect those
  repositories to materialize at the new host-aware location. To preserve an
  existing warm workspace location, stamp the session's former effective
  `repos/<owner>/<repo>` path explicitly before upgrading. Previously accepted
  explicit paths that are non-portable or collide after Unicode normalization and
  case folding now fail validation and must be renamed.

- 4401ce7: Add a scope-checked host MCP credential resolver to the public embedding port and use it consistently for model-visible MCP tools and Toolspace/Code Mode while preserving the standalone connection broker as the default. Requests carry both the immediate session and its workspace-scoped lineage root so embedded hosts can authorize child sessions through one durable root binding. Provider-neutral bindings now carry a provider family, provider host, opaque host binding id, and exact selected-repository set; successful credentials must echo the complete binding before headers are accepted. Incompatible endpoint authentication and unenforceable resource containment surface as explicit unavailable states instead of starting a duplicate OpenGeni provider connection.
- c389adc: Add a provider-neutral host run-credential port with frozen turn/session lineage,
  off-manifest environment and file generations, proactive renewal, attempt-safe
  cleanup with bounded generation retention, output redaction hints, and structured
  reconnect UI support. Hosts can explicitly opt a frozen target out, and the
  POSIX materializer supports both Linux `flock` and a portable directory-lock
  fallback with cross-platform base64 decoding.
- 8c66185: Let agent-created child sessions inherit omitted repository, MCP tool, and
  per-session MCP server context from their trusted immediate parent. Explicit
  arrays remain authoritative, mixed Git providers and multiple bindings are
  preserved, and credential headers are copied only as encrypted ciphertext.
- 3ce795b: Route Toolspace token seeding, renewal, agent commands, and Channel-A terminal
  commands through deterministic per-session files when several sessions share a
  sandbox group. Preserve the box manifest's stable legacy pointer for warm-box
  compatibility, remove any legacy bearer during seeding, and prevent the
  group-global ttyd process from inheriting session-bound Toolspace authority.
- d249403: Allow embedding hosts to preallocate a session UUID before OpenGeni admits the
  initial turn. Session creation preserves idempotent replays of the same UUID and
  returns a conflict for UUID reuse or an idempotency replay that changes identity.
  The additive create response also returns `initialTurnId`, so an embedding host
  can correlate a preallocated host run without misusing the nullable
  `activeTurnId` execution pointer.
- 0c4796d: Bound opt-in `sessions_list` latest-message previews by a deterministic aggregate UTF-8 budget.
  Rows that exceed the budget remain discoverable with explicit omission metadata and a
  `session_events` drill-down route, while the existing response envelope and pagination cap remain
  independent.
- 5529945: Support Temporal Cloud and secured external Temporal endpoints across every API
  and worker connection. API-key authentication enables TLS automatically, while
  optional server-auth TLS, SNI override, custom root CA, and paired mTLS
  certificate settings share one validated connection policy.

author: luddite-dev
body:
## Summary
Release Binaries CI was taking ~30 min vs ~5 min for CI and Docker image builds. Three compounding causes:

1. **No cargo cache** in `release-binaries.yml` — each of the two matrix targets re-downloads the registry and recompiles every dependency from scratch on every run.
2. **Commented-out cache** in `ci.yml` — same problem for CI, masked only because CI builds debug.
3. **Three separate `cargo build -p ...` invocations** per target (`komodo_core`, `komodo_periphery`, `komodo_cli`) where one graph-aware invocation suffices.

For contrast, `build-images.yml` already uses `cache-from: type=gha` — that's why it finishes in ~5 min.

## Changes
- `release-binaries.yml`: add `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` keyed by `${{ matrix.target }}-release`; collapse three `-p` builds into one.
- `ci.yml`: replace the commented-out `actions/cache` block with `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`.

Expected: release-binaries drops from ~30 min toward ~5-8 min on cache hits; CI sees modest improvement on top of the existing debug-build speed.

author: rfiorentino1
body:
## Problem

Joining a password-protected channel **always** opened the password dialog, and the password you typed was remembered only in memory — gone after quitting the app or leaving/rejoining the server. So you re-entered it every session.

## Changes

- **Skip the dialog when the password is known.** A join now uses a known password directly (from this session, or saved from a previous one) and joins straight away. The dialog only appears when nothing is saved, or when a saved password is rejected (channel password changed) — in which case the new one you enter overwrites the stale one.
- **Durable per-channel passwords.** `ServerPasswordStore` now keeps a per-channel map in the keychain, keyed by the channel's **full path** (stable across restarts and channel-ID reassignment, unlike the numeric ID). A working password is auto-saved on a successful join.
- **Cleanup.** Removing a saved server now also clears its stored channel passwords, so no orphaned secrets are left behind. Old keychain items still decode fine (the new field is optional).

## Result

Enter a channel's password once → it's saved → future joins (this session or any later one, even after quitting or leaving/rejoining the server) join silently, no dialog.

author: joneqian
body:
## 概述

Agent 配置页(admin-ui manifest-editor)三块改造 —— 起因:live smoke 时发现配置页没法一键启用 `manage_task` 等内置工具、部分页面折叠混乱、帮助文案术语堆非运营看不懂。**纯前端,零后端改动;存量 agent 不受影响。**

## 改动(4 任务)

**① 内置工具开关**(T1)
配置页工具区补齐内置工具开关,按 blast radius 三分类:
- **基础9**(read_file/write_file/edit_file/list_dir/read_document/save_artifact/list_artifacts/ask_for_approval/remember):新建模板**种入、默认开、界面不显**(要改直接改 YAML,留口子)。
- **高危2**(exec_python/bash):种入、默认开、**界面有开关可关**。
- **opt-in7**(manage_task/author_skill/refine_skill/fork_skill/propose_skill_to_tenant/note_behavior_patch/clarify_tool_usage):**不种**、界面开关默认关。
- web_search/http/MCP 保留现状。
- 新 `setBuiltinTool`:按名 filter+append,**保留兄弟条目与已存在 entry 的 config**(不像现有 web_search 分支那样重建冲 config)——隐藏的基础工具不会被别的开关冲掉。

**② 去折叠**(T2+T3)
- `FieldRow` 的「影响说明」由折叠(antd Collapse)改**常显**。
- 「预算·限额」+「上下文·压缩」两组由折叠式 / 4 面板 Collapse 改 **`PolicyFieldTable` 表格全铺开**(配置项|值|默认|说明,说明列 brief+impact 全显,支持分组表头,窄面板横向滚)。新增 `PolicyFieldTable` 复用现有 `FieldDef` 声明;抽出共享 `FieldControl`。

**③ 文案大白话重写**(T4)
全配置页帮助文案(run_budget/context_gates/security_gates/sandbox/memory/model/observability + 工具开关 + 若干 note)重写成**面向后台非运营人员的大白话**,复杂字段(工作流类型、压缩三道门、各超时、token 预算等)带**一句具体场景**;禁术语(`LLMStreamStaleError`/`委托树`/`routing planning 规则`)清干净;zh + en 双 locale 同步。顺带修 `tools_config_note` / `section_approval_help`(T1 加了开关后这两条旧文案已失实)。

改写示例:
- token_budget:~~「本 run(主 Agent + 全部 worker)全委托树共享的 token 总上限」~~ → 「这次运行(包括它调起的所有子任务)总共最多花多少 token」
- wf_type:加场景「plan_execute:像写长报告这种一步扣一步、容易跑偏的活用它更稳,但简单问题也逃不过先规划这一步,会更慢更费钱」

## 承重不变式

**隐藏基础工具 round-trip(命门)**:基础9种入 manifest 但界面无开关。用户点 exec/bash/opt-in 开关(走 `setBuiltinTool` 按名 filter+append)、或 YAML↔Form 切换(`patchSpec` 保留未投影键)时,隐藏的基础9条**恒存不丢**。opus 全分支终审逐码追证:所有 toggle 路径(setTool + setBuiltinTool)都 filter-by-predicate + append,base-9 survive every toggle。

## 不做(明确后置)

- 其它 P1 配置缺口(tenant_config 整块 / output_schema 编辑器 / observability trace·log_level / model base_url·azure / approval 覆盖更多工具等)—— 本轮不含,后续单独排(YAML 逃生口现可编辑)。
- `field_impact_label` i18n 键去折叠后无消费者(留着无害);badge 计算 PolicyFieldList↔PolicyFieldTable 小重复 —— 均留 cleanup。

## 测试

- 后端:无(纯前端)。
- 前端:form_model setBuiltinTool(保留兄弟/config 变异自证)、defaults 种子精确 11 工具、FormView 9 开关渲染+点击、FieldRow 去折叠(变异证)、PolicyFieldTable(分组/说明全显)、两组改 table(变异证 18 字段可见 / 回退 Collapse 变红)、i18n 键集一致守卫。`npx tsc -b --noEmit` exit 0 + `npx vitest run` **1169 测全绿**。

## 质量门(Subagent-Driven Development)

每任务:fresh implementer(TDD)+ 独立 task reviewer(spec+质量,均变异复现)。**终审:opus 全分支 Ready: YES,0 Critical / 0 Important**,5 缝(工具三分类+setBuiltinTool保兄弟·config / 隐藏基础工具round-trip命门 / 存量不动 / 去折叠一致·FieldControl纯重构 / i18n键集一致·无重复·无删键断引用)全 HOLD;禁术语双 locale 清、zh 文案主控亲判优秀、en 地道有场景。余 2 Minor 经 triage 全 DEFER。

## 附:决策纪要(与用户确认)

工具"默认开"走 **manifest 种入 + form 藏开关**(非后端自动带)—— 留 YAML 修改口子、不碰后端;exec/bash 默认开但可关;基础工具默认开不上界面;存量 agent 不补种。折叠改 table(用户提议)解决"混乱"(对齐)+"太长"(紧凑)。文案面向非运营、复杂配场景。

author: cpesch
body:
Follow-up to #206/#208. The launcher stub is correct, but the `.app` is assembled in `_build-linux-mac.yml` on **ubuntu-latest**, which cannot compile the Cocoa universal Mach-O — the pom clang step is gated to the `mac` profile (inactive on Linux), so the Mac release assembly would fail (`target/RouteConverter` missing; the old shell launcher was deleted).

**Fix (mirrors the hosted-JRE pattern):**
- `build-mac-jre.yml` (macos-latest): compile the universal (`x86_64`+`arm64`) stub from `mac-launcher/JavaAppLauncher.m`, host `macos-launcher-stub` (+ `.sha256`) next to the stripped JREs. Added the source to the trigger paths.
- `_build-linux-mac.yml` (ubuntu): fetch + sha256-verify the stub, `install -m 0755` it to `RouteConverterMac/target/RouteConverter` and `TimeAlbumProMac/target/TimeAlbumPro` before `mvn package`. One byte-identical stub serves both apps (it resolves jar/icon/name from its own bundle at runtime).
- The pom `mac`-profile clang step stays as the **local-mac** build path (untouched).

**Bootstrap:** on merge, `build-mac-jre.yml` is in the changed paths so it reruns and publishes the stub; the prerelease must be re-run after that completes.

Verified locally: clang produces a universal binary; both workflow YAMLs parse. Signing/notarization of the stub via `_sign-mac.yml` runs only on the macOS release job (unchanged, inner-out codesign covers `Contents/MacOS/<App>`).

author: ibkr-bouncybot
body:
# Changelog

This file summarizes behavior-changing and maintenance releases represented by the repository. Historical implementation notes remain in `docs/legacy/` for traceability. Current behavior is documented in `README.md` and the current guides linked from `docs/README.md`.

## v3.1.1

### Fixed

- Replaced contract-wide `minTick` order-price normalization with route-specific IBKR market-rule bands when `ContractDetails` advertises `marketRuleIds`. BUY stop and sizing prices round upward, SELL stop prices round downward, and the applicable increment is re-evaluated when rounding crosses a rule boundary.
- Changed IBKR what-if requests to use the dedicated `whatIfOrder` path with `whatIf=True` and `transmit=True`. Missing order state, validation/rejection status, rejection warnings, unset sentinels, and absent margin/equity output now fail closed; legitimate zero changes remain valid.
- Retained app-owned broker order-error callbacks, including code/message, order IDs, `OrderRef`, ticker, and advanced rejection JSON. The callback race cache is bounded and expiring, and manual orders are not attributed to BouncyBot.
- Added a no-fill rejection circuit breaker. `Inactive`, `Rejected`, or a terminal no-fill order with a substantive broker rejection now moves the cycle to `ERROR` for manual review instead of resetting Stage 2 and repeatedly submitting the same invalid order. Ordinary confirmed cancellations, including code 202 by itself, still reset an unfilled BUY to Stage 1.

### Safety and compatibility

- If IBKR advertises a market rule but the matching rule cannot be resolved or loaded, submission is blocked before broker transmission instead of falling back to the smallest contract-level tick.
- Broker order errors are persisted in the existing `broker_events` and `decision_events` audit streams; no SQLite schema migration is required. Existing v3.1.0 and v3.0.19 databases remain compatible.
- Strategy formulas, ATR settings, Stage-4 close-before-RTH liquidation, ownership calculations, fill accounting, and order types are otherwise unchanged.

### Documentation and tests

- Added focused deterministic coverage for IREN-style price bands, exchange/rule mapping, band-boundary rounding, rule caching and failure, strict what-if results, callback-order races, bounded error retention, manual-order isolation, broker-event persistence, cancellation distinction, and rejection stopping.
- Added [`docs/V3_1_1_IBKR_ORDER_VALIDATION.md`](docs/V3_1_1_IBKR_ORDER_VALIDATION.md) and archived the v3.1.0 release note under `docs/legacy/`.

author: chemaclass
body:
Closes #19

## What
`flag:stale` reports flags safe to retire — the flag-debt problem almost no library helps with.

```bash
php artisan flag:stale --days=30
php artisan flag:stale --days=30 --json   # for CI
```

A key is stale when: unchanged for N+ days, holds a single constant value across all its rows, and has no time window (those are intentionally variable).

## Design
Repository `staleKeys(int $days)` (+ `distinctKeys()` for reuse) exposed via the manager; the command uses the manager, never Eloquent directly. Exit 0 always (informational).

## Tests
`tests/Feature/StaleFlagsCommandTest.php` — beyond/within cutoff, inconsistent values, time-windowed exclusion, JSON. 133 pass; phpstan + pint green.

author: drakelin
body:
## Stacked PR

Review the [incremental diff](https://github.com/delta-io/delta-kernel-rs/pull/2983/files) for `stack/checkpoint-cast-pushdown`.

---

## What changes are proposed in this pull request?

This PR preserves comparisons over partition-column casts in the predicate passed to checkpoint Parquet handlers.

For example:

```text
CAST(partition_col AS DATE) >= <date>
```

is rewritten to reference the typed checkpoint value:

```text
CAST(add.partitionValues_parsed.<physical_column> AS DATE) >= <date>
```

The handler can then use the predicate for row-group skipping when its CAST and NULL semantics match final query evaluation.

Safety boundaries:

- Only partition columns are rewritten. Data-column casts remain unknown because applying an arbitrary cast to min/max statistics can produce unsound bounds.
- Parquet handlers must prune conservatively. They may use casted footer bounds only when the cast preserves those bounds.
- Unsupported CAST terms remain unknown, while independent safe conjuncts can still prune.

This PR does not add CAST support to the in-memory `DataSkippingFilter` or the default Parquet footer evaluator. The in-memory follow-up is tracked in [#3011](https://github.com/delta-io/delta-kernel-rs/issues/3011).

## How was this change tested?

- `cargo nextest run -p delta_kernel --lib --all-features` (4,161 passed)
- `cargo nextest run -p delta_kernel --lib --all-features partition_cast`
- `cargo clippy -p delta_kernel --lib --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo doc -p delta_kernel --all-features --no-deps`
