author: lyxot
body:
## Summary

Adds a disposable macOS CI proof for finite VLM shape planning, following the real-model family matrix from #3. This PR changes CI only; it does not modify production code.

The workload is intentionally short and correctness-focused: 12 unchanged examples from a pinned real VLM dataset, with a temporary fixed cap of 7 so the established qualified families exercise signature-reducing bucketing rather than exact planning.

The workflow also tests the hypothetical state where upstream #893 has merged. It pins that PR at `42362afd9172ae806a5a555d8ca2fd6539f40eeb` and applies only its `compile.py` and `loader.py` production diff to temporary current-main and feature worktrees. Both children record and compare the same nonempty overlay digest; no #893 production file is committed here.

## Coverage

- Covers all 36 unique image-capable model repositories from #3.
- Omits duplicate video cases and audio-only candidates because this workflow exercises image+text training.
- Runs each repository in an independent `macos-14` job, with up to five jobs in parallel.
- Reports explicit model-size, disk-headroom, and OOM outcomes as resource skips.
- Resolves compile policy after model setup and reports architectures declined by both main and feature as `skipped-unqualified`; they are never counted as planner passes.
- Reports an upstream-main model-load incompatibility with the pinned runtime as `skipped-unsupported` only when the terminal error is positively identified during `model_load`.

## Real-data workload

Every model uses the same deterministically selected schedule from [`axolotl-ai-co/llava-instruct-mix-vsft-small`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/axolotl-ai-co/llava-instruct-mix-vsft-small), pinned at revision `a3ca113612453f2624904f1c99d8b650a56cc430`:

- pre-scan all 2,592 real train rows;
- choose 12 unchanged rows from three naturally repeated image-size families and four natural text-length bands, then shuffle with seed 3407;
- selected rows contain 12 unique text lengths from 114–574 characters and image sizes 333×500, 375×500, and 640×480;
- preserve the original images, messages, answers, labels, and conversation contents;
- QLoRA rank 4, batch size 1, gradient accumulation 1, and 12 training steps;
- max sequence length 384, CCE, gradient checkpointing, and full-step compile;
- no configured MLX memory limits;
- current main plus the pinned #893 overlay as the compiled/unplanned baseline;
- this feature plus the same overlay with `compile_max_variants=7`.

Each matrix job is bounded at 180 minutes. Main and planned children each receive 80 minutes, leaving 20 minutes for checkout, dependency installation, downloads outside the children, result serialization, and artifact upload.

## Required evidence

A model passes only when CI proves all of the following:

- main and planned fixture digests, trained-token totals, and per-step token series match exactly;
- final train loss differs by at most 0.8%;
- both applicable paths finish with full-step compilation enabled;
- fixed-cap planner action is exact at or below 7 raw signatures and bucket above 7;
- reported raw/planned counts equal the actual installed catalogs;
- the installed catalog contains at most 7 signatures;
- runtime-observed `(phase, family, endpoint)` signatures exactly equal the installed catalog;
- observed widths equal admitted endpoints;
- the planned path consumes the exact 12 real row IDs in shuffled order;
- the guard reports lazy finite VLM batches and full-step compile scope;
- main and feature use the same pinned #893 overlay digest.

The aggregate additionally requires at least one verified bucket result. It fails for any correctness/parity/planner error, missing artifact, or lost compile qualification relative to main. Feature-child failures and every post-load failure remain hard failures.

## CI evidence

[Run 30138844443](https://github.com/Lyxot/unsloth-zoo/actions/runs/30138844443) attempted all 36 repositories and produced seven verified A/B passes:

| Family | Action | Signatures raw → planned | Trained tokens | Loss relative difference | Padding work | Main / planned runtime | Main / planned MLX peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2-VL | bucket | 8 → 7 | 1,286 | 0.074% | 1.40% | 116 / 101 s | 2.14 / 2.10 GiB |
| Qwen2.5-VL | bucket | 8 → 7 | 1,286 | 0.057% | 1.40% | 136 / 122 s | 3.75 / 3.72 GiB |
| Qwen3-VL | bucket | 9 → 7 | 1,212 | 0.090% | 3.35% | 91 / 58 s | 3.20 / 3.15 GiB |
| Qwen3.5-VL | bucket | 9 → 7 | 1,267 | 0.089% | 3.34% | 80 / 35 s | 2.07 / 2.04 GiB |
| Qwen3-VL MoE | bucket | 9 → 7 | 1,212 | 0.186% | 3.35% | 2,058 / 2,052 s | 13.85 / 13.80 GiB |
| LLaVA | exact | 1 → 1 | 36 | 0.000% | 0.00% | 260 / 238 s | 5.67 / 5.66 GiB |
| Mistral3-VL | exact | 3 → 3 | 2,169 | 0.000% | 0.00% | 2,589 / 2,655 s | 14.08 / 14.05 GiB |

All seven preserved the exact per-step trained-token series and observed exactly the installed catalog. The five bucketed runs reduced signatures to the configured cap with 1.40–3.35% quadratic padding-work overhead.

Runtime deltas from 12-step cells are dominated by model load and first compilation and are not performance claims. The large Qwen3-VL MoE and Mistral3-VL cells still took about 75 and 95 minutes end to end, respectively, so they are useful one-time coverage but unsuitable for routine fast PR gating.

The other 29 repositories produced:

- 10 explicit `skipped-unqualified` outcomes;
- 4 pinned-runtime/model-load `skipped-unsupported` outcomes;
- 3 resource skips;
- 12 hard main/parity failures.

The aggregate remains intentionally red for those hard failures. One blocking feature finding is Gemma4: its planned path stayed exact at 7 signatures with zero padding, but main and planned trained-token histories diverged (1,108 versus 1,376 total) and both losses became NaN. Other hard failures include processor keyword/tensor-mode incompatibilities, missing pad tokens or LoRA targets, missing TensorFlow, mismatched model weights, and Metal execution errors.

## Effect of upstream #893

Compared with the prior 140-step run without the overlay:

- LLaVA changes from a processor `patch_size=None` failure to a complete exact A/B pass with identical tokens and loss.
- GLM-4.6V and LFM2-VL change from unsupported model-load failures to clean, symmetric compile-unqualified classifications.
- No other family gains an end-to-end training pass from #893 in this matrix.
- Qwen3-VL MoE and Mistral3-VL now finish because the schedule is 12 steps instead of timing out during the previous 140-step run; that is a workload-length gain, not an #893 gain.

LLaVA's prepared schedule collapsed to one 384-wide signature and only 36 supervised tokens, so this proves the repaired processor and exact planned path are compatible; it does not prove variable-width LLaVA bucketing.

## Validation

- Python byte compilation and Ruff
- pinned real-dataset selection and deterministic fixture digest
- processor-level post-prepare survey for the established qualified families
- 36-entry matrix completeness and selected-model filtering
- current-main/feature #893 overlay composition, identity, and nonempty digest checks
- workflow YAML parsing
- aggregate exact-only rejection and bucket acceptance
- two focused development reviewers plus an independent clean reviewer
- `git diff --check`

author: nh13
body:
Sizes the per-chunk read pool from the actual read count instead of a bytes/100 heuristic.

## What
The per-chunk chaining pool was sized `nreads = actual_chunk_size / 100 + 10` (an estimate assuming ~100 bp/read). At the 256 MB chunk cap this speculatively allocated a ~5 GB `seedBuf` before parsing a single read, then often freed it when the real read count differed. This starts the pool empty and lets the pre-existing grow-on-demand path — which already runs before any read indexes the buffers — size it exactly to the chunk's read count in one allocation, reused across chunks.

## Byte-identity
The grow check already guarantees capacity ≥ `n_seqs` at index time for any starting value including 0, so no buffer is ever under-sized. `calloc`/`malloc` zero-init semantics are unchanged. The original over-allocation was pure waste.

Validated: full-run record md5 identical to the frozen baseline on all four samples.

## Performance
Interleaved A/B, wgs-5M t16, byte-identity gated, best-of-5: **−0.70%** median, stable.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved processing for empty or zero-read inputs, preventing unnecessary buffer allocation.
  * Scratch memory is now allocated based on the actual number of reads processed, improving memory efficiency.
  * Enhanced grow-on-demand handling supports reliable processing across chunks of varying sizes.

It's a little more involved than just enabling strict mode, as you can see. I didn't realize strict mode was turned off until a recent typescript update. author: kunalsuri
body:
## Summary

Principal-level UI/UX audit of `site/` (every page and component read,
app run locally, every route screenshotted at mobile/desktop widths,
light/dark). Full plan and per-item acceptance criteria in
[`docs/ui-ux-improvement-log.md`](docs/ui-ux-improvement-log.md).

Four prioritized fixes, ranked by user impact × frequency × consistency
benefit, discounted by regression risk — no new dependencies, no
changes to `data/kb.json`/the kitchen pipeline/the capability-tool
taxonomy:

1. **Mobile navigation was unusable.** The 7-item nav had no
   hamburger/collapse; at <768px every multi-word label line-wrapped
   individually, producing a ~90px broken header on every page. Added a
   toggle button + slide-down panel (vanilla JS, matching the existing
   `ThemeToggle.astro` pattern); desktop is pixel-identical to before.

2. **Install-command tool tabs didn't work at all — for anyone.**
   Started as a keyboard-accessibility fix (the tab radios were
   `display:none`, so keyboard/screen-reader users could never reach
   them) but turned up a deeper pre-existing bug: the per-tool CSS lived
   in `<style is:global>{jsExpression}</style>`, which Astro never
   evaluates — it rendered the literal, un-interpolated JS source into
   the page. The tab switcher was inert for mouse users too; clicking
   "VS Code" never actually showed the VS Code install command. Fixed
   by computing the CSS in frontmatter and rendering it via
   `set:html`, verified against dev SSR and the static build. While
   auditing this pattern, found and fixed the same missing-focus-ring
   bug in 4 more spots across `SkillExplorer.tsx` and
   `SimilarityGalaxy.tsx`.

3. **Dead Tailwind color classes silently dropped styling sitewide.**
   `zinc-450`, `zinc-650`, `zinc-850`, etc. aren't real Tailwind shades
   (only `50/100/.../900/950` are) — Tailwind emits no CSS for them, so
   the intended muted-gray text/borders never applied across
   `index.astro`, `about.astro`, `Doctor.tsx`, and the skill detail
   page. Mapped all ~34 occurrences to their nearest real shade.

4. **No skip-to-content link; copy buttons gave no screen-reader
   feedback.** Added a standard visually-hidden skip link (first
   focusable element, jumps real DOM focus to `<main>`) and a shared
   `aria-live="polite"` region that all "Copy" actions (prompt, install
   command, skill ID) now announce to.

## Validation

- `npm run lint` — clean
- `astro check` — 0 errors (35+ files)
- `npm run test` (Vitest) — 50/50 passing
- `npm run build` — all 526 pages build
- `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright) — 10/11 passing; the one failure
  (a `page.reload()` timeout in `theme-toggle.spec.ts`) was confirmed to
  reproduce identically on a clean checkout of this branch's base
  commit — pre-existing, sandbox-only (repeated headless-Chromium
  reloads under swiftshader), unrelated to these changes
- Manual visual sweep: all 7 routes × mobile/desktop × light/dark (28
  screenshots) — no regressions
- Keyboard-only pass: skip link, mobile nav, install-tab switching
  (Tab + arrow keys), copy-button focus rings — all verified

Note: the `Site (Vitest + Playwright)` CI check has been failing since
before this branch existed (`npm audit --audit-level=high` flagging
transitive `fast-uri`/`svgo` advisories; Dependabot already has an
update open for `svgo` on `main`). Left the lockfile untouched — out of
scope for a UI/UX audit and would conflict with Dependabot's in-flight
fix. See the PR comment thread for detail; will rebase once `main`
recovers.

## Test plan

- [x] Implement each item incrementally, commit + push after each
- [x] `npm run lint`, `astro check`, `npm run test`, `npm run build` after each unit
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` and a manual keyboard-navigation pass
- [x] Screenshot diff (mobile + desktop, light + dark) for touched pages
- [x] Final regression pass across all 7 routes

author: seantunley
body:
## Dependency

Stacked on PR #210. Merge marketing PRs #202 and #207–#210 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## What changed

- New surveys are created as inactive `draft` records.
- Governed lifecycle: draft, in review, changes requested, approved, published, inactive and archived.
- Review validation and mandatory change-request notes.
- Submitter/approver separation.
- Immutable `SurveyVersion` snapshots.
- Replay-safe historical backfill for existing active and inactive surveys.
- Survey responses are stamped with the published survey version.
- One active survey per tenant/trigger enforced by a partial unique index.
- Transactional trigger replacement during publication.
- Advisory and row locks prevent duplicate version numbers and concurrent publication races.
- Published surveys cannot be edited in place; operators create an independent revision draft.
- Existing survey editor is routed through the governed draft service and can no longer activate a survey directly.
- Governed `/marketing/surveys` list and lifecycle detail workspaces.
- Audit records for draft creation, review, approval, publication, deactivation, archive and revision.
- Lifecycle contract tests.

## Safety guarantees

- Drafts never fire triggers.
- Only approved surveys can be published.
- A submitter cannot approve their own survey.
- A published version remains immutable.
- Trigger replacement is explicit and transactional.
- Re-running the migration does not reset later lifecycle states.

## Validation requested

- Prisma migration replay on a database containing legacy surveys and responses.
- Typecheck and lint the new lifecycle actions and pages.
- Verify submitter/approver separation.
- Verify simultaneous publish attempts create one ordered version sequence.
- Verify public responses remain associated with the correct published version.

author: koehlersb747
body:
## What

A context-window overflow is a 400 / invalid-request error, so it previously surfaced as the generic `ValidationError` — indistinguishable from a rejected sampling parameter or a malformed request. Consumers that want to *react* to overflow specifically (compact history and retry, switch to a larger-context model, surface a distinct message) had nothing narrower to catch.

This specializes the shared status dispatch so an overflow 400 raises `ContextLengthExceededError` — a `ValidationError` subclass, so every existing `except ValidationError` keeps matching. **Purely additive.**

## How

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| `dataknobs_llm.exceptions` | New `ContextLengthExceededError(ValidationError)`; re-exported at the package top level for discoverability |
| `LLMProvider._dataknobs_error_for_status` | `_CONTEXT_LENGTH_MARKERS` frozenset + static `_is_context_length_error(status, message, *, code=None)`; a `code` kwarg and an overflow branch placed **after** 429 and **before** the generic 400 |
| `providers/openai.py` | Passes the machine `code` (`getattr(exc, "code", None)`) into the dispatch |
| Anthropic / Bedrock / Ollama / HuggingFace | **Untouched** — each already folds `str(exc)` into the dispatched message, so the message markers fire for free |

Detection is a machine `code` (OpenAI) or a conservative message marker (all vendors), and stays deliberately narrow — an unrelated 400 (a rejected sampling parameter, a malformed request) remains a plain `ValidationError`. The original vendor SDK error is preserved on `__cause__`.

## Backward compatibility

Additive, no consumer sweep: because the new type *is a* `ValidationError`, every existing `except ValidationError` / `except OperationError` / `except DataknobsError` still catches it. The `code` kwarg defaults to `None`, so the other provider call sites are unchanged.

## Tests

New `packages/llm/tests/test_context_length_error.py` (22 tests), reproduce-first with **real** openai / botocore SDK error objects (no mocks) — each fails on HEAD and passes after the fix:

- OpenAI overflow via machine `code`; Anthropic overflow via message marker; Bedrock overflow via real botocore `ClientError` marker
- A **discriminating** non-overflow 400 (rejected `temperature`) that stays a plain `ValidationError`
- Base-predicate units: status-gate-first (a marker in a 429/401/500 never fires), code-or-marker detection, 429 branch precedence
- Export parity + `ValidationError` subclass

The full existing error-handling suite (base + 5 providers, 77 tests) still passes.

## Docs

Dual docs updated — `packages/llm/docs/PROVIDERS.md` + the mkdocs mirror `docs/packages/llm/guides/providers.md` (translation table row + note) — plus a CHANGELOG entry.

author: mjradwin
body:
## Summary

Removes the long-standing duplication between `views/partials/yahrzeit-row.ejs` (server-rendered rows) and the `yahrzeitRow()` string builder in `src/client-yahrzeit.js` (rows added by the "Add another name" button and CSV import). The two were hand-maintained copies that drifted independently — most recently the autofill / password-manager opt-out attributes had to be added in both places.

Follow-up to #87, which is the change that motivated this cleanup.

## Approach

The server now renders the existing partial **once** into an inert `<template id="yahrzeit-row-tmpl">`, passing the literal token `__IDX__` as the row index. To add a row, the client takes that markup and replaces `__IDX__` with the new row number. The EJS partial is the single source of truth for the row markup; the client script owns only the numbering.

```
views/partials/yahrzeit-row.ejs   ──rendered with num──▶  server rows (real values)
                │
                └──rendered with num='__IDX__'──▶  <template>  ──cloned + renumbered──▶  client rows
```

`<template>` is a native HTML element whose contents are parsed but inert (not rendered, not submitted, invisible to `getElementById`) until cloned into the live document — so the placeholder ids inside it never collide with the real rows.

A token replace is used rather than `cloneNode` + attribute rewriting because the index appears in a **text node** (the "N." row label) as well as in **irregular ids** (`del-N`, `sN-0`), which an attribute walk would miss; one string pass handles both uniformly.

Also drops the now-unused `data-sprite-href` form attribute and the `spriteHref` / `pmIgnore` constants from the client script — the trash icon and opt-out attributes are now pre-rendered in the template.

## Net effect

`src/client-yahrzeit.js`: −52 / +16 lines (the ~40-line HTML string builder is gone).

## Testing

- Full server test suite green: 465 passed, 8 skipped.
- Added server-side render assertions (throwaway) confirming the template renders with `__IDX__` tokens and the correct opt-out attributes, and that `__IDX__` → N substitution yields well-formed, uniquely-numbered rows.
- **Real-browser test** (throwaway script using the already-present `puppeteer` dep + pre-installed Chromium — no `package.json` change): loads `/yahrzeit/new`, clicks "Add another name" twice, and verifies 3 uniquely-numbered rows, the `N.` text label, blank/default field state, the name/year snub attributes vs. day (autocomplete only), a working Delete button, no leftover `__IDX__` in the live DOM, and zero page JS errors.

Releases **v1.0.7.17** via the automated release flow (merge → tag → GitHub Release + GHCR image).

## Highlights since v1.0.7.16
- **Server-side oversized-event drops now surface as Error markers.** An event whose properties exceed the 64 KB per-event limit was dropped with only a server-log warning — invisible on the Events page. This is common when a client runs an older `Serilog.Sinks.Ameto` (no client-side truncation) and sends the full event (real case: Wallet.API destructuring a 267 KB `{@Response}` into a property). Both server drop paths now enqueue a compact Error marker in place of the dropped original — same timestamp / trace-span / service — carrying `DroppedBy=server`, `EventBodyBytes`, `EventBodyLimitBytes`, `OriginalTemplate` (truncated) and `OriginalLevel`. `DroppedBy=server` distinguishes it from the client sink's own marker; the marker is tiny so it can never itself be oversized. Query them with `DroppedBy = 'server'`.

author: hschreiber
body:
Just realized that nanobind is not differentiating method overloads by closest type, but by "first argument type which fits" in order of ".def" definition. Which means that if you do:
```C++
.def(nb::init<const Sequence1D&>())
.def(nb::init<const Tensor1D&>())
```
the second version is never reached as any numpy array etc. can also be converted into a std::vector<...>. And a copy is made.
So I changed everything to:
```C++
.def(nb::init<const Tensor1D&>())
.def(nb::init<const Sequence1D&>())
```

author: toddawhittaker
body:
Follow-ups from the review of #193's CSV endpoint (security + code agents flagged the same core issue). No behavior change for a normal single-table download.

- **Resource exhaustion (sec #1 / code #1):** `_select_table_sql` re-ran **every** query in `sql_log` (up to ~20) at the 100k download cap, holding all results in memory at once. It now **probes each candidate cheaply (`LIMIT 1`)** for its column shape, picks the best match, and runs **only that one** at the full cap — peak memory is one result, not N. The endpoint also enforces the **per-user chat rate limit** (a download re-runs a large query; it was unthrottled), and streams the CSV **row-by-row** instead of buffering the whole string on top of the materialized rows.
- **Timeout robustness (sec #2):** `SQLTimeoutError` is now caught — in the probe loop (skip that candidate) and at the endpoint (→ 504) — so one slow stored query no longer 500s the whole download.
- **Selection correctness (code #9):** among queries matching the shown table's column count, the tie now breaks to the **last** one (closest to the answer, since the listing runs right before its COUNT) instead of the longest, which could be a different query on a single-table answer.
- **Duplicate "Download CSV" (ui/ux #4):** the prompt/marker no longer tell the model to name the "Download CSV" button — it echoed the literal label next to the real button (a fake affordance). It now says the data can be downloaded below the table and explicitly not to quote the button.

**Tests:** existing "picks the table query, not a trailing COUNT(\*)" case still green; new "prefers the LAST column-count match" case; ruff + prompt + backend suites pass (fixture-safe).

body:
## Summary
Adds **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** integration to CraftAI in two complementary halves:

1. **Campaign delivery (MCP client → server)** — on approval in the review screen, deliver the finished campaign. Channel-aware:
   - **email** channel → download `.eml` or **send via SMTP**
   - **any other** channel (linkedin, ad, social, blog) → **download HTML**
2. **Knowledge-base (MCP server, read-only)** — expose CraftAI's RAG knowledge base and campaign records as MCP tools any client can query.

CraftAI acts as the MCP **client** for delivery, and as an MCP **server** for the knowledge base — demonstrating both sides of the protocol.

## What's included
**Delivery (`0ee535c`)**
- `mcp_email/` — self-contained FastMCP (streamable-HTTP) server: `render_campaign_email` (`.eml`, no SMTP), `send_campaign_email` (SMTP), `render_campaign_html`; small composer/sender/client helpers
- `main.py` starts the MCP server as a subprocess, gated by `EMAIL_MCP_ENABLED`
- `api/routers/email.py` → `POST /api/v1/email/{brief_id}` (`mode: eml | send | html`)
- Channel-aware delivery UI in `ui/pages/reviewer.py`: on approve **and** a standalone panel for already-approved briefs (email defaults to Download `.eml`, other channels to Download HTML)
- Composer uses structured `subject`/`body`/`cta` for email briefs (+ CTA button)
- `.env.example` documents `EMAIL_MCP_*` / `EMAIL_FROM` / `SMTP_*` (placeholders only)

**Knowledge base (`31d7343`)**
- `mcp_server.py` — standalone FastMCP (stdio) server: `search_knowledge_base`, `list_recent_briefs`, `get_brief_status`, `get_campaign_image`, `list_personas`

## Design notes
- **Read-only** apart from SMTP send; **off the pipeline critical path** — if the MCP server is down, the app runs and only delivery reports "unreachable".
- **Fully removable**: delete `mcp_email/` + `api/routers/email.py` + `mcp_server.py` and undo the `[mcp-email]`-tagged hooks in `main.py` / `api/main.py` / `reviewer.py`.
- Trigger is **human-click only** (never autonomous).

author: alexisibarra
body:
## What

Adds the architecture spine for YouTube Organizer, plus a Phase-1 work split, and reconciles the
four upstream docs the spine supersedes so they stop describing a repo that doesn't exist.

Produced through the `bmad-architecture` coaching flow. Full decision history — including the
alternatives weighed and rejected for every call — is in the run's `.memlog.md` (53 entries).

## The spine

`_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-youtube-organizer-2026-07-24/`

**Paradigm:** layered services, one anti-corruption gateway for YouTube, and a transactional
outbox for every outbound source mutation. 20 `AD-n` invariants, feature altitude — it fixes what
epics must share and stops there.

Load-bearing decisions:

| AD | Decision |
|---|---|
| AD-2 | Two-tree repo, no Nx/pnpm; npm for the frontend |
| AD-3 | DRF serializers are the API contract; TS types generated via `drf-spectacular` + `@hey-api/openapi-ts`, CI fails on drift |
| AD-4 | One list endpoint owns every browse surface, with a fully enumerated query grammar |
| AD-6 / AD-7 | Transactional outbox; persist → verify → *then* clear `_Inbox`, so FR-6's crash-safety is structural rather than careful coding |
| AD-9 / AD-17 | Phase 1 is localhost-only and sync is user-triggered |
| AD-14 | Drop `djangorestframework-simplejwt` for a first-party PyJWT auth module |
| AD-19 | Tag identity is normalised; tag membership mutates by delta only, never set-replacement |
| AD-20 | Backup invariant, gating the only irreversible upstream operation |

`WORK-SPLIT.md` breaks Phase 1 into 14 epics with a dependency graph. Critical path
`E1 → E5 → E6 → E7 → E13`; cheapest useful slice is the sync engine with no UI at all.

## Two findings worth a look

**SimpleJWT is a dead end here.** Last release 5.5.1 (2025-07-21); PyPI classifiers stop at
Django 5.2, and the changelog never mentions 6.0. It's the whole auth mechanism, so "probably
still works" isn't good enough — AD-14 moves token issue/verify to a small first-party module
over PyJWT 2.13.0. The cookie contract with the frontend is unchanged; only the backend
implementation moves, and `JWTAuthCookieMiddleware`'s global request mutation retires with it.

**The library had no durability story.** FR-6 deletes the YouTube copy after import and FR-4
later deletes whole playlists upstream, while AD-17 puts the only survivor in an unbacked Docker
volume on one laptop. PRD §8 names local durability an NFR. AD-20 adds a `make backup` target
from the first data-model story and gates FR-4's irreversible deletion on a recent backup.

## Doc reconciliation

Amended surgically — struck through with the reason and the `AD` id beside each, not rewritten.

- `Docs/FRONTEND-STACK.md` — Nx/pnpm rows and the shared-types package; install commands to npm; phantom-dep rule corrected for npm hoisting; pin-staleness warning (`~16.1.6` is behind the 16.2.x LTS line and a July 2026 security release)
- `Docs/CI-AND-GITHUB-GATES.md` — translation table from Accountr's Nx/pnpm/Prisma commands to this repo's; changesets and deploy marked not-applicable/deferred
- `EXPERIENCE.md` — UJ-2 and the sync state rows move from scheduled to manual trigger
- `_bmad-output/project-context.md` — spine declared binding; stack, auth mechanism and pre-push hook corrected

## Not in this PR

The `.github/workflows/*` and `.githooks/pre-push` files still contain Accountr's Nx/Prisma steps.
The docs now describe the right commands, but rewriting the CI itself is real work and belongs in
epic E3 rather than a docs commit.

## Review notes

Docs only — no application code, no dependency changes, no migrations. Nothing here is executable,
so CI has nothing to gate; the decisions are what needs review, particularly AD-14 (replacing a
working auth library) and AD-9 (dropping the unattended-sync premise for Phase 1).

author: imaustink
body:
## What

Switches the **chat** path to the same live Remote Control surface the GitHub triage path already uses, and cleans up several confusing chat-only artifacts: a doubled auth prompt, funky link formatting, a re-auth caused by unshared credentials, and a false "no PR found" warning on tasks that never involved a PR.

Per the design discussion: opencode stays live (its preview page + ADR 0026 NATS tunnel are untouched), the claude.ai session URL scoped to the login account is acceptable, and the RC login is a single shared operator account.

## Changes

**1. Chat facade surfaces the Remote Control URL** (`agent-orchestrator`). The streaming chat facade routed the `remote-control-url` progress event into a 120-char status label that mangled the URL; it now streams it as clickable *"watch live / take over"* content, as its own paragraph (leading + trailing blank lines) so it never runs together with a preceding chunk. Non-streaming path skips it (no live session left once a blocking response returns).

**2. Fix the doubled auth prompt on the chat side** (`agent-orchestrator`). The link was surfaced twice — live via `progressListener`, then again in the terminal `result`. The terminal result is now a short, non-duplicative nudge when the link was already shown live.

**3. Share the Remote Control login credential across flows** (`agent-orchestrator`). It was keyed by the per-caller `identity.subject`, but triage (gateway shared-bearer subject) and chat (per-user JWT `sub`) resolve different subjects for the same human — so linking in one flow forced a re-link in the other. Every `claude-remote` call now routes through one `SHARED_REMOTE_CONTROL_SUBJECT` (`linkSubjectFor`). Every other provider stays strictly per-user.

**4. Stop the false "no open pull request was found" warning** (`claude-code-swe-agent`). On a first, marker-less turn the repo is cloned *during* the turn, so `priorHeadSha` is null and the old `madeNewCommits` check read true just because a repo now existed — even when the agent only read it (e.g. to file an issue). Now, when there's no prior HEAD, "did we commit" is measured as commits past the clone's default-branch tip (`origin/HEAD..HEAD`), so a read-only turn stays silent while a genuine commit+PR still shows ✅ and a commit-without-PR still warns.

## What is explicitly NOT touched

- **Triage flow** (`issues.labeled`) — the reference behavior. Continuation/review-only turns keep the exact HEAD-diff behavior (they have a prior HEAD). Proven by existing tests.
- **opencode preview page / live tunnel** (ADR 0025/0026).

## Testing

- `agent-orchestrator`: 339 tests pass, typecheck clean. Added streaming RC-URL test; updated the auth-timeout test (de-duplicated result) and the multi-provider identity-gate tests (`claude` per-user vs `claude-remote` shared subject).
- `claude-code-swe-agent`: 23 tests pass, typecheck clean. Added real-git integration tests for `countCommitsAheadOfOriginHead`.

body:
## What

Files the **approved** Epic B B2 build design — spec + decision only, no implementation code. Implementation is a follow-up, gated on #656 merging and this change being approved. (Matches the repo pattern of committing an OpenSpec change to main early at 0/N tasks.)

Owner-confirmed engine choice: **weighted-LPA** (rebalance edge weights on the existing LPA); **Leiden deferred** as a gated future fork.

## Why (measured, in #656)

The community partition clusters by entity **type**, not **theme** — proven by the white-box co-location diagnostic in #656 (`colocation_mean=0.60`; theme-spanning queries scatter because entity-id sibling/system-peer virtual edges dominate the LPA vote mass: sibling 10×0.7=7.0 + system-peer 15×0.3=4.5 vs explicit 1–3×1.0). B2 adds ephemeral semantic **mutual-kNN** virtual edges, weighted to compete with the structural edges, embedding-readiness-gated, strictly additive over an always-committing structural floor.

## Contents

author: yansun1996
body:
## What this fixes

A job whose `WorkDir` does not exist on the assigned compute node could drain the node — and, because the job then requeues onto other nodes, drain node after node across the partition until it hit `JobHoldMaxRequeue`. A single user's bad `WorkDir` could take a large fraction of a partition offline.

## Root cause

`run_hook` set the prolog/epilog child process's working directory to the job's submitted `work_dir`. That path may only exist on the *submitting* node. When it is absent — or present but not traversable — on the compute node, `Command::spawn()` fails at `chdir()` before the hook script ever runs. spurd classifies this spawn failure as a hook execution failure and drains the node, even though the node and the hook are perfectly healthy.

The failure signature is a fast (~1ms) "script failed to execute" with nothing written by the script body, and a node draining with `Reason=prolog failed: ... script failed to execute`.

## Approach

Fix it at the shared root in `run_hook`: attempt to spawn the hook in `work_dir`, and retry from `/tmp` on any spawn failure. This mirrors `slurmstepd`, which does the same for the job process itself (`chdir(cwd)` falling back to `/tmp`). Attempting the spawn and falling back — rather than pre-checking the path with a `stat` — is deliberate: it also covers a directory that exists but isn't traversable (permissions, NFS `root_squash`) and avoids a TOCTOU window a pre-check would leave open. A spawn failure that still persists from `/tmp` (a missing or non-executable script) surfaces as a real error, so genuine hook problems are not masked. `SPUR_JOB_WORK_DIR` continues to report the submitted path, so a hook that needs the intended location can still act on it — only the process CWD falls back.

Because the fix lives in the shared hook runner, it covers every hook type in one place — prolog/epilog on the node, and `prolog_slurmctld`/`epilog_slurmctld` on the controller, where a compute-node `WorkDir` may never exist locally.

Genuine hook failures (script present, valid CWD, non-zero exit) still surface as failures and still drain, unchanged.

## Why run from /tmp rather than fail the job

The issue title frames this as "drains node instead of failing job," but the fix intentionally does neither: it runs the job (and the hook) from `/tmp` and keeps the node up. This is deliberate, for parity with Slurm, which spur targets for CLI/API compatibility:

- When a job's working directory is missing on the compute node, Slurm's `slurmstepd` chdir's into it and, on failure, falls back to `/tmp` and continues — the job runs, it is not failed, and the node is not drained.
- Slurm never runs the node prolog in the job's `WorkDir` at all: the directory is passed only as the `SLURM_JOB_WORK_DIR` environment variable, and drain-on-prolog-failure is keyed on the script's exit code, not on a chdir at spawn.

So a missing/bad `WorkDir` is a user-side path error that, in Slurm, never takes a node offline. The real defect here is that spurd let user-supplied input (the `WorkDir`) determine whether a hook could even spawn, and then treated that spawn failure as a node-health fault. Matching Slurm's actual behavior — run from `/tmp`, never drain for a user path error — is the correct outcome; failing the job instead would diverge further from Slurm, not less.

## Tests

- A hook run against a nonexistent `work_dir` now succeeds instead of failing to spawn.
- A hook run against an existing-but-non-traversable `work_dir` (mode `000`, as with `root_squash`) also succeeds via the `/tmp` retry — a case a `stat`-based check would miss.
- A hook whose CWD falls back to `/tmp` still exposes the submitted path via `SPUR_JOB_WORK_DIR`.
- A hook that runs in an accessible `work_dir` uses it as-is.
- A genuinely missing/non-executable script still errors after the `/tmp` retry, so real failures aren't masked.

Validated end-to-end on an isolated 2-node deployment: with this change, a job submitted with a nonexistent `WorkDir` runs to completion and the node stays `IDLE`; without it, the same job drains the node with the reported signature. The non-traversable case likewise keeps the node up.

author: chrisagrams
body:
## Problem

zlib has been compiled **without `-O3`** since v1.0.11, silently dropping single-file
compression throughput by ~20–24%.

`vendor/ZlibInclude.cmake` invokes zlib's `configure` with an explicit
`env "CFLAGS=-fPIC ..."`. zlib's `Makefile.in` sets its optimization via
**conditional assignment**:

```make
CFLAGS   ?= -O3
```

`?=` only applies when `CFLAGS` is unset. By exporting `CFLAGS` in the environment,
the invocation **suppressed zlib's default `-O3`**, so zlib was built with `-fPIC`
and **no optimization**. Since mscompress spends heavily in zlib inflate/deflate on
spectrum binaries, this dragged throughput down across the board.

Introduced in `7b4fc39` ("Zlib fix + slim down action") — the `-fPIC` was a legitimate
static-link fix, but it clobbered `-O3` as collateral. The macOS branch
(`CFLAGS=-Dfdopen=fdopen`) has the same latent bug.

## Fix

Prepend `-O3` to the explicit `CFLAGS` on both the Linux and macOS `configure`
invocations, preserving the existing `-fPIC` / `-Dfdopen` flags.

## Evidence

Bisected on a quiet aarch64 box (GB10, 20-core; merlin's shared x86 was too noisy to
see the signal). Single 369 MiB DIA mzML, `-t 20`, warm cache, interleaved reps.

Regression located by `git bisect run` (throughput predicate, threshold 700 MB/s):
first bad commit = `7b4fc39`, throughput 727 → 645 MB/s.

Two clean from-scratch v1.0.16 builds differing **only** in this flag:

| build            | zlib CFLAGS      | min       | median    |
|------------------|------------------|-----------|-----------|
| as-shipped       | `-fPIC`          | 602 MB/s  | 551 MB/s  |
| **with fix**     | `-O3 -fPIC`      | **744 MB/s** | **644 MB/s** |

**+24% (min) / +17% (median)** — recovers v1.0.16 back to the pre-regression
(v1.0.6 ≈ 735 MB/s) level.

## Correctness

- Output unchanged: compression ratio 0.4073, identical before/after.
- `ctest`: 100% passed (43/43).
- Build-only change; no source touched, orthogonal to any in-flight source work.

author: ivan-orekhov
body:
## Problem

[KTL-4744](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KTL-4744)

The search page renders two `SearchField` instances — the main one in the hero block and a compact one in the sticky bar shown after scrolling past the main filter. In non-category mode the compact instance was wired with `onChange={undefined}`, so typing there never triggered the search and only Enter worked; to users this looked like an intermittent "search ignores typing" bug, depending on which of the two visually identical fields they typed in.

When a search did fire while scrolled down, the results swap collapsed the page height, the browser clamped the scroll to top, the sticky bar unmounted mid-typing, and focus (plus un-flushed debounced text) was lost.

## Changes

- **`SearchField` is now fully controlled**: the query text lives in the parent, so both bars always render the same text and none of it is lost when one of them unmounts. Debouncing moves to the callers via a new shared `useDebouncedCallback` hook (invokes the latest callback, exposes `cancel()`).
- **Compact bar triggers search-as-you-type** — wired to the same handler as the main field.
- **Focus handoff**: when results replace the content and the page ends up at the top, the sticky bar hands focus (caret at the end) and text over to the main field, so typing continues seamlessly.
- **Scroll behavior**: typing-driven URL updates use `scroll: false`; sort/tag/platform/mode changes keep the default scroll-to-top. Enter commits the search immediately (cancels the pending debounce). Escape/Clear on an empty field stays a no-op.
- **Navbar**: search input got its own controlled state; suggestion fetches are debounced, skipped for an empty query, and cancelled on Enter navigation.
- **Test**: Playwright regression test — typing in the compact bar triggers the search without Enter, and the focus handoff preserves the text.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `next lint` clean.
- `tests/search.spec.ts`: 8/8 passing (incl. the new regression test) against a local dev server with the production API.
- Full Playwright suite: 72 passed; the 8 failures in `category-page`/`package_page`/`project_page_labels` are pre-existing on a clean checkout (they expect the internal test API dataset, which is VPN-only).

author: tryanks
body:
Closes #114.

A main-thread-blocking audit (26 sites catalogued) found the GPUI thread doing synchronous disk I/O and subprocess work across session switching, streaming, terminal, and settings paths. This PR root-fixes the hot ones; everything converted follows the existing `blocking::unblock` + `cx.spawn` + generation-guard pattern.

## Session timeline loads (#114)

Switching to, reopening, or background-loading a session read and folded its **entire JSONL history synchronously** on the GPUI thread — a visible hitch on every switch for long sessions.

- Sessions install immediately (parked sessions keep their in-memory snapshot; cold opens start empty) and the folded timeline swaps in from a background read, guarded by a per-session load generation.
- A JSONL **append watermark** detects events appended while a background read was in flight (parked sessions with live turns keep appending) and re-reads, bounded — raced events can never be silently dropped.
- Orchestrate `status`/`result` answer from in-memory timelines when the child is loaded, and batch remaining disk reads into one background task replying through the broker channel.
- Idle-child reaper, child-callback fold, and all synchronous `.git/HEAD` probes moved off-thread.

## Store writes → single FIFO background writer

Every store write was synchronous: one JSONL append **per agent event** during streaming, full sessions-index read/parse/rewrite per `persist_meta`, transcript copies on fork, `terminal-ui.json` rewrites throughout resize drags, and settings/secrets saves.

- One FIFO `async_channel` drained by a single writer task owns all store mutations; index ops keep read-modify-write merge semantics inside the writer.
- In-memory state stays authoritative and updates synchronously; the writer is durability-only.
- Fork waits for the transcript clone before opening the fork.
- Write failures surface through the same `RuntimeError` notices via a report pump; the quit hook drains the writer through a barrier before exiting.

## One-shot blocking sites

Preview port scan (up to ~720 ms of sequential connect timeouts per click), `git worktree remove` on session delete (seconds), image paste/drop (metadata size check **before** reading, then read+transcode+write in one background task with slot reservation), orchestrate dispatch `canonicalize`, ACP registry cache read, install-source canonicalize, AI-title scratch dirs (ran on the main thread inside a gpui *local* task), plan saves, typed-path `is_dir`, profile home creation.

## PTY spawn + secrets

Terminal open/restart/new/split allocated the PTY and spawned the shell synchronously (tens of ms per action). Spawns now run behind a pending-spawn registry with session/workspace re-validation on completion; closing the drawer cancels in-flight spawns; the thread-local cwd override is resolved on the calling thread; the macOS openpty serialization from #148 is untouched. `secrets.json` reads (provider start, probes, version checks, model catalogs) moved into `unblock`; mutations go through the FIFO writer and never log values.

## Audited, deliberately left synchronous

- `provider_probe.rs` Codex `auth.json` read — one small local file; async-fs pools are unsafe inside gpui local tasks (see `crates/runtime/src/blocking.rs`).
- `ProviderDialog::new` env read-back — once per dialog open.

## Out of scope (different pattern — render is synchronous, needs caching not offloading)

#154 — per-row `canonicalize()` and per-link `exists()` probes in chat/diff/markdown renderers.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --locked` (682 passed, 5 ignored) — including new regression tests: async timeline install + stale-completion discard + watermark retry, FIFO write ordering, fresh-store visibility, fork-after-clone, async dispatch cwd resolution, async terminal install with cwd override, secret round-trip.

author: jdcrayme
body:
This pull request introduces a highly robust and realistic flight path navigation controller.

1. **PD Controller:** A Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller ($K_p = 0.00025, K_d = 0.00025$) replaces the purely proportional cross-track steering logic in both `NavigateTaskNode` and legacy `runWaypoint`. This successfully damps the lateral flight path oscillations and eliminates overshooting.
2. **Heading Error Blending:** To prevent the abrupt jump/step-change in cross-track error when passing a waypoint, a smooth blending factor based on heading alignment with the target course is introduced. Cross-track corrections are completely zeroed out during steep turns ($>45^\circ$) and are smoothly phased back in as the aircraft aligns with the new course, providing elegant and physically realistic autopilot turns.
3. **Capture Radius Sync:** Exposes a public `captureRadius()` getter in `DigiBrain` so the behavior tree's `WaypointCaptureCheckNode::onTick` can dynamically query the configured capture radius.

All unit tests and integration scenarios pass successfully with exceptionally tight altitude hold and lateral tracking performance.

author: alexander-turner
body:
Risk tier: medium

## What & why

The auto-resolve-merge-conflicts resolver silently dropped any PR whose author is a bot. Its discover step's emit filter carried `((.author.is_bot) | not)`, so a conflict-blocked PR opened by the Claude GitHub App (`claude[bot]`) was **labeled** `merge-conflict` by the labeler but then **never resolved** — the label promised an action the resolver refused. In this repo the bulk of PRs are opened by automation, so that gap meant the resolver rarely fired on the very PRs it exists to unblock (concretely: #2550 sat `dirty`/CONFLICTING with a `merge-conflict` label and no resolve run).

This removes the bot rail from the discover filter (and from the parallel undecided-count filter it mirrored). The other rails are unchanged:

- **Fork rail kept** — `isCrossRepository == false` still excludes cross-repo (untrusted-author) PRs, whose tokens are read-only anyway.
- **Draft rail kept** — draft PRs are still skipped.
- **`auto-resolve-blocked` opt-out kept** — a bot PR carrying that label is still excluded.

Safety net unchanged: a resolved head is re-validated by CI + human review before it can merge, and the resolver only comments when it actually pushes something.

`author` is dropped from the queried `--json` field set (the filter no longer reads it).

## Review focus

- `.github/scripts/auto-resolve-discover.sh` — the emit filter and the undecided-count filter both drop `((.author.is_bot) | not)`; the fork/draft/blocked rails remain. `author` is dropped from the `fields=` `--json` request.
- `.github/workflows/auto-resolve-conflicts.yaml` — header comment updated to reflect that bot authors are now eligible.
- `.github/scripts/auto-resolve-discover.test.mjs` — the script's **existing** colocated suite, updated for this change: the `pr()` fixture factory drops `author` (satisfying the key-set contract test, which derives the expected keys from the script's `fields=` line), the push-scan test flips the bot PR from *dropped* to *emitted*, and the nested-shape guard narrows to the surviving `.labels[].name` read.

## How it was tested

`node --test .github/scripts/auto-resolve-discover.test.mjs` → 6 passed:
- push scan emits eligible CONFLICTING PRs and drops draft/fork/mergeable/blocked (a bot-opened PR is now among the emitted, since author is no longer fetched or filtered);
- `auto-resolve-blocked` PR dropped;
- no eligible PRs → empty array;
- UNKNOWN re-queried until it settles to CONFLICTING;
- the two field-shape contract tests (top-level key set == `fields=`; `.labels[].name` nested shape).

## Decisions made

**Fully removed the rail rather than allowlisting a specific bot.** An allowlist of `claude[bot]` alone would close the immediate gap while still excluding future trusted automation; removing the rail treats every same-repo, non-draft, non-blocked bot PR uniformly. The fork rail (the actual untrusted-author boundary) is what carries the trust guarantee, so third-party same-repo automation (e.g. a future dependabot) would also become eligible — but such PRs are typically lockfile/manifest conflicts that hit the resolver's pre-LLM "unmergeable → human handoff" path, and any resolved head is still gated by CI + human review before merge.

**Updated the existing `.mjs` suite instead of adding a second harness.** The first cut of this PR added a parallel `tests/test_auto_resolve_discover.py` under the mistaken premise that the discover filter had no coverage. It does — `.github/scripts/auto-resolve-discover.test.mjs` is the contract-guarded canonical suite. A second, same-script suite in another language is exactly the rebuild-what-exists / cross-language-drift smell the repo discourages, so the Python file was removed and the `.mjs` suite updated in place (commit `c35bbb7de`).

## Lessons Learned

- **A label applied by one job but honored by another can silently promise an action the second job refuses.** *What*: the merge-conflict labeler labels every CONFLICTING PR, but the auto-resolver's discover step re-filtered by author and dropped bots — so the label implied "will be auto-resolved" for a class the resolver skipped. *Where*: any two-stage "flag it / act on it" automation split across jobs with independent eligibility predicates. *Why*: the flag's audience reads it as a promise; when the actor's filter is stricter than the flagger's, the gap is invisible until someone notices the flagged item never moves. Keep the actor's eligibility predicate identical to the flagger's, or have the flagger apply the same exclusions.

author: danipopes
body:
Internal function declarations now lower to stable nonzero IDs, and calls through function-typed expressions use one shared MIR dispatcher per parameter and return shape. Dispatch targets are collected during lowering, while invalid or uninitialized pointers use Solidity panic `0x51`. Bare virtual function values resolve to the most-derived override, while explicitly qualified base functions retain their declared target.

This follows solc via-IR's ID-and-dispatch model without duplicating the dispatch CFG at every dynamic call site. Constant selectors specialize before helper-local inlining, and a narrow late pass propagates transparent assembly casts once frame-slot promotion exposes their IDs. That handles the view-to-pure cast used by `console.sol` without rerunning broad inlining, while stored or selected runtime values retain the shared helper.

Ambiguous MIR call targets print as `{name}{id}` instead of positional `fnN` references, while declared function names remain unchanged. Focused built-MIR fixtures pin returned, selected, aggregate-loaded, constructor-stored, void, public-target, multi-argument, multi-return, and cast pointers. Runtime checks cover higher-order calls, base and virtual inheritance targets, valid calls, and distinguish invalid-pointer panic `0x51` from arithmetic panic `0x11`.

The focused devirtualization pass reduced Seaport codegen from 1,107.9 ms to 929.6 ms compared with the prior dispatcher-cloning implementation on the same CodSpeed runner; the other 98 benchmarks were unchanged.

author: copilot
body:
The `build-pyodide` CI job has been failing consistently because `_copy_bins()` cannot find the z3 executable after a successful cmake build.

**Root cause**: `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.pyodide.build]` sets `ldflags = "... -sSIDE_MODULE=1"`. pyodide-build injects this into the environment `LDFLAGS`, which cmake propagates to `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS`. The z3 shell target is therefore linked as a WASM side-module — emscripten emits a `.wasm` file whose name doesn't match any of the expected paths (`z3.wasm`, `z3.js.wasm`, `z3`):

```
error: Could not find any executable in build directory. Tried:
- .../build/z3.wasm
- .../build/z3.js.wasm
- .../build/z3
```

**Fix** — `src/api/python/setup.py`:

- **`_configure_z3()`**: pass `Z3_BUILD_EXECUTABLE=FALSE` to cmake when `IS_PYODIDE`, so the shell target is never built
- **`_copy_bins()`**: guard BINS_DIR creation and executable copy behind `if not IS_PYODIDE`
- **`setup()`**: set `data_files=[]` for Pyodide builds (no executable to package)

The z3 CLI isn't usable in a Pyodide environment anyway — Python users only need `libz3.so` via ctypes, which continues to be built and packaged correctly. Non-Pyodide builds (Linux/macOS/Windows) are unaffected.

author: mattn
body:
Adds an `algia group` command for NIP-29 relay-based groups — Slack-like channels hosted on a relay (e.g. Block's [Buzz](https://github.com/block/buzz)). Builds on the NIP-42 pre-auth from #29 (now merged).

## Commands
- `group list` — list groups (kind 39000 metadata)
- `group timeline --id <group-id>` — past messages (kind 9, `#h`)
- `group stream --id <group-id>` — live messages (kind 9)
- `group post --id <group-id> <msg>` — post a message (kind 9 + `h` tag)
- `group delete --id <group-id> <event-id>...` — delete via moderation event (kind 9005); one target per event, as NIP-29 relays require
- `group react --id <group-id> --target <msg-id> [--content +]` — react (kind 7 + `h` tag)

## Notes
- Group id is the `h`-tag value (the `d`-tag on the 39000 metadata).
- Writes authenticate via preAuth + `PublishMany` reactive auth.
- NIP-09 kind 5 does not work for group content and plain `like`/`delete` lack the `h` tag + auth, hence dedicated subcommands. Buzz's NIP-11 lists no NIP-18, so repost is intentionally omitted.

All read/write paths verified live against `wss://vim-jp.communities.buzz.xyz`. (Replaces #30, which auto-closed when its stacked base branch was deleted on merge of #29.)

author: jimeh
body:
Five committed test suites are assigned to no CI runner, so roughly 33
assertions have no regression protection. Green CI does not currently mean
what the committed suite implies — and the gap sits directly on the surface
that the upcoming unload-protocol (C001) and shutdown (C010) work will change.

The Node runner excludes the `browser`, `electron-browser`, and `electron-main`
layers, and the Electron runner loads only what this workflow enumerates by
hand. A suite missing from that list runs nowhere and fails nothing.

Suites wired up:

- `src/vs/hucode/test/browser/omniConfigurationService.test.ts`
- `src/vs/hucode/test/browser/projectSwitcher/openProjectSwitcherTarget.test.ts`
- `src/vs/hucode/test/electron-main/omniWorkspaceOpen.test.ts`
- `src/vs/hucode/test/electron-main/omniWorkspaceReopen.test.ts`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/test/electron-browser/overlayManager.test.ts`

## Verification

All five pass. Verified against the **full 34-suite Electron list**, not in
isolation — suites that have never shared a runner can leak state into each
other:

```
415 passing (943ms), 0 failing
```

Each of the six new suite headings was confirmed present in that run, so
nothing was silently skipped.

## Scope

Replacing the hand-maintained enumeration with layer-appropriate globs or a
completeness guard is **A2**, deliberately left out so this wiring can land on
its own.

`AGENTS.md` gains two notes that cost time to rediscover: local Electron runs
need `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1` (chrome-sandbox must be root-owned mode 4755,
and only CI does that with `sudo`), and the hand-maintained list is why a
committed suite can run nowhere.

Item **A1**, phase 1 — see `docs/hucode/hardening-plan.md`. Covers candidate
**C005** (partial; A2 covers the remainder).

author: fohte
body:
## Purpose

- Allow linking a GitHub account so tq can eventually manage GitHub issues/PRs as tasks

## Approach

- Implement GitHub OAuth App connection using the same OAuth flow shape as the existing Google Calendar connection, with connect/disconnect in the settings page

<details>
<summary>Design decisions</summary>

#### Representing GitHub's missing refresh_token / expires_at

| Decision | Design | Pros | Cons |
| -------- | ------ | ---- | ---- |
| Adopted  | Make `oauth_tokens.refresh_token` / `expires_at` nullable, and add a CHECK constraint keeping them required for `google_calendar` rows | Enforces the required fields for existing providers (`google_calendar`) at the DB level | Requires altering existing columns |
| Rejected | Store a dummy refresh token or a far-future `expires_at` for GitHub rows too | No schema change needed | Fakes values that don't actually exist, leaving meaningless data in the table |

#### Handling a token revoked on GitHub's side

| Decision | Design | Pros | Cons |
| -------- | ------ | ---- | ---- |

author: sohamsave07
body:
Bumps `Flask` from `1.0` to `3.1.3` to resolve [GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726) / CVE-2026-27205 (Dependabot alert #14, low severity — Flask wasn't setting `Vary: Cookie` in all cases where session data is read, which can leak session-specific responses through shared caches).

Since Flask 1.0 → 3.1.3 is a 2-major-version jump, this also bumps everything Flask actually needs to run on that version:
- `Flask-RESTful` 0.3.3 → 0.3.10 (0.3.3 imports a private Flask helper that was removed in Flask 2.2+, so the app wouldn't even start otherwise)
- `Werkzeug`, `Jinja2`, `MarkupSafe`, `itsdangerous`, `click`, `blinker`, `aniso8601`, `six` → versions compatible with modern Flask/Python

**Extra fix needed to keep the app working:** `requirements.txt` already had `SQLAlchemy>=1.3.0` unpinned, which resolves to SQLAlchemy 2.x today. SQLAlchemy 2.x no longer accepts raw strings in `Connection.execute()` — independent of the Flask bump, this was already going to break on a fresh install. I wrapped the 4 raw SQL strings in `app.py` with `sqlalchemy.text(...)` so the app actually runs; verified `GET /departments` returns 200 with real data from `salaries.db`.

**Not fixed here, flagging for visibility:** those same 4 queries build SQL by string-formatting the URL path segments (`department_name`, `pos_name`, `name`) directly into the query text — that's a SQL injection vulnerability, separate from the Dependabot alert this PR addresses. Happy to fix in a follow-up (parameterized queries) if wanted.

author: blackhill24
body:
Closes #119

The issue's premise was that the offline suite could not see the bugs that kept
shipping — `2153 passed, 0 failed` survived breaking `_api_constant` outright — and
that fixing each symptom individually is what let the class survive five consecutive
"fix" commits. So this attacks the class, and then measures whether it worked.

## The root cause, and the fix for it

Production code probes the Resolve bridge with `_has_method()` and `_api_constant()`.
`_has_method` tests `dir()`, because the bridge fabricates a callable for any
attribute name. A `MagicMock`'s `dir()` lists only the children a test has *touched*,
so every method a test did not explicitly configure reads as **absent**: the gate
closes, production takes its fallback, and the test asserts on the fallback having
never executed the path it was written for.

`tests/bridge_double.py` is the one faithful `PyRemoteObject` double — `dir()` =
methods only, `getattr` fabricates `None`, `hasattr` always `True`, constants answer
via `getattr`. `tests/core/test_bridge_double_fidelity.py` pins all four, and
additionally asserts a MagicMock gets both probes *wrong*, so making the double
mock-shaped fails loudly instead of silently going green everywhere.

## All 12 fix-plan items

| # | What landed |
|---|---|
| 1 | `tests/bridge_double.py` + the repo's first `tests/conftest.py` |
| 2 | Fidelity meta-test, incl. `MagicMockIsUnfaithfulTest` |
| 3 | `pytest.ini` — the `test_*.py` / `live_*.py` split is now a declared contract |
| 4 | Gate coverage in the domains §2 measured at zero; `autospec=` on helper patches |
| 5 | All 51 hand-rolled doubles audited; finding pinned by a guard test |
| 6 | `_has_method`/`_api_constant` de-duplicated + a structural identity guard |
| 7 | Export-path regression tests binding the copy the export path actually uses |
| 8 | `expected_status` asserts instead of declares |
| 9 | Eleven `_record_tool_result` copies collapsed into one helper |
| 10 | Both always-pass harnesses fixed |
| 11 | Guard: every `live_*.py` has a reachable nonzero exit |
| 12 | `scripts/mutation_gate.py`, wired into the publish workflow |

## Definition of done — measured

| mutation | issue baseline | now |
|---|---|---|
| break only `granular/common._api_constant` | 0 failed | **3 failed** |
| break only `granular/common._has_method` | 0 failed | **2 failed** |
| `_has_method -> True` | 10 failed, 10 files | **40 failed, 11 files** |
| `_has_method -> False` | 32 failed | **57 failed** |
| re-introduce `cc007ef` | 6 failed, 1 file | **14 failed, 4 files** |

- Offline suite: 2153 -> **2306 passed, 0 failed**.
- `scripts/mutation_gate.py`: **6/6 mutations killed**.
- Live suite: **50 PASS / 4 SKIP / 0 FAIL** on Resolve Studio 21.0.2.4 — back at
  baseline, with exactly the 4 documented SKIPs.
- `live_duplicate_clips_validation.py --output-dir` and `live_script_smoke.py` were
  verified by failure injection: both return nonzero when a step fails, and the
  latter no longer reads stdin.

## Three things found beyond the issue's own audit

1. **The live suite caught a conflation in the task-8 fix, on its first run.**
   `probe_interchange_roundtrip` *succeeds*, and the probe then compares the
   re-imported timeline against the original and finds lost media links — so "the
   call worked" and "the capability works" genuinely differ, and the recorder cannot
   see the difference. That was written as `expected_status="partially_supported"`,
   which the new assertion correctly read as a falsified claim. `classify_as=` +
   a mandatory `classification_reason` now separates an evidence-backed downgrade
   from a claim. It is one-directional by construction: it may only move a
   *supported* observation down, never launder a failure into a pass.
2. **§5 said two always-pass harnesses; a cruder first version of the guard flagged
   five.** Three were false positives — `live_fuse_diagnose`, `live_fuse_smoke` and
   `live_path_probe` all reach `sys.exit(1)` inside `main()`, and two more fail by
   raising `AssertionError`. The guard now models both as real exit paths and
   discounts a `raise` inside a swallowed `try`. Only the two named in §5 were broken.
3. **`_requires_method` is a third duplicated helper the issue did not list**, but
   the copies genuinely differ — the granular one returns the legacy flat
   `{"error": str}` shape while `envelope`'s returns the structured envelope — so
   collapsing them would change the granular error contract. Left alone deliberately;
   it already calls the shared `_has_method`.

## What was deliberately not done

The issue's "Scope not yet covered" list (vacuous-assertion sweep across all 234 test
files, per-module coverage numbers, mutation-testing the drift guards, cross-test
pollution, `resolve-advanced/`) is untouched — it is explicitly follow-up work.

author: marius-cetanas
body:
> Written by an implementer agent (Claude Opus 5) under the supervised-build protocol, and opened
> under the maintainer's credentials because the `portulan-agent` App is deliberately refused
> repository-contents read and therefore cannot open a pull request. Conversation below comes from
> `portulan-agent[bot]`. See [`.portulan/gate-map.md`](.portulan/gate-map.md), "Which identity acts".

Milestone 3, session 1. The fresh-machine install was meant to be a demonstration. It was a defect
report.

## The finding

```
$ claude plugin details portulan          # installed from the remote, empty config dir
Component inventory
  Skills (3)  clarify, codify, portulan
  Agents (0)
```

Three agent files shipped in the cache. `plugin-lint` counted three. `claude plugin validate --strict`
exited 0. The persona-binding criterion had been ticked in session 0. Every one of those was true and
the personas were inert on every install anyone had ever done.

**The defect is not in any file**, which is why session 0's checkpoint missed it while doing exactly the
right thing — it measured the first-party validator's coverage by forcing reds, and every red it forced
was inside a file. This one lives between a manifest and a loader, and only an install shows it.

A seven-form fixture matrix, **with a positive control**, established the mechanism. The control is the
part worth copying: `Agents (0)` alone cannot distinguish *"the personas did not load"* from *"this
command does not count agents"*, and a second throwaway plugin reporting `Agents (1)` from the same
command in the same minute is what made it a measurement rather than a reading.

| `agents` declaration | plugin loads | registered |
|---|---|---|
| **absent**, files at `./agents/` | yes | **1 — the control** |
| absent, files at `./plugin/agents/` | yes | 0 |
| `["./agents/probe.md"]` explicit file, default path | yes | 0 |
| `["./plugin/agents/implementer.md", …]` ← what this repository shipped | yes | **0** |
| `["./agents/"]` · `["./plugin/agents/"]` · `["./plugin/agents"]` | **fails to load at all** | — |

Row 3 is the one that matters: the same files, in the place the host reads, register nothing once a key
names them. **The key does not fail to help — it suppresses the scan that works.**

## The fix, and the alternative that is worth recording as refused

`git mv plugin/agents/*.md agents/`, and the `agents` key is gone. That is the platform's default agents
directory, which for a plugin rooted at this repository is the repository root.

**Re-rooting the plugin at `plugin/` is the tempting alternative and it is wrong**: the installed payload
is the plugin root's subtree, so that plugin would ship skills and agents and *not* `core/` — and the
install exists to deliver the engine. A symlink `agents/ → plugin/agents/` was also built, and worked
through two of the three install paths; it was rejected because the third — a clone from the remote —
was never measured, which makes it an untested behaviour resting on a platform quirk.

`docs/plan.md`'s topology block is amended to match, on the maintainer's explicit delegation, and the
annotation carries the constraint's provenance so the location does not read as taste.

**Verified from a real install, not from `--plugin-dir`:** marketplace add plus install into a versioned
cache reports `Skills (3)` and `Agents (3)  reviewer, librarian, implementer`, with
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/core/engine.md` readable at 43 lines — one check confirming both the repo-rooted
decision and this fix.

## Two fail-opens the fix itself opened, both closed here

1. **The recipe printed `0 agent(s)` and GREEN** the moment nothing declared them. The milestone
   criterion asks that CI check *"every declared skill and agent"*; for agents the manifest cannot carry
   the claim at all. `plugin-lint` now finds them by convention, **fails** on a present `agents` key, and
   asserts this repository's count of three against the tree.
2. **The `map` check could not see a top-level symlink at all** — `awk -F/ 'NF > 1'` yields only
   directories containing tracked files, and git tracks a symlink as one path with no `/`. Found while a
   symlink was briefly the fix; kept after it was not, because the hole is in the check rather than in
   that tree. It is task `0004`'s eighth fail-open, and the fourth whose defect is a *short input set*
   rather than a wrong answer.

## Claims corrected rather than repeated

- **The payload decision rested on a false sentence.** `plugin/README.md` said a local-directory install
  skips symlinks resolving outside the plugin directory. Measured on a committed git fixture with that
  exact shape, **both readings follow the link**. The decision stands anyway, on a reason the record
  never gave: this repository's own lint refuses that shape, so taking the alternative means relaxing the
  check the gate map singles out as the one to scrutinise hardest. A third path is left **explicitly
  unmeasured**, because measuring it means publishing a fixture repository — and one measurement standing
  in for two claims is how the false sentence got written.
- **The bundle ships three workspace manifests, not two.** The third is the deliberately drifted fixture,
  which is the *worse* one to boot on. Counted rather than remembered.
- **Session 0's open question 1 was wrong.** GitHub shorthand needed no
  `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS=1`; the CLI probed SSH and fell back to HTTPS unaided.

## Also here

`CHANGELOG.md`, the first — required by Protocol → Versioning since the plan was locked, and never
produced until a supervisor asked for it. Plus one new memory rule, and tasks `0005` and `0006` created
on the maintainer's instruction for a later session.

## What this does **not** do

**Milestone 3 does not close.** Two things are outstanding and both are recorded unticked rather than
smoothed over:

- **The boot.** It needs a live session, and every one returns `Credit balance is too low` — including a
  control `claude -p` with no plugin loaded, which is how it was classified as an auth failure rather
  than mistaken for a packaging failure.
- **The remote install path.** `Agents (3)` is read from `--plugin-dir` and from a local-path install;
  the clone cannot carry the fix until this merges. Ticking it on the strength of a different install
  path would be this pull request's own defect, one level up.

`v0.1.0` is **not tagged**. The ruling is *fix first, then tag the merge*, so the tag names a commit that
does not exist yet.

## Verification

Five recipes exit 0 · suite **151/151** (146 → 151, red on 9 before the fix, then 1 more) · `plugin-lint`
GREEN, 3 skills / 3 agents · `claude plugin validate --strict` exit 0 · every new check forced red on the
real tree before its green was believed · seam scan clean across files, commit message, and branch name.

**Supervised in three fresh contexts**: session-open (APPROVE-WITH-ADJUSTMENTS, 8 required, 6 changing
the work — *"list what the host actually registered"* is what found `Agents (0)`), and two pre-commit
passes (4 and then 7, the second re-run because the maintainer changed the fix and delegated a topology
amendment). The second pre-commit's work item: **the rejected symlink arrangement passed every check
here** — rebuilt by the supervisor, lint GREEN, map GREEN, suite green — now refused by a
repository-anchored test rather than a rule in the lint, because the platform accepts that shape and a
generic refusal would encode this repository's risk appetite into a tool other plugins run.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
Fixes the "connection refused" 502 error that crashes the app on every request.

**Problems fixed:**
1. **Missing root route**: App had no route for GET /, causing requests to fail
2. **Middleware order bug**: Session middleware was added AFTER static files, but Express session needs to run before routes that use req.session
3. **Hardcoded secrets**: Now uses environment variables for SESSION_SECRET and checks NODE_ENV for secure cookies

**Changes:**
- Add explicit GET / route that serves chat.html
- Move session middleware to run before static files middleware
- Use process.env.SESSION_SECRET instead of hardcoded string
- Set secure cookie flag based on NODE_ENV

author: panagiotiskaraliolios
body:
## AI Layer Phase 3b-i — AI-assisted CSV statement import

Upload an arbitrary broker CSV → an LLM maps its columns onto our canonical transaction schema → review the mapped rows in an editable table (duplicates + bad rows flagged) → click **Import** to write them.

### Design: the LLM is a pure mapper, never a writer

The defining property (verified in the whole-branch review): the model **only** returns a `ColumnMapping` (column indices + a `sideMap` + a `dateFormat`) — it reorders the user's own CSV cells and nothing more. The transaction *data* never originates from the model, and every produced row is re-validated by `validateRow` at preview **and again server-side** at commit.

- The write is a normal session-authenticated `transactions.bulkImport` triggered by the user's Import click — **no signed-token seam** (3a needed one because the *model* initiated that write; here the *user* does).
- The only DB write path (`bulkCreateTransactions`) is reachable **only** from the two session-authed procedures (`importCsv`, `bulkImport`); `aiImport.preview` (the sole place the LLM runs) performs no write.
- Only the CSV header + first 8 sample rows are sent to the model, telemetry recording is off, and the CSV/sample rows are never logged (including on a model error).

### Reuses the existing importer

The branch first **extracts the reusable core** of `transactions.importCsv` (`validateRow`, `resolveUnknownSymbols`, `detectDuplicates`, `bulkCreateTransactions`, `CanonicalRecord`) into `src/server/services/transaction-import.ts`, unchanged in behaviour, and drives it from both the classic importer and the AI flow. 3b-ii (PDF, future) reuses everything from the `CanonicalRecord[]` hand-off onward by swapping only the extractor.

### What's new

- `src/server/ai/import/` — `schema.ts` (`columnMappingSchema`, `applyMapping`, `reformatDate`) + `map-columns.ts` (`mapColumns` via the AI SDK's `generateObject`, mirroring `advice-judge.ts`).
- `src/server/api/routers/ai-import.ts` — `aiImport.preview` (map → classify rows into `ok` / `duplicate` / `needs-fix` → return for review).
- `transactions.bulkImport` — re-validated, re-deduped session-authenticated bulk write.
- `src/app/(dashboard)/import/` — the dedicated `/import` flow (model picker, upload, editable review table, Import).
- `docs/ai-csv-import.md`.

### Testing

`typecheck` 0, `biome` clean, **`test:unit` 438 pass / 0 fail**, **`test:db` 85 pass / 0 fail**. New coverage: `validateRow`, `applyMapping`/`reformatDate`, `mapColumns` (mocked model), `bulkImport` + `previewImport` (real Postgres, incl. cross-user/dedup), `toBulkImportRows`, and a cross-file canonical-order invariant test.

### Review

Built subagent-driven, TDD, with a task review per task and a whole-branch review on the most capable model. The final review confirmed no Critical issues and a sound security composition; its two Important findings (a model-error log that could serialize sample rows; the commit toast dropping failed-row counts) and two Minors are fixed in this branch.

author: kittors
body:
## 背景

对 #811（`56415f64`）做对抗式复查后发现的问题。原修复方向正确、确实关闭了报告的漏洞，但有几处需要纠正。

## 1. 局限说明严重低估了绕过面（最重要）

原注释只列了 L4 中继（nginx `stream`、HAProxy TCP、socat、iptables DNAT、cloudflared）。但**裸的 nginx `proxy_pass` 默认不设置任何转发头**——nginx 只隐式设 `Host` 和 `Connection`，`X-Forwarded-For` 等必须运维显式写 `proxy_set_header`。因此：

```nginx
location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8317; }   # 无 proxy_set_header
```

这个**最常见的同机反代配置**在 HTTP 层与本地客户端完全无法区分，两个受保护端点都照旧敞开。已实测确认：仅带 `Host`/`Connection` 的外部请求，`IsLocalOriginRequest` 返回 true。

前置代理若存在请求走私（CL.TE/TE.CL）漏洞，攻击者可直接构造发往后端的字节流，同样绕过，且**不需要任何运维配置错误**。

注释改为明确写清：这个检查**只是缩小暴露面，并没有关闭它**；需要在敌意网络中站得住的端点必须有自己的凭据。仓库自带的 `docs/reverse-proxy_CN.md` 确实设置了转发头，但没有任何东西强制这一点。

## 2. management 的拒绝提示是错的

原提示说「或把代理加入 trusted-proxies 以恢复真实客户端 IP」，暗示这是一条获得访问权的出路。**但它不是**：`IsLocalOriginRequest` 按设计不看 trusted-proxies，经中继的请求永远不被判为本地。已用 gin 实测：即使把 `trusted-proxies` 配成 `127.0.0.1`，经中继的 loopback 请求仍然 `localClient=false`。

提示改为：`allow-remote=true` 才是授予访问的开关，`trusted-proxies` 是**附加**步骤（让按 IP 的节流看到真实客户端），而不是替代方案。

## 3. 中继头清单存在潜在陷阱

清单里 20 项有 10 项不是 textproto 规范形式（`X-Real-IP` → `X-Real-Ip`、`CF-Ray` → `Cf-Ray`、`X-Azure-ClientIP` → `X-Azure-Clientip` 等）。当前能工作**纯粹因为 `Header.Values()` 会规范化查找键**；一旦有人改成直接 map 索引（仓库里 `gemini-cli_handlers.go` 和 `internal/wsrelay/http.go` 已有这种写法），**半个清单会静默失效**。

改为在初始化时统一规范化，并加两个测试锁定：一个断言清单本身规范，一个断言通过原始 map 直接塞入的头仍能被识别。

## 4. amp 模块存在同根因缺陷，一并迁移

`internal/api/modules/amp/routes.go` 的 `localhostOnlyMiddleware` 用裸 `RemoteAddr` + `IsLoopback()`，没有任何中继头检查，同机反代下每个外部请求都满足。

该处是纵深防御（默认关闭，且后面串了 API key 认证），但属于同一根因，已迁移到共享 helper。

## 5. 拒绝日志无限量，且记录的信息没有用

每个被拒请求都 `log.Warnf` 一行，无采样无限流。而「这个端点正在被扫描」恰恰是产生海量日志的条件，攻击者在读 body 之前就被拒绝、代价极低——这是一条廉价的磁盘填满路径。

更讽刺的是它记录 `RemoteAddr`：在这条警告本来要诊断的反代场景里，`RemoteAddr` **恒为本地代理地址，什么也标识不了**。

改为每分钟最多一行，并把被抑制的条数折进下一行（突发仍然可见）；同时记录 `util.ForwardedClientIP` 得到的真实客户端 IP，并明确标注为 claimed——该值由攻击者控制，不能当作可信证据。

## 验证

本地执行完整 `./scripts/ci-pr.sh`，**退出码 0**。

新增测试：
- 头名规范性 + 通过原始 map 索引设置的头仍被识别；
- 50 次连续被拒请求只产生 1 行日志、抑制计数为 49。

既有测试 `TestIsLocalOriginRequestRejectsRelayedLoopbackPeers` 的断言相应放宽为比较规范形式（`RelayIndicationHeader` 现在返回 `X-Real-Ip` 而非 `X-Real-IP`，这正是 `http.Header` 内部存储的形式，检测行为不变）。

## 未纳入本 PR

- **文档**：`docs/reverse-proxy_CN.md` 与 `config.example.yaml` 仍按旧行为描述，应补充「反代后 management 需要 allow-remote」以及 `proxy_set_header` 的必要性。建议单独出一个文档 PR。
- `internal/api/public_lookup_middleware.go` 与 `identity_auth.go:184` 的限流键仍是裸 `c.ClientIP()`，声明了 trusted-proxies 时可用轮换 `X-Forwarded-For` 规避配额。属独立问题。

影响目录：仅 `CliRelay/`。

Refs #517, #404
