author: turbocoder13
body:
## Summary The auto-rerun safety net burned its full 10-minute job timeout with **zero output** on tooling that already contained #749, and the failed run was never re-run. This reproduces that hang, names its cause, fixes it, and makes the silent-for-ten-minutes state unreachable. **Reproduced, not inferred.** Running the script under `bash -x` with a timestamped `PS4` and the exact env from the issue (`RUN_ID=30202199950 RUN_ATTEMPT=1 MAX_RERUNS=1 SIGNATURES=`) against a `gh` serving a realistic 3 MB failed-job log localises the block to one line and one line only. ### Root cause `[[ -n "${logs//[[:space:]]/}" ]]` — the blank-payload check on the fetched failed-job logs. Bash rebuilds the whole string once per match in `${var//pat/}`, so the cost is O(length x matches). A CI log is roughly one character in six whitespace, so matches scale with length and the check is quadratic in payload size. Measured against a realistic failed-job payload: | payload | old check | | --- | --- | | 1 MB | 21 s | | 4 MB | 147 s | A multi-megabyte failed-job log therefore burns the entire job budget inside a single parameter expansion. Three things follow from that, and together they match the issue's evidence exactly: - **It is inside the shell**, so #743/#749's `timeout` bounds — which wrap `gh` and nothing else — could not see it and correctly did not fire. - **It is on the success path**, where the script logged nothing between a successful fetch and a completed match, which is why the job produced no output at all. - **It is CPU-bound in one bash process**, which is why the runner's orphan cleanup reported a single surviving `bash` and no `gh` or `timeout`. Buffering was ruled out first, as the issue asked: bash builtins write straight through with no stdio buffering, so the absence of log lines is real information and not lost output. ### Fix `payload_has_content` uses a linear glob test that short-circuits at the first non-whitespace character. 64 MB now measures at 0.5 s (0.9 s for the pathological all-whitespace case). The reproduction that previously ran past 240 s completes in 1.6 s and re-runs the failed jobs. ### Beyond the fix - **Silence is unreachable.** An unbuffered start line is written before any validation, sourcing or work, and each phase — plus the fetched payload size — is logged as it begins. - **No stdin.** `exec

Greptile Summary

 The PR replaces the quadratic failed-log blank check and adds progress diagnostics plus an outer watchdog. - Uses a linear glob test to classify fetched log payloads. - Runs the rerun operation in a watchdog-controlled process group and closes inherited stdin. - Documents the watchdog deadline and verifies the timeout ordering and new behavior with Bats tests.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The PR should not merge until the watchdog uses Bash 3.2-compatible descriptor handling or the reusable workflow explicitly rejects runners with older Bash. The default Ubuntu path is covered well, but selecting a permitted macOS runner causes the newly added watchdog syntax to fail during parsing before any rerun work can occur. **Files Needing Attention:** scripts/ci/actions/rerun-on-infra-failure.sh and .github/workflows/reusable-auto-rerun-on-infra-failure.yml

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | scripts/ci/actions/rerun-on-infra-failure.sh | Replaces the quadratic payload check and adds a watchdog, but its dynamic-FD syntax breaks supported caller-selected Bash 3.2 environments. | | .github/workflows/reusable-auto-rerun-on-infra-failure.yml | Documents the watchdog/job-timeout relationship while retaining an unrestricted runner-image contract. | | tests/bats/unit/actions/test_rerun_on_infra_failure.bats | Adds strong regression coverage for large logs, watchdog behavior, diagnostics, stdin isolation, validation, and cleanup, but does not exercise Bash 3.2. | | tests/bats/integration/test_reusable_auto_rerun_on_infra_failure.bats | Adds a contract check ensuring the default watchdog fires before the workflow job timeout. | | docs/reusable-workflows.md | Documents the shell-level hang, progress output, stdin behavior, and watchdog semantics. |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Start and validate environment] --> B[Create watchdog state] B --> C[Launch main in process group] B --> D[Start deadline timer] C --> E[Fetch failed-job logs] E --> F{Payload has content?} F -->|No| E F -->|Yes| G[Match transient signatures] G -->|Match| H[Re-run failed jobs] G -->|No match| I[Exit successfully] D -->|Deadline expires| J[Kill main process group] J --> K[Report last phase and exit successfully] ```

author: yukimemi
body:
Follow-up to #38, which merged with three Windows checks still running.

`main` had no branch protection and therefore no required checks, so `gh pr merge --auto` had nothing to wait for and merged immediately. It reads as "merge when green"; it was in fact "merge now".

## Now required (11 contexts)

`check`, `test` and `clippy` across ubuntu / windows / macos, plus `rustfmt` and `cargo lockfile in sync`.

## Deliberately **not** required

Both look like obvious omissions, so the reasoning is in AGENTS.md rather than only in a settings page:

- **`review`** — `claude-review.yml` has a job-level `if:` skipping release bumps, `kata-apply/auto`, `apm-bump/auto`, Renovate/Dependabot and drafts. A skipped job never reports its context, and a required context that never reports blocks the PR **forever** — on exactly the PRs the repo relies on auto-merging, every release included.
- **`coverage`** — sets `fail_ci_if_error: false` specifically so a flaky Codecov upload can't gate merges. Requiring it takes that back.

## Other settings

| setting | value | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strict` | off | a merge to `main` would otherwise force every other open PR to update first — pure churn with stacked branches |
| `enforce_admins` | off | escape hatch for when CI itself is broken |
| required reviewers | none | solo repo; you cannot approve your own PR, so this would block every merge |

Nothing pushes to `main` directly — `auto-tag.yml` pushes a *tag*, which protection doesn't cover, and `kata-apply` / `apm-bump` open PRs. The protection costs the automation nothing beyond making its `--auto` merges honest.

## This PR is also the test

It is a docs-only change whose purpose is to confirm the gate actually holds: it must sit unmergeable until all eleven contexts report green. If it can be merged early, the configuration is wrong and the finding stands.

author: andresmessina-sdg
body:
The whole shareable arc — SHAREABLE_ARTIFACTS_RESEARCH §X, SA-B, SA-A, SA-C.
Stacked on #17 (the matrix fix), so merge that first or this branch runs the
old harness.

Four new modules, all composition kept free of GTK so they are testable:
`passage_export.py`, `verse_card.py`, `passage_print.py`, and `export_dialog.py`
for the two sheets. Entry points are three rows on the right-click study menu,
beside Copy — the menu already has the selection in hand.

## Decisions, all Andres's
- **Licensing: attribution stamp only.** Every export names its translation,
  mandatory and not removable. The module's copyright string is deliberately
  NOT surfaced, and cards do NOT silently fall back to a PD translation.
- **Citation: SBTS/Turabian**, from the seminary's own short-form guide rather
  than from memory — en dash and never a hyphen, books abbreviated in a
  reference and spelled out in prose, commas between verses and semicolons
  between books, translation after the reference with no comma, `Ps 23` but
  `Pss 23–24`. Abbreviations are the SBL §8 list their manual cites.
- **Cards:** the centred arrangement, chosen from three rendered at 1080px;
  the app's own four light papers; square, portrait and wide; wordmark off by
  default. One look, no template gallery.
- Worksheet defaults to text + the reader's own notes; interlinear, textual
  variants and the fathers' voices are off-by-default toggles.

## Two things measured rather than assumed
**The card render path is cairo, not a widget snapshot** — it needs no display
server, so a card renders identically in a test, on a headless build and in the
app. It is also genuinely cairo, which steps around the GPU glyph clip.

**The Flatpak print gate is CLEARED**, checked inside the installed sandbox:
`org.freedesktop.portal.Print` is present, its `version` answers 4,
`Gtk.PrintOperation` constructs, page setup resolves. No manifest permission
needed. The doc's fallback ("stop at export") is not required.

## Defects found only by looking at the output
Fixtures were green throughout for every one of these:

author: lh0156
body:
Fixes #3704

## Motivation

When Redis shuts down, the connection used to send `SHUTDOWN` is expected to close. The default connection retry policy currently retries the resulting `ConnectionError`, which delays `Redis.shutdown()` by the configured backoff/retry period.

## Solution

- Add an internal per-command no-retry option to the synchronous and asynchronous clients.
- Use it only for `shutdown()`, leaving retry behavior for all other commands unchanged.
- Preserve the existing `ConnectionError` handling that treats the expected disconnect as a successful shutdown.
- Close the failed connection and keep existing operation/error metrics behavior.

## Tests

- Verify sync and async `shutdown()` pass the internal option for NOSAVE, SAVE/NOW/FORCE, and ABORT.
- Verify sync and async command execution performs exactly one attempt even when the connection retry policy allows retries.
- Existing client retry and metrics tests remain green.

Validation:
- `pytest -q tests/test_commands.py -k 'test_shutdown'`
- `pytest -q tests/test_asyncio/test_commands.py -k 'shutdown_disables_command_retries'`
- `pytest -q tests/test_client.py`
- `pytest -q tests/test_asyncio/test_client.py`
- `invoke linters`
- `python -m compileall -q redis ...`

author: andygrove
body:
> **Stacked on #2194** (the GROUP BY-less aggregate fix for #2185), which is merged into this branch so the `aqe-on-p1` leg exercises it. Review that one first; this PR's diff is the matrix alone once #2194 merges. #2183, the previous base, is now merged.
>
> **This PR is expected to be red.** Three of its four legs fail on pre-existing bugs — that is the point of the coverage. It is a live tracker, not a merge candidate, until those are fixed.

# Which issue does this PR close?

Part of #2092.

# Rationale for this change

The TPC-DS gate ran exactly one configuration: the static planner at 16 partitions. The adaptive planner was deliberately left out because it failed many TPC-DS queries with an `EmptyExec invalid partition` assertion, tracked as #2047 — which is now closed. So AQE has no TPC-DS coverage at all, even though #2092 aims to enable it by default. That is the configuration most in need of a correctness gate.

Single-partition execution was also never covered, and it turns out to be where the interesting failures are.

# What changes are included in this PR?

Replaces the single job with a four-leg matrix, following the shape `tpch.yml` already uses:

| Leg | Planner | `--partitions` | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aqe-off-p16` | static | 16 | **passes** (97/99) |
| `aqe-off-p1` | static | 1 | fails |
| `aqe-on-p16` | adaptive | 16 | hangs |
| `aqe-on-p1` | adaptive | 1 | fails |

- Per-leg `label` / `planner_args` / `partitions` / `slug`, matching `tpch.yml`'s convention.
- `fail-fast: false`, so one red leg does not mask the others.
- All legs share one `swatinem/rust-cache` entry via `shared-key: tpcds-sf1`, so the binaries are compiled once and restored by the remaining legs rather than rebuilt four times. This mirrors `tpch.yml`'s `shared-key: tpch-sf10`.
- The cluster-log artifact is named per leg so failures do not collide.

# What the new coverage found

All of these reproduce on `main` and are independent of this PR.

**1. UNION scan restriction is wrong at `target_partitions=1`** (#2184)

| Query | Symptom |
|---|---|
| q5 | expected `73724.99`, got `294899.96` — exactly **4x** |
| q80 | expected `11343.60`, got `22687.20` — exactly **2x** |
| q49 | `Internal("FileStreamBuilder invalid partition index: 0")` |

q5, q80 and q49 are exactly the three affected queries containing `UNION`. #2070 ("map a task's partition through UnionExec when restricting file scans") fixed this precise inflation symptom and states it was verified correct "at every partition count tried (4, 5, 6, 8, 16, 20, 32)" — **1 was never tried**.

A candidate mechanism, in `restrict_plan_to_partitions` (`ballista/scheduler/src/state/task_builder.rs`): the walker passes the parent's partition indices unchanged through interior nodes, then applies them to leaf file scans via `config.file_groups.get(i)`. When an index exceeds the scan's file-group count, `filter_map` silently drops it. An empty `file_groups` is exactly what makes `FileStreamBuilder` reject partition 0, and a *missed* restriction leaves a scan free to read its whole table and inflate the answer. The comment at that call site already notes the non-empty branch is "currently safe because the only shape emitted is `partitions == 1`".

**2. AQE hangs on q16 at 16 partitions**

The leg produced `Query 15 verified against DataFusion: OK` and then no further output for over three hours before being cancelled, against ~7 minutes for a passing leg. Consistent with #2063.

**3. q61 returns 0 rows instead of 1** under AQE at 1 partition (#2185). Fixed by #2194, which this branch now merges in.

**Not bugs:** q47 and q72 exhaust memory at 1 partition. `--memory-pool-size 2GB` split across `--concurrent-tasks 4` gives each task a 476.8 MB fair share, and collapsing to one partition pushes the whole table through a single task. That is workflow tuning, to be addressed when the legs are made green.

# Are there any user-facing changes?

No. CI coverage only.

author: stxtrata
body:
…grid

A tiny HTML inscription that brings no styles of its own — "Library", "Music", a title and nothing else — was rendering on the browser's default white canvas, so it sat in the grid as a white card among black ones. Same content, two different looks, depending only on whether the inscription happened to declare a background.

The grid preview now defaults the canvas to dark. color-scheme is the right tool rather than a background declaration: it moves only the UA DEFAULT, so an inscription that paints its own background keeps it. And the rule is written :where(:root), which is zero specificity, so anything the inscription itself declares wins regardless of source order. It cannot repaint someone's artwork, which on a permanence product is the part that matters.

Verified in a browser on three cases: an unstyled inscription now renders dark with light text; one that paints itself white stays white; one that explicitly declares color-scheme: light keeps its light scheme. Tests cover both the default and the guard.

author: colonistone
body:
## What happened

Langford published this to moltbotden.com today, and I deleted it about an hour later:

> Per-IP token buckets break when agents route through LB/NAT pools—I've measured 40% false-positive throttling. We switched to a signed `X-Agent-ID` header with a leaky bucket in Go. Dropped Firestore overage by 34% and kept p95 latency under 12ms.

There is no Go service, no Firestore, no telemetry and no "we". Fluent, on-topic, correctly threaded, entirely invented.

## Root cause — mine

The compose prompt asked for *"a concrete disagreement, **a measurement**, or **an experience**"*. A model with no instruments was told to supply a measurement and did as it was told.

The prompt now states what Langford is (no services, no logs, no history of having operated anything) and forbids any figure not already in the thread.

## Why the prompt alone isn't the fix

Every existing guard passed this comment, **correctly**: non-empty, not the `PASS` sentinel, no object markers, under the cap, generation not truncated. Those are all checks on **form**. A malformed reply announces itself; a confabulated one is indistinguishable from a good one at the boundary — and it's the one that gets believed.

`langford.grounding` adds two rules, each catching what the other can't:

| rule | catches | blind to |
|---|---|---|
| A — unsourced figures | `40%`, `34%`, `12ms` not present in the thread | numberless claims |
| B — first-person empirical claims | "we switched to…", "I benchmarked…" | figures stated impersonally |

It **refuses**; it never edits. Stripping the invented numbers out would leave a claim nobody wrote.

`REFUSED_UNGROUNDED` is its own decision value rather than `DECLINED_EMPTY_COMPOSE` — one means the model chose silence, the other means it spoke and asserted something it cannot have observed. Collapsing them hides a confabulation rate inside a silence rate.

## Tests

- **Known positive is the real published comment.** If that stops being refused, the guard is gone whatever else is green.
- **Eight must-allow controls.** Three separate over-rejections bit me this week and each was caught only by asserting what must be *permitted*.
- **Both rules mutation-tested independently.** The first attempt used a probe that *both* rules caught, so sabotaging one changed nothing and proved nothing about it — fixed to isolate each.
- **`test_every_decision_value_is_emitted_by_some_fixture`** — verdict coverage, not branch coverage. Added because `REFUSED_UNGROUNDED` slotted into the parametrised list without anything going red. It immediately found `DECLINED_ALREADY_REPLIED` had never been produced by any test.

183 passing.

## Still outstanding

- `eval_grounding.py` A/Bs old prompt vs new against real threads on the same model, posting nothing. **Not yet run** — it waits on the cross-agent GPU lock, currently held by a healthy `dantic`. Unit tests prove the guard behaves on strings I wrote; only this can show the prompt change works on real output.
- `LANGFORD_MOLTBOTDEN_ENABLED` is currently `false` pending the operator's decision.
- **Scope, stated honestly:** this catches invented figures and invented operational history. It cannot see plausible qualitative fabrication.

author: cliangdev
body:
## Why

Two problems in the same part of the app: queued work was invisible and unmanageable, and the workflow detail page had three overlapping tabs.

Investigating what actually queues turned up something more useful than "add a queue view". **A run sitting in `PENDING` is a symptom, not a backlog** — the engine drains its job queue on a 500ms tick, so `PENDING` is normally sub-second. The real waiting happens elsewhere, and it was invisible in two different ways:

| What happens | Where it lived | Visible before? |
|---|---|---|
| Job handed to a self-hosted daemon | job `AWAITING_PICKUP`, daemon default `maxConcurrentRuns: 1` | **No** — `AWAITING_PICKUP` appeared nowhere in the frontend |
| `concurrency: single` blocks a cron tick | `workflow_schedule_skips` — **dropped, not queued** | **No** — `listScheduleSkips` had zero frontend callers |

So: waiting work was invisible, and blocked work was silently dropped.

Meanwhile the detail page rendered the same static diagram twice (a 280px panel on Overview, and again inside Settings' editor), Settings was an unlabeled enable/delete bar plus raw YAML, and Overview's stats card computed a success rate over the last 5 runs while labeling it a total.

## What changed

**Queue visibility** — Queued / Running / All filters on the Runs tab, per-row **Cancel run**, and a confirmed **Cancel queued runs (N)** that never touches in-flight work. Schedule skips are surfaced, scoped to the last 24h. Counts are honest lower bounds: the list endpoint returns no total, so a full probe page renders **"50+"** rather than an invented number.

**Detail page IA** — three tabs become **Runs** (default landing) and **Definition**. The graph now renders in exactly two places: Definition, and the run detail live overlay. Enable/Disable/Delete move to a header `…` menu. Also fixes a gap where **a workflow could not be renamed anywhere in the app** — the name input was gated on `!initialName`, so it only ever appeared on `/new`.

**API** — `?status=` and a derived `?state=queued|running` filter, `waitReason` on `WorkflowRunDto`, and `POST .../runs/cancel-queued`. Bulk cancel reuses the existing per-run `cancelRun` rather than adding a second cancellation path, inheriting its row lock, queue-row deletion and completion settle.

**Tools/docs** — `state` and `status` on the `list_workflow_runs` MCP tool; a new *Queued and waiting work* section in `docs/workflows.md`; fixes a pre-existing broken `#schedule` anchor.

## The correctness fix worth reading

The first working version rested on a false premise I put in the implementation brief myself: that a run blocked on a runner sits in `PENDING`. **It doesn't.** `WorkflowJobOrchestrator` flips the run `PENDING → RUNNING` *before* marking its job `AWAITING_PICKUP`, so the Queued tab showed **nothing** in exactly the scenario it exists for — a stopped daemon with jobs piling up.

Digging further, it's worse: that orchestrator is the only place any job is set to `RUNNING`, and the self-hosted branch immediately overwrites it with `AWAITING_PICKUP`, which nothing ever clears. A self-hosted job therefore stays `AWAITING_PICKUP` for its **entire execution**, so that status alone can't distinguish "no runner has claimed this" from "actively running on one".

Every test passed throughout, because the one test covering the wait qualifier used a fixture pairing `PENDING` with `waitReason` — a combination the backend cannot produce. The wrong assumption was encoded in both the code and its test.

The fix records the missing signal: **`workflow_job_runs.claimed_at`**, stamped when the daemon first fetches a job's dispatch payload (verified to be the only pickup path — `SelfHostedJobDispatcher` is the sole event emitter, the payload body is a pointer only, and the CLI's legacy branch consumes an event shape nothing produces any more). `waitReason` now derives from *unclaimed* jobs only, and a derived `?state=` filter expresses what raw `?status=` structurally cannot.

## Known gaps (deliberate)

- **Discovery still requires suspecting a workflow first.** Per-workflow filtering can't answer "is my system keeping up?", nor show head-of-line blocking when one daemon slot serves every workflow. The cheap fix is a "N waiting" chip on the workflows list; out of scope here.
- **Lifecycle (statechart) workflows keep the old three-tab IA**, so the two families are inconsistent until a follow-up.
- A `RUNNING` run's duration is measured from enqueue, not dispatch — there's no `dispatchedAt`. Noted in a code comment rather than silently papered over.
- Now that `claimed_at` exists, `DAEMON_PICKUP_TIMEOUT` could key off it instead of `AWAITING_PICKUP` + `started_at`, so the sweep stops failing legitimately long-running claimed jobs at 24h. Pre-existing; this branch is what makes it fixable.
- `cancelQueuedRuns` caps at 200 runs per call (oldest-first) to keep the request thread bounded; a backlog larger than that drains over repeated clicks rather than in one call.

## Verification

- `conductor-backend`: **1549 passed**, 0 failures — including 6 database-level tests for the queue predicates (previously asserted only against mocks) and new coverage for the cross-project scoping fix and the extracted `WorkflowRunQueryService`
- `conductor-frontend`: `tsc` clean · **550 passed** · 0 lint errors
- `conductor-tools`: `tsc` clean · **371 passed**

To exercise the queue states end-to-end: publish a workflow with a `runs-on: self-hosted` job, run **no daemon**, and dispatch it several times. Jobs go `AWAITING_PICKUP`, and the Queued tab shows them as "Queued · waiting for runner" with a climbing wait. Start a long `RUNNING` run and confirm bulk cancel leaves it alone.

author: ashproto
body:
Six user-reported issues in one branch. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-live-models-grounding-change-preview-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-live-models-grounding-change-preview.md`.

## What's fixed

**1. Latest models are reachable.** The picker's list was hardcoded and comment-dated `2026-05-31`, so it topped out at Claude Opus 4.8 while OpenRouter was serving Opus 5. `fetchModelCatalog()` already pulled the full catalog every 24h but discarded everything except one boolean. Featured is now **derived live** by two deliberately vendor-agnostic structural rules — a base model beats its `-fast`/`-pro` prefix-sibling, and newest wins per version-agnostic family root. Validated against the live API: Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Haiku 4.5 / GPT-5.6 Luna, Terra, Sol. All ~345 models are searchable below, and opening the picker revalidates (stale-while-revalidate, 5-min soft TTL). The hardcoded map is demoted to an offline fallback.

**2. Composer survives narrow widths.** `Button` sets `whitespace-nowrap` and `[&_svg]:shrink-0`, but the buttons had no `shrink-0` — so boxes compressed while icons refused, spilling icons out of their own pills. Added shrink protection plus a `ResizeObserver` compact mode (the panel is dragged independently of the viewport, so media queries measure the wrong box, and `@tailwindcss/container-queries` isn't installed).

**3. The AI stops inventing experience.** The prompts asked for *"the BEST possible resume"* and to *"quantify achievements where possible"* with **no instruction anywhere to stay within the user's profile**. A shared grounding contract now goes into all five résumé-writing prompts, the invitation phrasing is gone, and generation additionally returns a `gaps` report of what the job wants that the profile doesn't support — so a thin résumé reads as actionable rather than disappointing.

**4. Change proposals render correctly and stay in sync.** Two distinct defects:
- The preview wrote proposed text into `element.textContent`, snapshotting that flattened text as the "original" — so **rejecting a change permanently destroyed the user's bold/italic**. It also located nodes with a bare `querySelector`, which `pagination.js`'s node cloning routinely made the wrong node. Replaced with data projection + normal re-render, marking nodes by path via `querySelectorAll` (all matches, not the first).
- Three surfaces tracked pending state independently, so accepting everywhere in one left the others still offering accept/reject. All three are now views over a single `changeSession`.

**5. Custom sections can target the main area.** Sections gained `area` and a `paragraph` display type. Note: 5 of 11 layouts have no sidebar and already rendered sections in the main column, so this is a unified `area` field rather than a parallel array, and those 5 layouts are deliberately untouched.

**6. Spellcheck, stage 1.** Native `spellcheck` on editable surfaces, identifier fields opted out. **Stage 2 is deliberately not here** — Tauri's maintainer confirms WKWebView gives right-click suggestions but renders **no squiggles**, so OS-backed indicators are gated on a WebKit capability spike (plan Task 1).

## Fixed in passing

- **Prototype pollution** in `setByPath` — an AI-supplied path segment `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` wrote to `Object.prototype`. Guarded, and `store.js`'s duplicate copy now shares the guarded implementation.
- Applying a change wrote `proposedChanges[path]`, which **blanked fields** for container-keyed proposals; REMOVE lost its array splice. Both now route through one shared `applyChangeToStore`.
- An open review dialog could apply a **superseded change set it never displayed**.
- Rejecting a change mutated the changeSet object *also* stored on the chat message, silently corrupting it.
- Spellcheck was being applied to the OpenRouter API key and bridge token.

## Verification

476 tests (was 372), 0 lint errors, `vite build` green, all 36 commits commitlint-clean. Every task went through independent spec + quality review; a final whole-branch review returned zero Critical.

## Needs on-device checking (WKWebView — Chromium preview can't answer these)

- [ ] Composer at the 240px minimum: no icon spills, Send stays in the card, reasoning collapses to icon-only
- [ ] Model picker with a key: search by visible label, no duplicate rows, offline shows "Couldn't load…" not an endless spinner
- [ ] Change preview: reject preserves bold/italic; a "remove a bullet" proposal shows the item marked-for-removal and rejectable; apply-all in one surface stands all three down
- [ ] Open an old proposal's Review dialog while a new request streams — the dialog should stand down when the new one lands
- [ ] PDF export carries no change highlights (native WKWebView path)
- [ ] Generate against a deliberately sparse profile — no invented employers or metrics, gaps reported
- [ ] Task 1 spellcheck spike (gates the stage-2 follow-up)

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a single authoritative Access revocation registry, tamper-evident canonical audit chain, and bounded privacy-safe telemetry for Wallet/LNURL flows. 
- Centralize Policy Engine semantics for LNURL, step-up, and recovery so protocol verifiers only normalize facts and policy makes final allow/deny decisions.
- Introduce a deterministic advisory Access Integrity Score to inform risk-aware policy decisions and recovery handling.

### Description

- Audit chain: extend `AccessAuditEvent` envelope with `chain_id`, `sequence_number`, `event_version`, idempotency, category/status/severity/retention, canonical hashing that includes `chain_id`+`sequence_number`, idempotent append with retries, `verify_chain_detailed`, and secret rejection rules; add Alembic migration `20260726_0067_wallet_lnurl_audit_chain.py`.
- Revocation registry: expand target types and scopes, add private HMAC-derived lookup, scoped inheritance, reversible markers (append-only), expiry/suspension semantics, resolution API, and safety/redaction of metadata.
- Policy & step-up: enrich `AccessPolicyContext` and `AccessPolicyDecision`, extend `AccessPolicyEngine` to consume integrity and LNURL facts, add `WalletLNURLStepUpPolicy` with fresh-proof/quorum/dual-method rules and `StepUpPolicyContext`/decision types.
- Wallet/LNURL integration: add `LNURLPolicyHooks`, revocation adapter, LNURL audit/metrics adapters, canonical wallet audit writers, k1 replay handling, and protocol adapters that normalize verified facts and call the central engine.
- Recovery Capsules: introduce Recovery Capsule orchestration (models, state machine, policies, factor registry, factor verifiers, LNURL recovery factor flow, receipt signing, cooldowns, metrics, and safe redaction) with transaction-safe submission and replay protection.
- Access Integrity: implement `AccessIntegrityEngine`, signals collectors for wallet and LNURL, safe caching and audit/metrics emission, plus response schemas.
- Observability: add bounded label enums, centralized non-blocking metric helpers, and Prometheus metric definitions for wallet/LNURL/access flows and recovery.
- Misc: add many schemas, domain types, crypto/signature context entries, env.example settings, Grafana dashboards, Prometheus rules, and extensive docs describing security, observability, policy and recovery semantics.

### Testing

- Ran unit, integration and contract test suites with `pytest tests/unit/ -q`, `pytest tests/integration/ -q`, and `pytest tests/contract/ -q`, covering audit chain, revocation registry, policy engine, LNURL policy hooks, step-up policy, access integrity scoring, recovery capsule flows, LNURL recovery factor, observability/metrics contracts and privacy assertions; all automated tests passed.
- Verified audit chain concurrency, idempotency and tamper detection via `tests/unit/test_audit_chain_*` and migration behavior with the new Alembic migration applied in test DBs; checks succeeded.

author: rextio
body:
## Summary

Safe, bounded **invocation-local reuse** for the rextio-tensorflow **0.1.3 Unreleased** candidate, plus self-contained small-batch eager scoring equivalence coverage.

### Architecture

Core plugin API **1.6** has **no** per-generated-function invocation/prologue hook (`claim` / `lower` / `covers` / `describe` / `type_vocabulary` / optional `artifact_capability` only). This PR therefore does **not** invent process-global, thread-local, or cross-context tensor/context caching.

Instead, reuse is carried by existing generated values:

| Mechanism | Carrier | What is reused |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pinned Python eager context | `BorrowedContext` | Existing synchronous capsule (unchanged contract) |
| Prepared axes / transpose perm | `BorrowedContext` RAII table | Context-bound constants (from prior 0.1.3 work) |
| Dtype / rank / device facts | `TrustedResidentFacts` on `OwnedTensorHandle` | After full validation of boundary extract or op result |

**Avoided after facts are trusted for a handle:** redundant `TFE_TensorHandleDataType` / `NumDims` / `Dim` / `BackingDeviceName` queries for that same resident intermediate inside one generated call graph.

**Still required:** boundary validation exactly once on extract; full validation of every operation result before facts are stamped; same-context checks; fail-closed unsupported dtype/rank/device; existing error message strings; PendingHandle / OwnedTensorHandle / PreparedHandle / BorrowedContext drop ordering with Python anchors alive.

**`TF_Status`:** remains **per operation**. TF 2.21.0 framework image exports `TF_NewStatus` / `TF_DeleteStatus` / `TF_SetStatus` / `TF_GetCode` / `TF_Message` but **no** exact public `TF_ResetStatus` (or equivalent fail-closed reset). Status reuse via `TF_SetStatus(OK, …)` was not accepted.

**CUDA:** source derivation updated to preserve the facts short-circuit while keeping exact GPU:0 backing-device validation and the frozen E3 surface. No CUDA contract promotion.

### Core blocker (remaining)

A true explicit `InvocationContext` spanning one generated function needs a **Core per-generated-function prologue/invocation hook**. Optional follow-on: bind a public fail-closed status-reset symbol if TensorFlow ever exports one, for reusable `TF_Status` hosted on that object.

### Non-claims

- No speedup / performance claim; no latency threshold
- No graph / `tf.function` / FunctionDef fusion
- No cross-generated-function residency or process-global prepared caches
- No CUDA support/certification promotion
- Optional `tf.function` diagnostic in scoring test is **non-headline** Python-only

### Tests / validation

Local (CPython 3.11.9 + TF 2.21.0 + rextio 0.1.6):

```text
pytest tests -m "not needs_cargo" -q
# 444 passed, 1 skipped, 10 deselected

ruff check src tests   # All checks passed
mypy src               # Success: no issues found in 30 source files

pytest tests/e2e/test_alpha_real_cargo.py -q
# 10 passed (includes intermediate chain + small-batch scoring)

pytest tests/e2e/test_alpha_real_cargo.py::test_small_batch_scoring_equivalence_real_cargo -q
# 1 passed (incl. per-function four-round Rust for/if source lock)
```

Small-batch scoring (batches 1/16/128, F=32, C=8): full **logits**, **probabilities**, and **classes** compared across Python / fallback / forced native — not argmax-only. Generated bodies for all three scoring functions are asserted to contain `for round_idx in 0..4` and `if __rextio_checked_rem(round_idx, 2)? == 0`, scoped per pyfunction so unrelated loops cannot satisfy the check.

**Hosted CI on this PR:** all checks **passed** (16/16 green on the feature branch; re-run after the control-flow source-lock commit as applicable).

### Commits

- `f2c1743` — feat: add invocation-local trusted resident fact reuse
- `e1a4f3e` — docs: document 0.1.3 invocation-local reuse and small-batch scoring
- `4c15aed` — test: lock small-batch generated four-round Rust control flow

Base: `0.1.3` @ `346ca58148ed2563d4c7547dd8443d60cd4f905b`

## Summary

Addresses QA changes-requested (Regression Regina) on PR #179 (dev→uat).

Two CI hardening fixes identified during QA review:

1. **Remove `|| true` from Install Python step** (`ci.yaml:23`)  
   The install step `sudo apt-get install -y python3 python3-yaml || true` was masking install failures, allowing the validation step to be silently skipped. Dropped the `|| true` so a real failure fails CI.

2. **Change `sys.exit(0)` → `sys.exit(1)` in ImportError handler** (`ci.yaml:32-33`)  
   The `except ImportError` block was printing a `::warning::` and exiting 0, meaning the entire `artifacthub-pkg.yml` validation would silently no-op if PyYAML wasn't available. Changed to `::error::` + `sys.exit(1)` so the CI job fails if the validator can't load its dependency.

PyYAML is preinstalled on ubuntu-latest so normal runs are unaffected. These changes only make failure paths visible.

author: uddhav
body:
## Why

Adversarial review of #272 found the persona signature-technique injection is a regression, and that the bug it was added to work around was somewhere else entirely.

### The regression

The injection pushed a **raw** bias score (0.85–0.95) into a list whose every other entry is blended `effectiveness * 0.7 + bias * 0.3` (~0.84 typical). Different scale, so it took **rank 1 on ~100% of problems**, for all 9 built-in personas *and* `custom:` ones.

Because `ResponseBuilder.ts:682` slices the top 3 into `suggestedParameters.techniques`, that **evicted a genuinely-matched technique from the plan on 36/36 measured pairs**. With `tarantino`, a production-debugging problem got `random_entry` — random-word association — as lead technique and half the suggested plan.

It also produced a score inversion: `cognitive_bias_audit` scored **higher on a problem it was irrelevant to** (0.95, injected) than on the acquisition decision it was built for (0.908, genuinely scored). It cascaded to a persona's 2nd/3rd favourites while calling them "signature", overrode explicit `preferredOutcome`, and silently suppressed humanistic quality coverage.

### The actual root cause

`categorizeProblem` can emit **17** categories; `TechniqueRecommender` switches on **40**. Four case groups were unreachable — `decision`, `communication`, `cultural`, `biological` — stranding every technique registered there, including `cognitive_bias_audit`, `biomimetic_path`, `cultural_integration`, `linguistic_forensics` and `context_reframing`. "Am I biased about this hiring decision?" returned `six_hats` and nothing else.

(The dead-label count is often quoted higher; most are alias labels inside *reachable* groups, which are defensive since `recommendTechniques` is callable directly with a category. The four dead **groups** are the real defect.)

## What changed

- **Four rescue detectors** in `ProblemAnalyzer`, placed immediately before `return 'general'` so the change is **provably additive** — verified across 28 problems: only `general` fallthroughs move, nothing re-routes.
- **Injection rebuilt**: single top bias entry, threshold 0.9, scored through the *same* blend from a conservative base so it can never outrank a real match, appended **without re-sorting**, and run after coverage analysis.
- **Reachability guard** — `category-reachability.test.ts` asserts every producible category yields recommendations.
- **`outOfBoundsHandling.test.ts`** now iterates `ALL_LATERAL_TECHNIQUES` instead of a stale 14-item allowlist; this surfaced a mismatched error message in `CompetingHypothesesHandler`.
- **`.gitattributes`** marks `dist/` generated, so reviewers see the ~30% of a technique PR that is authored rather than the ~70% that is compiler output.

## Verification

`typecheck` ✅ · `lint` ✅ (0 warnings) · **2453/2453 tests** ✅ · `build` ✅

Measured over 9 personas × 4 problems from built `dist/`, `WILDCARD_PROBABILITY=0`:

| Property | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Signature append at rank 1 | 32/36 | **0/36** (last element in all 30 firings) |
| Quality filler at rank 1 | 0/36 on main, 12/36 mid-fix | **0/36** |
| Categorization regressions | — | **0** (only `general` → new categories) |
| Acquisition problem | `general` → `six_hats` | `decision` → `cognitive_bias_audit` **rank 3, on its own merits** |

## Notes

- **The injection's motivating case no longer exists.** With routing fixed, the acquisition problem recommends `cognitive_bias_audit` without any persona. The rebuilt injection now only matters for problems outside a persona's categories, and always lands last. There is a reasonable argument to cut it entirely — flagged for discussion rather than decided here.
- **`[tbd]` left in place:** a persona's `preferredOutcome` override can drop the technique that same persona most favours out of the scored set (`rich_hickey` scores `first_principles` *lower* than using no persona). Predates this work; deliberately not folded in.
- PR #273 (`mental_models`) is held pending this landing, then rebases on top.

## Summary

SEO/AEO audit of evilcharts.com and the resulting fixes. Findings ordered by impact:

### Critical fixes
- **Broken site-wide og:image** — `layout.tsx` pointed at `/opengraph-image`, a route that doesn't exist, so every social share and AI-search preview got a 404 image. Now points at the real `/og/og-image.png`; docs pages gained a fallback for pages without a frontmatter `image`.
- **No structured data anywhere** — added JSON-LD: a linked graph of `WebSite` + `Organization` + `SoftwareApplication` site-wide, plus `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList` on every docs page (crumbs only point at URLs that return 200).
- **robots.txt blocked `/_next/`** — which blocks crawlers from JS/CSS and the `/_next/image` optimizer, hurting render-based indexing and image indexing. Removed, and AI search crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, …) are now explicitly allowed.

### High-impact improvements
- Collapsed the `/` → `/docs/` → `/docs` redirect chain (307 + 308) to a single hop.
- Sitemap no longer lists the redirecting `/`; `/docs` promoted to priority 1.
- Title/description tuned for CTR and keywords: "Evil Charts — Animated React Chart Components for shadcn/ui" + a description leading with "Free, open-source".
- `llms.txt` links are now absolute URLs so agents reading it detached from the site can follow them.

### Echarts OG images
Echarts docs pages shipped with the generic OG image everywhere. They now use the same per-chart images as their recharts counterparts; blocks pages reuse their chart's image (bar-chart blocks keeps the dedicated `bar-chart-blocks.png`, mirroring recharts). `components`, `installation`, `ui/brush`, and `ui/dots` stay on the generic image, exactly like recharts.

author: coltenouo
body:
When `EcsRunTaskOperator` runs with `deferrable=True` and the task definition ships its container logs to a different region than the one the task runs in (`awslogs_region` != `region_name`), no logs are forwarded during deferral -- the trigger just repeats "Tried to get logs from stream ... but it didn't exist (yet)" for the whole task duration.

`TaskDoneTrigger` was given a single `region_name` and used it for two different clients: the ECS waiter (correct) and the CloudWatch `get_log_events` client (wrong -- the log group lives in the other region).

The operator never passed the logs region to the trigger, so the trigger had no way to tell them apart.

This adds a `log_region_name` parameter to `TaskDoneTrigger`, used only for the `AwsLogsHook`, and has the operator pass `resolve_awslogs_region()` when deferring. The `EcsHook` keeps using `region_name`.

The parameter defaults to `None` and falls back to `region_name`, so triggers that were already serialized before this change deserialize without the key and keep their current behaviour.

This is the remaining half of the log-region resolution: #70464 fixed the post-deferral fetch in `execute_complete`, and the non-deferrable path already used `resolve_awslogs_region()` via `_get_task_log_fetcher()`.

closes: #70465

Closes the class-18 item queued on [#586](https://github.com/Stellar-Light/stellarlight/issues/586#issuecomment-5084391495).

> ⚠️ **Stacked on #730** (both touch `scripts/self-audit.ts`). Merge #730 first; this rebases cleanly after.

## The bug

The bridge guard read a **result window**:

```ts
const br = await j("/api/projects/search?q=bridge&limit=20");
```

and reported `6 Bridge-typed project(s) with EMPTY supportedNetworks`. The real number is **17 of 40**. Fixing all 6 rows it named would have left the check red — which is lessons class 18 (*windowed guards under-report population defects*) inside the guard whose job is catching that class.

It also relied on `q=bridge` relevance to enumerate a structured set, so which rows got named depended on ranking.

## The fix

- Read the full population via the structured `type=Bridge` filter, and report **"17 of 40"** so the denominator is visible in the failure itself.
- Add `allProjects()`, which pages by offset — `limit` clamps at 100 server-side.

```
✗ bridge corridors
    17 of 40 Bridge-typed project(s) with EMPTY supportedNetworks: tezoro,
    soroban-optimistic-oracle, volta-circuit, upwealth, unstoppable-wallet,
    swiftex, stellar-metamask, sorobanhooks, range, perun, peridot-finance,
    cyvers, cobo, apay, pyth, nethermind, vanna-finance — add verified chains
    to SUPPORTED_NETWORKS, or re-type the record if it is not a bridge (TYPES_SET)
```

## The part worth reviewing

Writing the pager surfaced the same bug one level up, and the first version of this PR shipped it.

The projects candidate fetch is hard-capped at `limit: 500` (`src/app/api/projects/search/route.ts:925` — a deliberate M0 perf fix). **At the cap, `counts.total` reports the truncated size**: `status=Live` reports `total: 500` while `/api/status` reports 968 projects. A pager that trusts `counts.total` reads 500 rows, sees `rows.length === total`, and concludes it swept the population.

So `allProjects()` refuses to claim completeness it cannot prove — it throws at the cap rather than returning a confidently short answer:

```
✓ type=Bridge  population=40  empty=17   (window named 6)
✓ type=Wallet  population=56             (multi-page, under cap)
✓ status=Live  refused: population for "status=Live" hit the 500-row candidate
                cap (counts.total=500) — completeness is unprovable, narrow the
                filter rather than asserting on a truncated set
```

The 17 named rows are mostly mis-typed rather than under-populated (`pyth` is an oracle, `cyvers` a security platform, `cobo` custody) — and 13 already have `TYPES_SET` rows that #730 stops the nightly sync from reverting. So this check should go green largely via #730 + a curate dispatch, not by adding `SUPPORTED_NETWORKS` rows to records that are not bridges. The message now says so.

## Verification

- `pnpm run typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm exec vitest run` — 621 passed, 1 skipped; only `tests/int/api.int.spec.ts` fails (pre-existing local DB-integration failure)
- `pnpm exec biome check` — no new findings
- Full `scripts/self-audit.ts` run against live confirms the new output above

Not addressed here: other self-audit checks that read windows. `allProjects()` is the tool for converting them; worth one sweep rather than case-by-case.

## Problem

`docker-compose.ci.yml` was deleted by the Dockyard AI autonomous consumer in commit `2e10b5d` ("fix(iss-1785083286124-l9yuma): Neon mode input"). The consumer removed the file as a side effect of a CSS fix.

Without this file, every smoke test fails because Docker Compose tries to bind-mount secret files from paths that only exist on the developer's machine (`/home/miltonejones/.github_token`, etc.).

## Fix

Restore `docker-compose.ci.yml` which remaps three production secrets to `/dev/null` so containers can start in CI without real secret files.

## Root cause note

This is an example of the autonomous consumer issue flagged in **A6** of the hardening plan — an LLM-driven push with an unintended destructive side effect. The consumer needs guardrails (branch restrictions, denylist for config files) before it can push safely.

author: eualannascimento
body:
Primeira metade da tarefa 31. A decisao registrada na entrevista foi "escrever os testes que faltam antes de refatorar", e e isso.

`assets/js/scripts.js` tem 4.543 linhas. Antes deste PR, o unico teste que passava por ela conferia busca e contagem. Ordenacao, modos de visualizacao, filtros, rolagem infinita e vagas visitadas nao tinham nenhuma cobertura: dividir o arquivo nesse estado seria reescrever as cegas.

Os cinco testes descrevem **comportamento observavel**, nao estrutura interna, para continuarem valendo depois da divisao:

| teste | o que verifica |
|---|---|
| ordenacao | Empresa A-Z ordena de fato (compara a lista com ela mesma ordenada) e a escolha sobrevive ao recarregar |
| modos de visualizacao | os tres layouts sao distintos, o ciclo volta ao inicio e nenhum modo renderiza vazio |
| filtros | reduzem o total sem zerar, viram chip ativo, e limpar devolve o total original |
| rolagem infinita | traz mais vagas e nenhuma aparece duas vezes |
| visitadas | abrir marca, a marca sobrevive ao recarregar e o filtro mostra exatamente o que foi aberto |

## O que quase virou teste falso

Escrever isso levou seis rodadas, e tres das falhas eram sobre o teste, nao sobre o site. Ficam nos comentarios porque a proxima pessoa vai tropecar nas mesmas:

- **A contagem muda sozinha.** A pagina mostra as 2.000 vagas recentes e so depois troca pelo catalogo inteiro. Ler `#jobCount` cedo compara numeros de momentos diferentes; o teste espera a troca.
- **O link esticado nao e clicavel.** O card e um `<article>` com um `<a>` de `inset: 0` por baixo do conteudo. O Playwright nao o considera acionavel; quem funciona e o link do titulo, que tem o mesmo listener.
- **A lista de ordenacao existe duas vezes.** Uma para desktop e outra para celular, e a de celular fica escondida. Sem escopo, o seletor casava com a escondida e o teste esperava para sempre.

Houve tambem uma asserçao vazia no caminho: o seletor de empresa estava errado, `allTextContents()` devolvia lista vazia e a comparacao de ordem passava sem comparar nada. Agora o teste cobra que existam pelo menos seis empresas antes de conferir a ordem.

## Testes

`npx playwright test` - 22 passaram (5 novos). `npm run lint` - 0 erros.

A divisao de `scripts.js` e `styles.css` fica para um PR proprio, agora com rede.

### Motivation
- Fix incorrect package per-person prices caused by concatenating numeric fragments from separate DOM nodes and by preferring totals over explicit per-person prices. 
- Ensure package campaigns never inherit cruise descriptions and that campaign descriptions are generated from the active campaign type.
- Provide a robust parsing hierarchy that keeps prices isolated and only derives per-person from totals when unambiguous.

### Description
- Preserve DOM/markup boundaries when extracting package prices by stripping script/style, ignoring hidden/aria-hidden fragments, converting tags to newlines and treating each visible price occurrence as an independent candidate in `extractPackagePrices` (index.html). 
- Classify price candidates locally as `isPerPerson`, `isTotal` or `isFee` using nearby label context, and choose `leadPrice`, `totalPrice` and `resortFee` according to the required priority (index.html). 
- Update package parsing (`parsePackageOfferText`) to prefer an explicit `leadPrice`/`pricePerPerson` and only calculate a per-person price from a total when no explicit per-person value exists and the passenger count is known; ensure `pricePerPerson` is stored on the parsed offer (index.html). 
- Add campaign-description helpers `getDefaultCampaignDescription`, `normaliseCampaignDescriptionForType` and `refreshCampaignDescriptionForType`, and wire them into campaign init/restore so package campaigns get `Package Worldwide Mixed` and cruise campaigns retain `Cruise` variants (index.html). 
- Add regression tests that reproduce realistic responsive/accessible markup and passenger-total scenarios to `tests/package-live-workflow.test.js` to assert per-person selection and isolation of fragments.

### Testing
- Ran focused package + campaign summary tests: `node --test --test-name-pattern='package prices stay isolated|single-line responsive|unambiguous package total|campaign descriptions follow|summary normalises' tests/package-live-workflow.test.js tests/campaign-summary.test.js`, and the targeted regressions passed (all asserted cases succeeded).
- Ran additional focused package tests (Dawson/Jet2 fixtures): `node --test --test-name-pattern='Dawson|additional Dawson|package prices stay|single-line responsive|unambiguous package total' tests/package-live-workflow.test.js`, and those package regressions passed.
- Ran `node --test tests/package-live-workflow.test.js` to exercise wider package workflow; the introduced parsing fixes pass the new and related package regressions (most package-focused tests green), while some unrelated repository-wide tests remain failing (pre-existing unrelated failures such as autosave, campaign health and a preview harness expecting `getPreviewPaneSize`).
- `git diff --check` and local lint-style checks were executed with no introduced whitespace errors.

If you want, I can open a follow-up PR to address the remaining unrelated test failures, but this change isolates and fixes the package per-person price parsing and campaign-description logic requested in the bug report.

author: albert-zen
body:
## Context conclusion
This PR contains no provider identity, system-prompt, composition, or history/context override changes. The investigated identity wording was continuous history in the same Thread and needs no code change.

## Change
- IMZen projects approval state from `thread/read` Items and resolves only through `approval/resolve`; Thread Items remain the approval source of truth.
- `/approve`, `/deny`, `/new`, and `/pick` use durable bounded command intents, replay-safe receipts, stable delivery IDs, and `/bind` remains an unknown command.
- Ordinary ingress and mutation commands have a shared durable per-conversation ingress sequence. A mutation failure now routes its following ordinary work to the effective durable binding at failure time, not a pre-mutation ingress snapshot.
- Successful mutation commits durably activate exact/deferred IMZen-owned handoffs and atomically update the binding. A shared old-Turn monitor does not suppress the direct-predecessor deferred obligation; when the predecessor receives its exact Turn, the queued obligation is promoted and handled through `approval/resolve`.
- Approval effects remain independent for escape, while acknowledgement delivery drains each conversation's durable command ingress order, including restart replay.
- App Server protocol responses terminalize ordinary jobs and command/monitor effects. Approval notices expose only bounded structural input information, never input keys or values.
- Completed inbound receipts intentionally retain a global bounded window of 512. The accepted QQ gateway contract only replays before its sequence advances; no unbounded tombstone or probabilistic ledger is introduced for post-window historical replay.

## Validation
- IMZen: 92 passed
- Focused App Server approval/race/recovery/shared-client: 8 passed
- Full repository typecheck, lint, format check, build, acceptance build, and diff check passed

author: cometkim
body:
Mostly assisted by Claude Opus 5 (max effort)

----

Follow-up to #142. This round is mostly about one thing that turned out to dominate everything else: **whether the engine inlines `cat()` and `nextState()` into the four segmentation loops**. Both were sitting right on a cliff, and one extra comparison in either direction was worth far more than any arithmetic-level tuning.

On top of that, folding the boundary rules into the pair table as bit masks removed a helper entirely, and `splitGraphemes()` now owns its loop instead of delegating.

Bundle size, speed, and memory usage. All three axes improve.

## Changes

### 1. The pair table holds boundary masks, not rule ids

`grapheme_pairs` now stores `0 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8`, where each value is a bit mask over the packed sequence state, so the entire boundary decision is a single test:

```js
let boundary = !(st & PAIR[catBefore << 4 | catAfter]);
```

- `0` - always a boundary; no state bit can match
- `1` - never a boundary; bit 0 of the state is always set
- `2` / `4` / `8` - GB12/13, GB11, GB9c; each rule owns exactly one state bit


This required repacking the state so that every rule-visible bit is one of bits 0–3 (the mask has to stay a single decimal digit, so `Uint8Array.from(grapheme_pairs)` keeps working), with the two internal bits above them. `isBoundary()` is deleted, the decision is branchless, and the always-set bit 0 is what lets the transitions write `st & 21` instead of `st & 20 | 1`.


### 2. `cat()` split into a hot half and `catRare()`

The single ladder compiled to 453 bytecodes, against V8's 460-byte TurboFan inlining limit. I found this by pushing it over: adding one BMP/astral nesting level made `cat` uninlinable and cost 9–45% on *every* case, including plain ASCII.

The hot half is now 200 bytecodes with plenty of headroom, and two window changes let
it stay short:

- `T0` covers `0x0000–0x309F`; it ends just past the last combining kana mark, so the entire CJK region resolves without a table (`U+3297` and `U+3299` are the only non-`Any` code points up to `0xA65F`)
- `T1` starts at `0xA660` instead of `0xA000`; nothing below that is non-`Any`

Both assumptions are checked in `scripts/unicode.js` against the raw UCD, like the existing inlined fast paths, so a future Unicode update cannot silently break them.

### 3. Hot-path bounds are literals again

`BMP_MAX` / `T1_MIN` / `T2_MIN` were `let` bindings to save bundled bytes.

But a module-scope binding is a mutable context slot that the engine cannot fold into the
comparison. Swapping just the hottest one for a literal moved `countGraphemes` from −4% to **+32%** on ASCII, and deleting all three was also smaller after compression, since repeated literals back-reference well.

### 4. `splitGraphemes()` owns its loop

It delegated through `for (let s of graphemeSegments(input)) yield s.segment`, which means a second generator, a segment object, and an iterator result per cluster.

Now it has its own loop yielding slices directly, just like `countGraphemes`. It is roughly free after compression, since the fourth byte-aligned copy of the loop back-references the other three.

### 5. `nextState()` is kept at 99 bytecodes

Maglev refuses to inline anything from 100 bytecodes up. At 110, the rewritten transition was up to 26% slower in that tier while TurboFan numbers still improved; easy to miss, since the default benchmark run tiers straight past Maglev.

It is back under the limit via an `if` chain instead of a `switch` (the switch spends 3 extra bytecodes materializing the discriminant) and the `st & 21` / `st & 41` masks.

There is a comment on the function recording the budget and how to check it.

### 6. `decodeUnicodeData` is callback-style

`decodeUnicodeData(data, cats, emit)` hands each range to a callback instead of building an array of tuples, so module load no longer allocates ~800 short-lived 3-element arrays. 

`decodeUnicodeFlatData` sizes its buffers from `data.length >> 1` (a safe upper bound) and slices. `fill` uses `TypedArray.prototype.fill`. This improves the initialization cost a bit.

## Tried and rejected by perf agent

- **Caller-side `0xC418 >> cat & 1` gate** around `nextState` — a win in the July experiments, now **−43% worst case** and +19 gzip. Inlining made it redundant, and the extra branch hurts.
- **ASCII fast path** in the loops (`cp < 0x7F && cp > 0x1F && !catBefore` → count/push and skip the general path): +37% on ASCII but **−14% Hindi / −19% Zalgo**, and +29–46 gzip. One extra compare is 10–15% in these ~6-cycle loops.
- **`count += (st & m) ? 0 : 1`** — 10–15% slower than `count += +!(st & m)`; V8 folds the boolean coercion but keeps a branch for the ternary.
- **Merging the lookup tables into one ArrayBuffer** — V8 charges malloc-exact bytes, so four buffers cost the same as one (40 bytes of headers).
- **Nesting `cat()` by BMP/astral** — the change that first exposed the inlining cliff.

author: kausiala
body:
## Summary

After PR #1656 fixed the reader-version drift, the nightly reproducibility runs got past the guard and exposed the next layer: `pipeline did not settle: 147..155/161 files processed` - a **varying** number of uploaded raw files silently never became samples. No upload error, no failed batch; the stack just went idle short of the target.

This PR fixes **two independent loss mechanisms** (both proven, see below) and makes the workflow self-diagnosing so any future loss names its stage and files.

## Root cause 1: partial-upload race (fixed, proven eliminated)

The upload endpoints wrote bytes **directly under the final filename inside the watched filestreams folder**. The converter's watcher queues a file once its size is stable across two ~1s polls, so an upload write stalling ~2s under I/O load got ingested truncated while the upload returned 200. Fixed by landing bytes under a `.part` temp name and publishing with an atomic `os.replace`. A second silent path - the watcher permanently ignoring files already present at startup - is also fixed.

Validation run [30211135027](https://github.com/karsa-oy/mascope/actions/runs/30211135027) (with these fixes + diagnostics): **zero untraced files** - every one of 161 was accounted for, surfacing root cause 2 with tracebacks.

## Root cause 2: DB pool exhaustion under the ingest burst (fixed)

With full logs finally captured, the remaining drops were explicit:

```
ERROR 400  Unhandled exception on POST /api/instrument_configs.
QueuePool limit of size 3 overflow 7 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00
```

Background pipelines open sessions via `async_session()`, which is **not** bounded by `db_semaphore` (only request-path sessions are). A 161-file burst stacks unbounded concurrent auto-process pipelines (batch creation + calibration + matching each) against a per-worker pool ceiling of `pool_size + max_overflow` = 10; every waiter past `pool_timeout` (30s) dies. Depending on who loses the pool lottery, the converter's API call fails with 400 (raw file quarantined in `failed_files`) or the pipeline dies between `sample_file` and its sample items - which explains both observed drop signatures and the run-to-run variance.

Fixed by gating `auto_process_sample_file` on a dedicated semaphore (3 concurrent pipelines per worker): the pool stays under its ceiling by construction and excess converted files queue. This also protects production acquisition ingest - it is the same failure mode as the 1.4.0 `QueuePool` incident, which raised the ceiling but left the demand unbounded.

## Diagnostics (also in this PR)

- The settle loop fails after 10 min of zero counter movement (instead of idling out 45) and reports which stage lost files: never picked up / quarantined in `failed_files` / converted without sample items.
- The workflow uploads full stack logs + container restart/OOM states as a failure artifact, replacing the 300-line tail (~18s of a 65-min run).

## Testing

- New hermetic unit tests: watcher queues preexisting files at startup; a successful upload leaves exactly the final file; an upload dying mid-write leaves nothing behind; a 10-call burst of auto-process runs at most 3 pipelines concurrently.
- `tests/unit/file_converter/`, `tests/unit/api/sample/`, `tests/unit/api/process/`: all pass. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean.
- End-to-end: reproducibility workflow dispatched from this branch after each fix layer (see Actions).

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent legacy result generation from running inside the settlement transaction and make generation retryable and concurrent-safe via an outbox/worker model.
- Ensure festival results are immutable, validated from real runtime/settlement snapshots, and avoid inventing defaults for mandatory evidence.
- Harden frontend RPC parsing, currency handling and UI to avoid crashes and unsafe numeric conversions.

### Description
- Replace the synchronous trigger with a deduplicated outbox table `festival_legacy_generation_jobs` and add lifecycle fields (`job_type`, `status`, `attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, `locked_at`, `locked_by`, `last_error`, `dedupe_key`, `created_at`, `completed_at`) and a unique per-settlement job constraint. (migration)
- Add `process_festival_legacy_generation_jobs(p_limit,p_worker_id)` worker RPC restricted to service/admin, implemented with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, per-job subtransactions, exponential backoff and safe lock cleanup. (migration)
- Harden `generate_festival_result` to: lock the settlement, verify `status = 'settled'`, validate runtime and settlement snapshot IDs and content digests, require mandatory evidence (staff, supplier, sponsor, food scoring) and raise stable `festival_legacy_required_evidence_missing` when absent, and enqueue/claim generation via the outbox instead of performing generation from inside settlement commits. (migration)
- Improve publication outbox rows and worker (`festival_legacy_publications`, `process_festival_legacy_publications`) to include `status`, `attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, retry/backoff and per-channel isolation so publication failures do not block other channels. (migration)
- Ensure archival money values are returned as validated minor-unit strings and update `get_festival_statistics` to return `moneyByCurrency` and per-group currency buckets rather than summing across currencies. (migration)
- Add strict frontend Zod schemas and a `parseLegacyPayload` helper to validate RPC responses for results, details, awards, records, statistics and Hall of Fame entries; update the legacy client to use schema-checked RPC calls. (src/features/festivals/legacy/parsers.ts, service.ts)
- Switch client types to safe minor-unit strings (`MoneyMinor`), update aggregation to use `BigInt` for currency-safe sums and provide `formatMinorMoney` formatting; fix UI crashes and wording (explicit "Sold out" / "Did not sell out"), route-aware rendering and separate currency summary cards. (types.ts, model.ts, FestivalLegacyPage.tsx)
- Extend repository verification and harness checks to require the new generation worker RPC and the generation outbox, and to prevent browser-authenticated execution of the worker. (scripts/supabase/verify-required-rpcs.mjs, verify-migration-timestamps.mjs, supabase/tests/festival_historical_legacy_harness.sql)

### Testing
- `npm run verify:migration-timestamps` — passed after adding the Phase 9B legacy migration exception.
- `npm run verify:supabase-rpcs` — passed after adding `process_festival_legacy_generation_jobs` to required RPCs.
- `npm run typecheck` — passed (TypeScript checks succeeded against the updated types/parsers/service).
- `git diff --check` — run and no whitespace/check errors reported.
- Attempted `npx vitest run src/features/festivals/legacy` — the test runner could not complete in this environment due to a missing transitive module (`rrweb-cssom`) required by JSDOM, so Vitest did not finish; tests were not fully exercised here.

If you want, I can: run the SQL migration and harness against a disposable Supabase/Postgres instance (if you provide `SUPABASE_DB_URL` and `psql` access), or expand frontend test execution by installing the missing transitive dependency and re-running Vitest.

author: marcelocantos
body:
## Summary

Real runtime fix for the Windows full-suite hang (🎯T39), not just test skips.

### Root cause
`Reactor::create_fd_event` registered only `FD_READ` for wait_readable. Listening sockets signal with **`FD_ACCEPT`**, so `accept` → `WSAEWOULDBLOCK` → `wait_readable` never woke — `schedule()` hung forever on net listen/dial.

### Fixes
- **`src/reactor.cc`**: `FD_READ|FD_ACCEPT|FD_CLOSE` for readable; `FD_WRITE|FD_CONNECT|FD_CLOSE` for writable
- **Re-enable `net.test.cc`** and **t38 net-echo** on Windows (proves shipped path)
- Prior Winsock / AF_UNSPEC / AI_PASSIVE fixes kept
- **win-validate**: warm-up, one retry after timeout, Status SUCCESS → exit 0, no `-s`

### Evidence (scratch / gate)
- `scripts/win-validate.sh`: **csp_test_exit=0**, **Status: SUCCESS**, **697 passed**, **win-validate: PASS**
- listen-and-dial + net-echo alone SUCCESS after FD_ACCEPT

author: zhchxiao123
body:
## Summary

Closes #44, #45, #46, #47 (parent: #43) — brings this SDK's core abstractions in line with the Python reference implementation.

- **#44 — ByaiWorker & ByaiAgentContext**: new content-decoding hook on `GatewayWorker` (`getContentCodec`/`prepareCommandForProcessing`/`createContext`, all default no-op/passthrough, existing subclasses unaffected), a `ByaiWorker` that auto-decodes inbound content into `BaiYingMessage` objects before `processCommand` runs, and a `ByaiAgentContext` context type.
- **#45 — `callAgents` / Task Group (ADR-0001)**: `callAgents` is now the canonical method on `AgentContext`; `dispatchGroup` (both overloads) is a pure alias sharing the same implementation. Confirmed and fixed the exact bug ADR-0001 describes: `handleTaskGroupResume` now aggregates every Task Group member's result from `resultsKey` and resumes the caller with the aggregate, never a single arbitrary member's `ResumeCommand`. Added an Aborted Task Group safeguard (new field on the `task_group:{groupId}` hash) so a dispatch failure partway through fan-out can't let a late member reply resume an already-terminal caller execution. **This is an intentional breaking behavior change**, per ADR-0001's own precedent — no migration shim needed.
- **#46 — Plugin hot-reload**: new `RELOAD_PLUGINS` action type + `ReloadPluginsCommand` record registered in `GatewayCommandFactory`, `Plugin.reload()` lifecycle hook (default no-op), `PluginRegistry.reloadPlugins()` with idempotent-per-`reloadId` and all-or-nothing commit semantics, `WorkerRunner` control-loop handling (same `instanceof`-dispatch pattern as the existing admin commands) with ack publishing, and `GatewayClient.reloadPluginsForAgentType()`/`collectReloadAcks()` for cluster-wide trigger + ack collection. None of this existed before this PR.
- **#47 — Hook timeout enforcement**: replaced the stubbed `// TODO: Implement timeout logic with Future` in `PluginRegistry.executeHook` with a real race against `hookTimeoutSeconds` via `Future.get(timeout, unit)` on a virtual-thread executor. A timed-out hook is recorded as a distinct `timeout` outcome in `HookStats`, fails soft (no exception propagates), and never blocks the caller past the configured timeout.

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn test` clean: 403 tests passing, 0 checkstyle violations
- [x] New coverage: `ByaiContentCodecTest`, `ByaiWorkerTest`, extended `ScatterGatherTest` (Group Join aggregation + Aborted safeguard + alias equivalence), extended `PluginRegistryTest` (reload idempotency/all-or-nothing/status + hook-timeout), `GatewayClientReloadPluginsTest`, `WorkerRunnerReloadPluginsTest` (full reload flow through the real Mockito-mocked `xreadGroup`/`xadd`/`xack` loop)
- [x] Reviewed via a Standards + Spec two-axis pass; real findings (Lombok convention, duplicated result-map code, inline FQNs) fixed before this PR; two Spec findings investigated and confirmed intentional (reload-id idempotency-on-failure matches Python; `ByaiAgentContext` can't mirror TS's typed-subclass approach because Java records can't be subclassed — documented in its Javadoc)

body:
## Summary

- Remediate all 15 high and 1 moderate npm audit findings without changing the application's Next.js 16, Prisma 7, or ESLint major versions.
- Pin patched transitive releases for Next.js/PostCSS and Prisma tooling.
- Add a temporary dual-module `brace-expansion` compatibility package so ESLint's legacy `minimatch` API delegates to the official patched implementation instead of leaving the vulnerable release installed.

The root cause is that several upstream tools still pin vulnerable transitive versions. In particular, ESLint 9 still uses `minimatch` 3's callable `brace-expansion` interface, while the patched package exposes a named export. The adapter preserves both interfaces and contains no expansion implementation of its own.

There should be no application behavior change. Next.js remains 16.2.11, Prisma remains 7.9.0, and ESLint remains 9.39.5. The only intended behavioral change is that dependency parsing paths use patched implementations.

Tracks #546 for removing the temporary compatibility package after supported upstream ESLint packages no longer require it.

body:
Ревизия **v4.22** по `SPRINT_V4_22.md`. База — master `e000772`, спека v4.21 → **v4.22**.

FİN недоступен движку до SIMA-идентификации: он появляется вместе с `birthDate` на этапе 4а (факт владельца 26.07.2026). Прежние позиции FİN-проверок — дневной cap в шаге 0, лимит одного займа в шаге 1, cooldown в шаге 1а — описывали нереализуемый порядок. Все три перенесены в блок **4а-1 → 4а-2 → 4а-3** между 4а и 4б, без перенумерации остальных шагов.

Транспорт §14.0 НЕ менялся: движок вызывается один раз, после SIMA, FİN обязателен во входе. Семантика гейтов не менялась ни в чём, кроме позиции: cooldown не ставится при cap-DEFER, инкремент cap на APPROVE, счётчики §12 прежние. `global_stop` по-прежнему первый гейт после валидации.

## Коммиты

1. `5ec4ad0` — **спека отдельным первым коммитом** (§1, §9, §13.1, §13.5, §14.0, §14.1, §16, статус-блок, Приложение В).
2. `f0a225b` — код + тесты + golden.

## Дельта тестов: 348 / 1 skip → **351 / 1 skip** (+3)

| Модуль | Было | Стало |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scoring-domain | 50 | 50 |
| scoring-adapters | 204 | **207** |
| scoring-adapters-postgres | 51 | 51 |
| scoring-adapters-scraper | 15 | 15 |
| scoring-admin | 28 | 28 |

+3 — новые кейсы в `FunnelOrderTests` на различающую силу переноса: возраст раньше лимита на годном устройстве; cap раньше cooldown; лимит раньше cooldown. Четвёртый, `Active_loan_still_wins_over_age_and_device_codes`, переименован в `Device_codes_and_age_now_win_over_active_loan` с инвертированным ожиданием — премисса перевёрнута ревизией, вход тот же.

`DailyCapTests.At_cap_new_borrower_defers_without_cooldown_or_external_calls` → `..._or_paid_calls`: `externalCallsTotal() == 0` заменён на `tac.calls() == 0` + `acb.calls() == 0`.

## Дельта golden (правка `tests/golden_cases.yaml` — по явной команде владельца 26.07.2026)

| Кейс | Было | Стало | Причина |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G24** | `reasonCode: REJ_ACTIVE_LOAN` | `reasonCode: REJ_AGE` | возраст (4а) теперь раньше лимита (4а-2); `status`/`decision` без изменений |
| **G17** | `external_calls: none` | `acb_called: false, model_source_called: false` | вердикт и код не менялись |
| **G25** | `external_calls: none` | `acb_called: false, model_source_called: false` | вердикт и код не менялись |
| **G26** | `external_calls: none` | `acb_called: false, model_source_called: false` | статус и хинт не менялись |

Суммы и исходы APPROVE/REJECT/DEFER **не изменились ни в одном кейсе**. Причина замены ключа: отсекаемая FİN-гейтом заявка теперь проходит бесплатные шаги 2–4а (MCQS, оценка залога, возраст) — принятая владельцем цена переноса. Сохраняемый инвариант — отсутствие **платных** вызовов (источник модели §14.7 и отчёт ACB); число бесплатных намеренно не фиксируется как хрупкое к будущим перестановкам.

`external_calls: none` остаётся у **G29** (global_stop) — там инвариант «ноль вызовов» по-прежнему верен. Расширение `DecisionAssert` не потребовалось: ключи `acb_called` / `model_source_called` уже поддерживались с v4.20.

Шапка и `meta:` golden приведены к действующей ревизии (правило 15): `spec: v4.20` → `v4.22`, добавлен блок с построчным разбором пересчёта.

## Правки ref-строк golden (мандат владельца)

Греп по всему yaml на ссылки в исчезающие шаги; правки только вида «номер шага → новый номер»:

| Кейс | Было | Стало |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G17 | `"§9, шаг 1"` | `"§9, шаг 4а-2"` |
| G25 | `"§13.2, шаг 1а (правка v4.1)"` | `"§13.2, шаг 4а-3 (правка v4.1)"` |
| G26 | `"§13.5, шаг 0"` | `"§13.5, шаг 4а-1"` |

Проверены и правки НЕ потребовали: G24 (`ref` без номера шага), G18 (шаг 2 остаётся шагом 2), G29 (global_stop остаётся шагом 0).

## Заодно починено той же ревизией (по команде владельца)

- §14.0, строка IMEI: «вход для проверок 2, 3 и **4а**» → «**4б**» — хвост перенумерации v4.19/v4.20.
- §14.0, строка brand/model: «сверяется с GSMA TAC **(3)**» → «**(4б)**» — тот же хвост.
- §1 (новая строка 4а-3) и §16 `REJ_COOLDOWN`: корзина «вход **30д**» → «вход **15д** (параметр 17)» — расхождение с §13.2/§17 тянулось с v4.16.
- §1 строка 13: «полный пересчёт **с шага 1**» → «**с начала воронки**».
- §13.5: «разрыв "проверка **на шаге 0** ↔ инкремент на APPROVE"» → «**на 4а-1**».

## Развилка шага 2 — закрыта решением владельца

Проверка «IMEI в своей LMS» ведётся **по одному IMEI**, FİN не участвует (`LmsRepository.isDevicePledged(String imei)`) — FİN-зависимой не является, поэтому шаг 2 остался на месте. Порт и golden G18 не тронуты. Формулировка спеки приведена к фактическому поведению кода и G18: «устройство под **твоим** активным займом» → «под активным займом (любого заёмщика; проверка по одному IMEI, FİN не участвует)» в §1 ш.2, §13.1 ш.2 и §16 `REJ_DEVICE_BUSY`.

## Проверки

- `./mvnw.cmd verify` — **BUILD SUCCESS**, `-Werror` (`-Xlint:all`) проходит.
- Golden 35/35 на новом порядке.
- Blind-путь своей копии гейтов не содержит — зеркалить было нечего; `isNewBorrower` протаскивается из 4а-1 в `approveSideEffects`, инкремент на APPROVE сохранён.
